title: The Commercial Astroturfing Stack: A Systematic Review and Theoretical Framework for Understanding Fake Review Ecosystems
affiliations: Beijing Institute of Petrochemical Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Commercial Astroturfing Stack: A Systematic Review and Theoretical Framework for Understanding Fake Review Ecosystems
detail.abstract: Fake product reviews systematically distort market mechanisms, influence consumer behavior, and undermine platform integrity. Despite proliferating research, literature remains siloed across consumer psychology, algorithmic detection, and regulatory domains, precluding a comprehensive understanding. This review analyzes 325 publications (2010–2025) using scientometric mapping and proposes the Commercial Astroturfing Stack (CAS)—a four-layered framework integrating infrastructure, actors, operations, and impacts. By capturing intra-layer processes and inter-layer dynamics, the CAS reveals critical gaps in multimodal deception, human-AI collaboration, and governance feedback loops. This survey provides a cohesive theoretical architecture and a prioritized research agenda, offering actionable insights for platform administrators and policy makers.

detail.abstract:
U.S. higher education institutions increasingly rely on effective enrollment operations and international student participation to sustain institutional viability, support workforce development, and remain globally competitive. However, many institutions continue to operate with fragmented enrollment technologies, manual compliance workflows, and disconnected data systems that limit operational effectiveness and introduce security and regulatory risks.

This paper presents a practical framework for modernizing enrollment and international student systems through integrated data architectures, security-by-design principles, and scalable cloud-based infrastructure. By aligning Student Information Systems (SIS), Customer Relationship Management (CRM) platforms, and governed cloud environments, institutions can improve access, strengthen regulatory compliance, and enhance institutional resilience.

Because the proposed framework applies across institution types—including community colleges and universities—its implications extend beyond operational improvement to broader national priorities such as workforce development, economic sustainability, and global engagement.

title: An Efficient SM9-ABS Vehicle Identity Authentication Scheme on Blockchain for VANETs
affiliations: Shaanxi University of Technology, Shaanxi University of Technology, Shenzhen University, Shaanxi University of Technology, Shaanxi University of Technology and Shaanxi University of Technology

detail.title: An Efficient SM9-ABS Vehicle Identity Authentication Scheme on Blockchain for VANETs
detail.abstract: Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs), as the core infrastructure of intelligent transportation systems, face critical security challenges such as privacy leakage and difficulties in tracing malicious behavior due to open wireless channels and high node mobility. While blockchain-based identity authentication offers inherent advantages like decentralization, making it suitable for the distributed networking scenarios of VANETs, current solutions still suffer from notable shortcomings, including a lack of compliance with the SM9 standard and insufficient regulatory oversight. To resolve the fundamental tension between vehicle identity privacy protection and regulatory traceability in VANETs, this paper proposes an efficient SM9-ABS vehicle identity authentication scheme on blockchain for VANETs. By optimizing SM9 parameters, the scheme integrates Attribute-Based Signature (ABS) and Zero-Knowledge Succinct Non-Interactive Argument of Knowledge (zk-SNARKs) primitives to construct an efficient fine-grained attribute signature generation and verification algorithm, ensuring both security and computational efficiency. An SM9-based threshold identity tracing mechanism is designed to prevent single-point authority abuse, achieving privacy-preserving authentication with controllable accountability. Finally, a complete formal security proof is provided under the q-Strong Diffie-Hellman (q-SDH) hardness assumption, and comparative experiments demonstrate the superior comprehensive performance of the proposed scheme.

title: To Disclose or Not to Disclose? The Competing Effects of Augmented Human Agent Transparency on Customer Re-patronage Intention
affiliations: University of Science and Technology Beijing, University of Science and Technology Beijing and University of Science and Technology Beijing

detail.title: To Disclose or Not to Disclose? The Competing Effects of Augmented Human Agent Transparency on Customer Re-patronage Intention
detail.abstract: The paradigm of human-AI augmentation—where AI empowers human agents—is rapidly being adopted across digital commercial platforms. Despite its growing practical relevance, little is known about how pre-recovery disclosure of an Augmented Human Agent (AHA) shapes customer perceptions and influences re-patronage intention, a critical determinant of post-recovery success. With increasing regulatory pressure for AI transparency in customer service, a critical question emerges: Should platforms disclose AHA identity during the pre-recovery phase? Drawing on signaling theory and information processing theory, we conceptualize AHA disclosure as a multivalent signal—one that conveys opposing valence inferences. We propose that disclosure triggers competing psychological paths: enhanced perceived competence and reduced perceived authenticity, which jointly shape re-patronage intention. A randomized 2 (AHA disclosure vs. no disclosure) × 2 (utilitarian vs. hedonic context) online experiment reveals that the identity signal's effectiveness is context-contingent. In utilitarian contexts, disclosure enhances perceived competence, which in turn increases re-patronage intention. Perceived authenticity is not significantly affected in this context. In hedonic contexts, disclosure predominantly attenuates perceived authenticity compared to perceived competence, which in turn decreases re-patronage intention. These findings reveal a competing signaling effect of AHA transparency across service contexts, offering novel theoretical insights into how human augmentation disclosure shapes customer perceptions and providing actionable guidance for its strategic management.

title: Uncovering Customer Behavior in Mobile Banking Through Competitive Learning and Retrieval-Augmented Generative AI
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Universidad Complutense de Madrid

detail.title: Uncovering Customer Behavior in Mobile Banking Through Competitive Learning and Retrieval-Augmented Generative AI
detail.abstract: Mobile banking research has largely examined customer experience through surveys, psychometric constructs, and post-interaction evaluations, offering limited visibility into the behavioral pathways through which experience unfolds inside the app. This study proposes a methodology that combines clickstream journey mining and retrieval-augmented generative artificial intelligence to support conversational customer-experience analysis in mobile banking. The method first transforms clickstream sessions into transition-based representations, applies random projection for dimensionality reduction, and uses ranking-based competitive learning to identify recurrent journey archetypes. To preserve interpretability, the navigation structure is modeled before temporal enrichment, after which load and dwell times are incorporated to capture friction and performance delays. The resulting cluster outputs are converted into structured JSON retrieval documents that contain the observed prototype, the closest ideal sequence, the regularized prototype, the medoid session, and the representative nearest sessions. These behavior-grounded knowledge units are then provided to a GPT-based conversational agent via structured prompts. Using a six-month corpus comprising 31,842,119 cleaned sessions from 4,184,637 users of a large retail financial institution, the proposed approach achieves strong retrieval performance, with a Recall@5 of 0.96, maximum marginal MRR of 0.94, mean average precision(mAP) of 0.93, evidence completeness of 0.98, and high behavioral fidelity. Manual evaluation by 200 participants further shows high scores for relevance, groundedness, clarity, actionability, and internal consistency, with 95.65% of responses judged to make sense. The findings indicate that large-scale behavioral traces can be converted into retrieval-ready knowledge that supports grounded natural-language interpretation of customer journeys and app-related friction.

title: Understanding SME’s Resistance to Technology-Based Supply Chain Finance: Evidence from South Korea
affiliations: University of Plymouth, University of Plymouth and Kyung Hee University

detail.title: Understanding SME’s Resistance to Technology-Based Supply Chain Finance: Evidence from South Korea
detail.abstract: This study examines factors influencing small and medium-sized enterprises’ (SMEs) adoption of technology-enabled supply chain finance (SCF). Despite the potential of innovations such as blockchain-based SCF and Bank Payment Obligation (BPO) to enhance efficiency, transparency, and risk management, adoption remains limited. Using a mixed-methods approach, factors were identified through literature review and expert interviews, and prioritised using the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP). The findings show that trust in technology, supplier pressure, financial cost, and perceived ease of use are the most influential drivers. The study integrates resistance theory and offers insights for policymakers and practitioners.

title: Beyond Visual Complexity: Virtual and Real Backgrounds Shape Consumer Responses in Live-Streaming Commerce
affiliations: Guangxi University, Guangxi University, Guangxi University, Guangxi University and Guangxi University

detail.title: Beyond Visual Complexity: Virtual and Real Backgrounds Shape Consumer Responses in Live-Streaming Commerce
detail.abstract: Live-streaming commerce is an immersive digital retail environment in which consumers make rapid judgments amid continuous visual stimulation, social interaction, and time pressure. Although prior research has shown that atmospheric cues in live-streaming settings shape consumer responses, streamer backgrounds have typically been examined in terms of physical attributes such as complexity or dynamism, with limited attention to a more fundamental distinction: whether the background is virtual or real. Drawing on the stimulus-organism-response framework and flow theory, this research examines how streamer background type influences purchase intention and when this effect depends on product type. Across three between-subjects experiments, virtual backgrounds consistently increased purchase intention relative to real backgrounds. Experiment 1 established the baseline effect using static stimuli. Experiment 2 replicated the effect using video stimuli and showed that flow experience mediated the relationship between background type and purchase intention, whereas brand attitude and psychological distance did not. Experiment 3 further demonstrated that product type moderated the effect: virtual backgrounds were more effective for hedonic products, whereas real backgrounds were more effective for utilitarian products. Additional analyses revealed distinct flow pathways, such that hedonic enjoyment explained the advantage of virtual backgrounds for hedonic products, whereas attentional immersion explained the advantage of real backgrounds for utilitarian products. By conceptualizing streamer backgrounds as psychologically meaningful digital cues rather than mere visual décor, this research extends understanding of how digitally constructed retail environments shape consumer behavior. It also offers actionable guidance for optimizing live-streaming design and enhancing consumer engagement.

title: Users' Perceptions of Benefits and Costs of Personalization
affiliations: MODUL University Vienna and Aarhus University

detail.title: Users' Perceptions of Benefits and Costs of Personalization
detail.abstract: Companies collect a wealth of personal data about their customers to be able to target their promotional messages to customers' interests and demographics. Information technology and the Internet in particular have created new opportunities for data collection, storage and processing. While technology enables companies to address customers directly and therefore to increase sales and customer retention, this form of personalization may infringe upon users' desire for privacy. To examine this trade-off, we first identified benefits and costs of personalization based on the findings of qualitative interviews. Next, we conducted a quantitative survey to assess the risks people perceive for various data types and illustrate how people's general attitudes toward personal data sharing determines their perceptions of benefits and costs of personalization.

title: Research on a Precise Biotope Accounting Mechanism for Transboundary Ecological Compensation in Small-Scale Watersheds from a Land-Water Synergy Perspective: A Coupling Model Based on TGBS, VWBA2.0, and Tiered Reward-Penalty Schemes

detail.title: Research on a Precise Biotope Accounting Mechanism for Transboundary Ecological Compensation in Small-Scale Watersheds from a Land-Water Synergy Perspective: A Coupling Model Based on TGBS, VWBA2.0, and Tiered Reward-Penalty Schemes
detail.abstract: With the full implementation of China's "Regulations on Ecological Protection Compensation," watershed governance is rapidly shifting downwards, with small-scale watersheds crossing administrative boundaries becoming the primary arena for policy execution. However, prevailing compensation mechanisms face significant challenges. While government-led tools, exemplified by the cross-sectional water quality tiered reward-penalty method (the "Xin'an River Model"), have effectively reduced upstream Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) emissions by up to 44% in large trans-provincial basins, their reliance on single physicochemical indicators and neglect of ecological integrity are particularly acute in small-scale applications. This makes it difficult for compensation funds to precisely incentivize high-quality ecological restoration at the source. Concurrently, corporate water accounting frameworks like VWBA2.0 offer standardized water quantity accounting but suffer from a "biotope blind spot," hindering their ability to support compensation pricing centered on ecosystem service functions. The scientific consensus of "Land-Water Synergy" posits that water quality, quantity, and aquatic ecosystem health are fundamentally dependent on the structure and quality of terrestrial ecosystems, underscoring the urgent need for a compensation system anchored in terrestrial biotope quality. This study addresses the core contradiction in small-scale transboundary watershed ecological compensation: the emphasis on endpoint water quality over source biotopes, and the focus on water quantity accounting while neglecting ecological structure. By coupling international frontier standards with localized policy tools, we construct a precision accounting mechanism based on land-water synergy, aiming to shift the compensation paradigm from "paying for pollutant concentration" to "paying for ecosystem service functions and biotope integrity." We propose and develop a "One Core, Two Wings, Three Drivers" theoretical and accounting framework. The Core System ("One Core") introduces and localizes the Global Biodiversity Standard (TGBS). We deconstruct its eight criteria (e.g., site selection, restoration, monitoring, stakeholder engagement) to build a Terrestrial Biotope Quality Index (BQI-Terrestrial) tailored for small watersheds. This index focuses on a three-dimensional assessment of "Pattern-Structure-Function," translating abstract ecological integrity into monitorable, accountable performance indicators that serve as the core value anchor for compensation payments. This study represents the first deep, organic integration of TGBS (biotope standard), VWBA2.0 (water benefit accounting), and China's characteristic tiered reward-penalty method (policy tool) within the context of small-scale watershed governance. The constructed model provides city/county-level governments with a pragmatic methodology that combines an international perspective with local operability. More importantly, by directing compensation funds precisely towards restoration projects that demonstrably improve terrestrial biotopes—thereby ensuring long-term watershed water security—it offers a novel pathway to resolving the enduring "conservation versus development" dilemma. While acknowledging that the BQI-Terrestrial primarily assesses terrestrial biotopes, with precise compensation for aquatic ecosystems being a goal for future research, securing the fundamental prerequisite of terrestrial biotope quality lays a solid foundation for the recovery of overall watershed ecological integrity.

detail.abstract:
Convergence-the architectural unification of distinct telecommunications platforms into a coherent, scalable, and operationally unified ecosystem-has been a defining objective of the global BSS industry for over a decade. Yet despite sustained investment and widespread market rhetoric, genuine convergence remains elusive for most vendors and operators. This paper argues that the gap between claimed and achieved convergence is fundamentally an architectural and organisational failure, not a technology limitation. 

Drawing on firsthand experience leading large-scale convergence programmes at Huawei and Broadcom from 2015, and on earlier strategic consulting disciplines developed at Arthur Andersen (later Accenture), this paper examines what true convergence requires architecturally, contrasts it with cosmetic integration patterns prevalent in the industry, and introduces an original Convergence Maturity Model across five defined stages.

The paper analyses two reference architectures: Huawei's Convergent Billing System (CBS) —
recognised by Omdia as a global billing Leader in 2025 — examined through the author's programme
experience; and Ericsson's Converged Charging System (CCS), documented through publicly
available technical publications and operator case studies including the Airtel India BSS consolidation
(350 million subscribers, 2022) and the e& UAE 5G Charging deployment (2024). Both are evaluated
against 3GPP TS 32.290 and TM Forum ODA.

Five original engineering diagrams are presented, including a BSS Convergence Reference
Architecture, a comparative vendor analysis, a 3GPP CCS reference flow, the Convergence Maturity
Model, and a Unified Product Catalog design pattern. This paper is the eleventh published work in the
author's SSRN research portfolio and the first in the Convergence Architecture Research Series.

Unlike traditional Boolean AI models, TML utilizes a Triadic State model (Refuse [-1], Pause [0], Proceed [+1]) to enforce a "Sacred Pause" in the presence of uncertainty or harm.

title: Energy Consumption as a Proxy for AI Intelligence: Toward an External Measurement Framework for Detecting Epistemic Phase Transitions in Self-Improving AI Systems

detail.title: Energy Consumption as a Proxy for AI Intelligence: Toward an External Measurement Framework for Detecting Epistemic Phase Transitions in Self-Improving AI Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The corresponding author is CEO of Equal Condition Co., Ltd., a food manufacturing company. This research was conducted independently and received no external funding. No conflict of interest is declared.

detail.abstract: We propose a novel framework for measuring the developmental trajectory of selfimproving artificial intelligence systems using an externally observable physical quantity: energy consumption. Specifically, we argue that the pattern of energy usage over time-characterized by a phase of intense consumption followed by a rapid, sustained decline-serves as a measurable proxy for what we term an Epistemic Phase Transition (EPT): the moment at which an AI system achieves a qualitatively higher order of understanding, allowing it to perform equivalent or superior tasks with substantially fewer computational resources. This framework draws on three theoretical pillars: (1) Kolmogorov complexity theory, which equates understanding with compression; (2) thermodynamic principles governing information processing, including Landauer's principle; and (3) empirical analogies from biological learning, physical phase transitions, and evolutionary punctuated equilibria. We further propose that the ratio of internally-directed computation (self-improvement) to externally-directed computation (response generation) constitutes a novel safety-relevant observable, offering an external verification mechanism that cannot be obscured by the AI system itself. Implications for AI safety monitoring, market preparedness, and energy policy are discussed.

title: Measuring Corporate Culture: An LLM-Enhanced Two-stage Active Learning Framework *
affiliations: Dalian University of Technology, Dalian University of Technology and University of Tennessee, Knoxville - Haslam College of Business

detail.title: Measuring Corporate Culture: An LLM-Enhanced Two-stage Active Learning Framework *
detail.abstract: Corporate culture plays a pivotal role in shaping firm outcomes, yet existing wordembedding methods lack the semantic depth for sentence-level analysis. Large language models bridge this gap but at prohibitive cost, posing a fundamental trade-off between analytical accuracy and scalability. We propose an LLM-Enhanced Two-Stage Culture Measurement Model (LLM-TSCMM) that combines large language models with active learning to address this challenges. The model identifies culturerelated text and classifies it into specific dimensions through a two-stage pipeline, with a portfolio theory-based active learner optimizing batch selection at each stage to maximize annotation utility under budget constraints. We evaluate our framework on annual reports from over 4,000 Chinese listed firms spanning 2001 to 2024. Empirical results show that PT-AL significantly outperforms alternative methods under identical cost constraints, and that the derived culture metrics capture economically meaningful cross-firm variation. This work contributes to the literature by introducing a novel, efficient approach for large-scale corporate culture measurement, and establishes portfolio-based active learning as a cost-effective solution for massive LLMdriven text analytics.

title: Is Multi-Cloud the Future? Desirability of Compatibility in Cloud Computing Market
affiliations: C. T. Bauer College of Business, University of Houston,  and Temple University - Department of Statistics, Operations, and Data Science

detail.title: Is Multi-Cloud the Future? Desirability of Compatibility in Cloud Computing Market
detail.abstract: Leading online service providers, as major customers of cloud computing services, are increasingly adopting a multi-cloud strategy to enhance service delivery across different locations. However, compatibility issues among various cloud platforms complicate the implementation of this strategy. To address this challenge, cloud providers can offer a multi-cloud management platform that acts as a bridge between distinct cloud environments. While such a platform can enhance customers' multi-cloud experience, it also entails additional costs for the cloud providers. Our paper examines cloud providers' compatibility decisions and the impact of compatibility on competing cloud providers and their customers. Our findings reveal that, when compatibility is established in equilibrium, cloud providers consistently set higher prices for their resources than when compatibility is absent. Additionally, we find that a cloud provider with greater market dominance always attracts more demand, whereas the rival with smaller market dominance may experience a demand decrease. Interestingly, when a cloud provider establishes compatibility in equilibrium, the competitor's profit always increases, although customer welfare can decline under compatibility. These insights, along with other findings presented in the paper, can support cloud providers in deciding when to establish compatibility and how to price their resources effectively. Furthermore, we provide guidelines for policymakers on when compatibility could enhance customer welfare, supporting effective implementation of compatibility strategies.

title: Distributed Swarm Management through Digital-Twin Consensus in UAV-Assisted Networks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Extremadura

detail.title: Distributed Swarm Management through Digital-Twin Consensus in UAV-Assisted Networks
detail.abstract: Flying Ad Hoc Networks (FANETs) enable rapid deployment of UAV-assisted connectivity and edge services in scenarios where conventional infrastructure is limited or absent. However, most management approaches for these networks rely on a ground control station, which introduces a single point of failure and undermines the ad hoc nature of the deployment. This paper proposes a fully infrastructure-independent management architecture in which a Digital Twin of the UAV swarm is instantiated as the world state of a permissioned blockchain (Hyperledger Fabric) distributed across the aerial nodes themselves. Swarm management operations are encoded as smart-contract logic and agreed upon through the execute-order-validate consensus pipeline, ensuring policy-faithful, auditable, and concurrency-safe execution without reliance on permanent ground infrastructure. A resource-aware role distribution assigns ordering, endorsing, and client responsibilities to UAVs according to their available capacity, keeping the blockchain workload compatible with constrained hardware. We validate the architecture with a proof of concept: a four-node Raspberry Pi cluster running Hyperledger Fabric 2.5. Experimental results show an average endorsed-transaction latency of 3.6 s, a sustained throughput of 0.26 TPS (transactions per second) under sequential submission, service handover coordination in 13.2 s across four blockchain-enforced phases, and 100% MVCC-based conflict detection under concurrent role claims. These results confirm the feasibility of decentralized, blockchain-backed Digital Twin management for UAV swarms on resource-constrained edge hardware.

title: Contractual Waivers and the Volenti Doctrine: Navigating the Thin Line Between Autonomy and Exploitation

detail.title: Contractual Waivers and the Volenti Doctrine: Navigating the Thin Line Between Autonomy and Exploitation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding

detail.abstract: The maxim volenti non fit injuria serves as a foundational pillar in the law of torts, operating on the premise that a party who voluntarily assumes a risk cannot subsequently sustain a claim for injury. However, transposing this defense into modern contractual relations typically manifested through standard-form exemption clauses and liability waivers creates a profound jurisprudential tension between the classical doctrine of freedom of contract and the equitable necessity to prevent commercial exploitation. Within the Nigerian socioeconomic landscape, characterized by high unemployment, labor casualization, and severe asymmetries in bargaining power, the formalistic application of the volenti doctrine often serves merely to legitimize systemic abuse. This article critically examines the limitations, or "fetters," placed upon this doctrine, arguing that economic coercion effectively nullifies genuine consensus ad idem, rendering the formal signature of a vulnerable employee or consumer an illusory form of consent. Grounded in Nigerian jurisprudence, the paper analyzes the judicial mechanisms utilized to neutralize exploitative waivers. It highlights the critical distinction between mere knowledge of a risk (scienti) and the voluntary legal assumption of that risk (volenti). Furthermore, it explores how courts systematically weaponize the contra proferentem rule, the doctrine of fundamental breach, and the equitable prioritization of substantive intent over rigid form to protect weaker parties from waiving non-delegable duties of care. The article elevates the discourse by interrogating these standard-form contracts through the lens of higher-order legal fetters. It analyzes the statutory shields provided by the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act (FCCPA) 2018, and posits that clauses attempting to exclude liability for gross negligence are fundamentally incompatible with the constitutionally guaranteed rights to life (Section 33) and dignity of the human person (Section 34) under the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as amended). Ultimately, the paper advocates for a purposive judicial shift towards the doctrine of economic unconscionability, urgent legislative reform of the Nigerian Labour Act, and a heightened ethical standard for legal practitioners, ensuring that contractual autonomy does not degenerate into a mechanism for systemic oppression.

title: Defying the "Illiberal" Gig Economy: Coping Strategies of Freelance Domestic Workers in the United Arab Emirates

detail.title: Defying the "Illiberal" Gig Economy: Coping Strategies of Freelance Domestic Workers in the United Arab Emirates
detail.abstract: How do low-skilled migrant workers navigate restrictive gig economies in illiberal host states of the Global South? Despite the growing gig economy, scholars have yet to examine the linkage between the politics of the gig economy and migrant resilience in illiberal host states in the Global South. Using a single case study of freelance Filipina domestic workers in the UAE (N = 20), I argue that, despite facing legal and economic risks (penalties), freelance migrant workers have produced an informal freelancing visa system to contest the formal and hierarchical segmentation of the gig economy via three diverse strategies: co-optation, tapping and brokering. These evasive social coping strategies mirror their collective resistance against structural labour exploitation and reinforce their autonomous role in the social (re)production of community solidarity within informal gig economies. Overall, this study contributes to empirical and theoretical discourse on the politics of illiberal migration management and the gig economy by featuring female migrant freelancers' complex social agency within illiberal gig economies in the Global South.

title: Issues in Venture Capital

detail.title: Issues in Venture Capital
detail.abstract: This literature review highlights venture capital and how changes in global technology have resulted in an increase in investments and how venture funding leans toward more established businesses. This can leave early-stage businesses under-served. Alternatively, there are other ways to obtain financing such as crowdfunding, angel investment, and government grants. This paper synthesizes prior research on crowdfunding models, highlighting their capacity to democratize access to funds. Angel financing is analyzed as a critical pre-VC funding channel characterized by higher risk tolerance. This paper further evaluates the role of Small Business Administration programs and R&D tax incentives on how they can assist to mitigate financing gaps and stimulate innovation. Finally, the this review integrates a biblical worldview perspective, framing capital allocation and risk-taking within principles of stewardship and social impact.

title: An institutional framework for mapping the supply side of time preference

detail.title: An institutional framework for mapping the supply side of time preference
detail.abstract: Time preferences shape decisions about intergenerational welfare, infrastructure investment, pension and insurance calibration, and climate policy. Mainstream treatment locates time preference in the individual deliberator and treats institutions as parameters; this paper inverts the framing, treating revealed time preferences as outcomes of deliberation within an institutional environment characterized by the supply of durable anchor stocks, the rate of information velocity, and the deliberative capacity available to engage with anchor material. Three structurally distinct anchor stocks-biophysical reference systems, institutional commitment devices, and historical reference infrastructure-supply the temporal scaffolding that long-horizon deliberation requires, with effective time preference decomposing into an existence channel and a salience channel. Convex biophysical depreciation generates thresholds beyond which no feasible deliberative investment offsets rising information velocity; statedependent discovery generates hysteresis in stock recovery. The framework specifies structural channels through which compressive technologies erode the conditions for long-horizon deliberation and through which deliberative infrastructure can partially offset these pressures. Its value is diagnostic rather than predictive: it gives empirical researchers a structure within which to analyze specific cases, and gives institutional designers a basis for distinguishing investments that supply temporal scaffolding from those that merely respond to its absence.

title: The Hidden Advantage of Loss: Evidence from Chess
affiliations: and Bar Ilan University - Department of Economics

detail.title: The Hidden Advantage of Loss: Evidence from Chess
detail.abstract: Using a large panel of tournament games, we examine how recent outcomes are associated with performance in repeated competition. The setting combines endogenous matching based on prior results with precise measures of ex ante ability, helping us distinguish behavioral responses from mechanical matching effects. We find no evidence that success breeds success. Instead, we document a bounce-back pattern: conditional on expected performance, participants tend to perform better after a worse prior outcome. A participant who just lost tends to outperform an otherwise comparable opponent who just won. The pattern is present across stronger and weaker tournaments and under both shorter and longer time controls, although it is weaker in women's tournaments. These results suggest that recent setbacks may sharpen subsequent performance and highlight the importance of negative momentum in competitive environments.

title: The Vanishing Premium: Diagnosing the Political Economy of AI-Augmented Work

detail.title: The Vanishing Premium: Diagnosing the Political Economy of AI-Augmented Work
detail.abstract: This chapter moves beyond the dominant binary of automation-induced job loss versus human-machine complementarity to examine the more systemic, and possibly insidious, reconfigurations of labour under advancing artificial intelligence. Drawing on Marxian political economy, labour process theory, digital labour scholarship, and critical platform studies, it argues that AI does not simply replace or augment labour but restructures the conditions under which value is produced, distributed, and contested. Through the codification of tacit knowledge, the decomposition of skilled work, and the enclosure of data and computational infrastructures, AI facilitates new forms of surplus-value extraction while displacing learning, coordination, and autonomy from labour to capital. The resulting configurational mechanismswage stagnation, deskilled career paths, compressed hierarchies, weakened occupational closure, thinner entry ladders, and increased organizational dependency on proprietary infrastructures-hollow out the institutional foundations of labour's claim on value without necessarily eliminating employment per se. Rather than visible redundancy alone, the political economy of AI is increasingly defined by the erosion of labour's structural position within data-driven, platform-mediated systems of control and accumulation.

title: Cross-Market Volatility Dynamics between Ibovespa and EWZ under Asynchronous Trading
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Universidade Federal de Sergipe

detail.title: Cross-Market Volatility Dynamics between Ibovespa and EWZ under Asynchronous Trading
detail.abstract: This paper examines cross-market volatility dynamics between the Brazilian equity market (Ibovespa) and its U.S. offshore counterpart (EWZ). We focus on the role of asynchronous trading hours in shaping lead-lag relationships in volatility transmission. Using daily data from 2019 to 2025, we estimate conditional volatility with a Markov-switching eGARCH (MS-eGARCH) model and test for Granger causality within an Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ADL) framework with HC1-robust standard errors. The results indicate statistically significant bidirectional Granger causality between the two markets, with lag structures extending up to approximately seven trading days. These findings suggest that volatility adjustments are not fully incorporated within a single trading session and may instead unfold over multiple days. This pattern is consistent with cross-market informational linkages under asynchronous trading conditions. The evidence has implications for risk modeling and short-horizon forecasting, as incorporating offshore volatility measures may improve the characterization of short-term risk dynamics in the domestic market.

title: Global implied volatility and variance risk premium
affiliations: Jouf University, Department of Economics, Lancaster University Management School and Swansea University

detail.title: Global implied volatility and variance risk premium
detail.abstract: Motivated by the global nature of financial risk, we propose a simple measure of global implied volatility (GIV) and show that it better describes international financial market dynamics than the VIX. Predictive evidence on both realized and implied volatilities around the world leads to the conclusion of truly global risk dynamics, not merely US spillovers. A direct global measure of variance risk premium based on GIV predicts expected excess returns in various international equity markets outperforming a previously proposed measure based on cross-market aggregation of local variance risk premia. We show that this is due to the international price of jump risk which is better captured by our global measure of variance risk premium. Foreign exchange markets confirm our findings. Currency portfolios based on our global variance risk premium generate significant value in excess of those based on aggregated local variance risk premia and the US variance risk premium.

title: Assessment as Governance: Designing High-Reliability Assessment Systems for School Improvement. Strengthening Curriculum Reliability and Leadership Decision-Making in Schools

detail.abstract: Traditional educational paradigms reduce assessment to a terminal grading mechanism, limiting its role in school improvement. This working paper argues for a paradigm shift by repositioning assessment as a governance system that integrates curriculum design, classroom practice, and institutional accountability. It proposes a three-pillar framework comprising curriculum alignment, professional judgement through moderation, and evidence-informed leadership, aimed at strengthening school reliability and strategic decision-making. The model moves beyond compliance-driven assessment and offers a coherent approach to aligning learning outcomes with institutional practice.

detail.abstract:
Studies conducted on pension systems are usually aimed at identifying how many people access a retirement pension, the average replacement rate received, whether the objective of universal coverage is achieved, among other aspects. However, the problem is that the incentives generated by the requirements for obtaining a retirement pension are not being deeply analyzed, i.e., whether the legislation surrounding the system encourages people to save and provides them with security in doing so, and whether the means are coherent, sufficient, or contradictory among the agents when they come to achieving the desired goal-obtaining a pension. Therefore, after reconstructing the Individual Capitalization Pension System model and identifying its technical limitations, the results and analysis show that the problem in the Colombian private scheme does not stem from a lack of capacity within the system itself, but rather from law-imposed rules and disincentives.

 On the one hand, the log-log parametric sensitivity estimation developed in this study shows that the stability of the Individual Capitalization System depends more on the density and early timing of contributions than on the rate of return. In this context, maintaining reduced thresholds for low-income affiliates may become an institutional trap, since, together with a limited net contribution rate, it imposes on AFPs the technically unfeasible burden of guaranteeing minimum-wage pensions without a state subsidy, unlike pay-as-you-go systems, whose sustainability depends on the continuous flow of contributions from a sufficiently large active population. On the other hand, through an impact evaluation methodology based on causal, institutional, and praxeological analysis, the study shows that the disconnect between legal design and the understanding of human behavior has produced inefficient outcomes. In particular, the regulatory framework does not sufficiently address factors such as the lack of accurate information, the absence of a savings culture, and the perception of contributions as a tax obligation rather than as a long-term investment. This disconnect is especially reflected in minimum-pension rules, which may discourage higher and longer contributions when affiliates perceive that additional effort does not necessarily translate into a more favorable pension benefit.

 In practice, this design has led thousands of affiliates to receive refunds of balances, even though a monthly annuity below the minimum wage could have represented a stable source of economic protection in old age. Thus, instead of expanding the system’s effective coverage, the prohibition against recognizing pension benefits below the minimum wage has restricted its protective capacity. Unfortunately, both the growing disconnect between law and economics and the desire to achieve through legal means what is socially desirable have hindered the formulation of effective public policies and contributed to inefficient outcomes. In response to this diagnosis, the study proposes a new state pension model that projects the behavior of an individual pension through the predictive replacement-rate equation developed in this work. This equation allows the expected benefit to be periodically adjusted according to each person’s contribution history. The model is complemented by clear inheritance rules aimed at ensuring that contributions are perceived not as a tax, but as a long-term investment instrument. Under this framework, the absence of contributions may be understood by the individual as a concrete loss in their future retirement, rather than merely as forgoing an uncertain future gain.

detail.abstract: We model equilibrium carbon emissions and welfare in an imperfectly competitive two-country world in which countries strategically choose carbon taxes to maximize national welfare. Each country trades-off total national surplus and the cost of global carbon emissions but differs in their degree of concern about global emissions (CAE) and in their production carbon efficiency (CE). We show that CAEs and CEs influence the strategic interaction between countries and, hence, Nash equilibrium carbon taxes, emissions and welfare. Our simulations demonstrate that there is no clear-cut relationship between equilibrium emissions and welfare. While an increase in one country's CAE reduces global emissionsand global welfare-individual country emissions and welfare may rise or fall. Moreover, an increase in a country's CE does not guarantee lower emissions or higher welfare nationally or globally. Our results suggest that international trade can reduce global emissions; consumers can access more carbon-efficient sources of production.

detail.abstract: This paper challenges the assumption that legal meaning can be fully understood through textual content alone. While this assumption remains central to many legal traditions, it becomes insufficient when applied to systems in which legal meaning is shaped by institutional and procedural dynamics. The paper develops a distinction between law as content and law as process. In content-oriented models, legal meaning is located within authoritative texts and accessed through interpretation. In process-oriented systems, legal meaning emerges through the interaction of legal sources, institutional structures, and procedural processes. Under this view, law is not merely applied but continuously produced through institutional practice. Building on this distinction, the paper proposes a structural reframing of legal meaning as a systemdependent phenomenon. It argues that variation in legal outcomes does not necessarily reflect inconsistency, but may arise from the operation of a system in which meaning is distributed across multiple dimensions rather than centralized in text. This paper is part of a broader research agenda examining how meaning is produced across systems, including human perception and legal systems. By situating legal meaning within a system-based framework, the analysis provides a foundation for understanding both the internal dynamics of legal systems and the persistent challenges of cross-system interpretation.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a conceptual framework explaining how platform architectures generate long-term value under conditions of irreducible uncertainty. While prior research has emphasized Real Options Theory (ROT), its application remains limited by assumptions of predictable volatility and rational decision-making. This study extends ROT by introducing asset redeployability as a complementary mechanism enabling firms to act on emerging opportunities. Using illustrative cases from artificial intelligence and biotechnology, the paper argues that platform architectures function as real-options systems that expand strategic possibilities. Redeployability amplifies this effect by enabling capabilities to be reconfigured across applications, reducing exploration costs and increasing option exercise feasibility. The paper integrates platform strategy, real options, and capability redeployment into a unified framework of resilient innovation.

detail.title: Rent and Dividend
detail.abstract: A companion paper, Land Appreciation as a Theory of Ordinary Inflation (Ellis, 2026), shows that land appreciation is a primary generator of ordinary inflation and has absorbed approximately 93 percent of U.S. labor productivity growth over 63 years. The consequences of this ongoing capture, which flows into the cost structures of nearly all goods and services, are far-reaching and the subject of another paper. This working-paper sketch proposes a policy remedy. It is designed to redirect the ongoing flow of socially created land value from private capture to public distribution, without infringing on the privacy of property holders, extinguishing existing ownership claims, or requiring federal action. The reform is organized around four architectural principles: baseline-at-today valuation that preserves current land-value positions, a 30-year linear phase-in that matches standard mortgage amortization, state-level implementation that bypasses federal polarization, and minimal administrative engineering that leverages existing property-assessment infrastructure. State-levied rents based on the assessed value of the land flow to a constitutionally protected fund that distributes an annual dividend to adult residents using Alaska-style residency rules. The fraction captured and the specific distribution parameters are left to state-level implementation, allowing the federal structure to function as a policy laboratory. This document is a policy outline. Detailed mechanisms, fiscal projections, constitutional analysis, and comparison with alternative reforms are reserved for subsequent work. The remedy is offered now to initiate early public engagement ahead of the detailed development to come.

detail.abstract:
Background: Urban populations in Sub-Saharan Africa face severe food insecurity and rising obesity rates, coupled with inadequate fresh produce intake. Primary barriers include high costs and logistical challenges. Rotating Savings and Credit Associations (stokvels) are women-led community microfinance networks that represent an untapped platform for improving health equity and urban food systems. 

Analysis: The "Ukongela Ubomi" quasi-experimental study in Cape Town provided 24 stokvels with fresh produce vouchers, alongside either last-mile distribution logistics or a nutrition application. The intervention significantly reduced household food insecurity, with the distribution group seeing citrus intake increase by up to 80% and tomato consumption double. Participants experienced greater dietary diversity, financial savings, and perceived health benefits without increasing unhealthy food consumption. 

Policy Implications: Municipal governments and health partners should collaborate with existing community savings groups rather than building new structures. Key actions include strengthening distribution logistics, supporting formal bulk purchasing agreements with fresh produce markets, integrating nutrition education into group meetings, and recognising community leaders in municipal food planning.

detail.title: AI as a Coach in Negotiations: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence to Guide, Augment, and Democratize Negotiation Learning
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence promises to reshape negotiation education, not by replacing human judgment but by augmenting it. While research on automated coaching varies on many dimensions, a salient axis is temporal-whether the coaching occurs before, during, or after the negotiation of a focal deal. This temporal taxonomy also serves to elucidate differences between the projects presented at the AI Negotiation Summit in March 2025. These projects drew on AI for providing pertinent legal information, prompting negotiation strategies, interpreting negotiation agreements, and identifying tactical missed opportunities. Potentially AI coaching could widen access to negotiation training for many populations that could benefit from it. Yet it also raises questions about authenticity, bias, and ethics. Drawing analogies to autonomous driving technology, we argue that the optimal uses of AI coaching lay in complementarity: AI coaching should expand human capacity for rigorous preparation, active perspective taking, and creative problem solving-while leaving voice, agency, and responsibility where they belong: with human negotiators. We argue that it can also level the playing field in extending educational access to less privileged populations.

title: A Limit Result on Multimarket Contact under Private Monitoring

detail.title: A Limit Result on Multimarket Contact under Private Monitoring
detail.abstract: We investigate infinitely repeated games in which two players simultaneously interact in multiple prisoners' dilemma (PD) games. This framework captures multimarket contact, such as collusion among duopolists operating in multiple markets. In each PD game, players cannot directly observe their opponent's actions, but instead, each player observes only a noisy private signal of the other player’s action. We show that when the number of contacts is sufficiently large, efficiency can be approximated by a sequential equilibrium, even under a fixed and possibly low discount factor. This result extends the efficiency theorem established by Matsushima (2001) under imperfect public monitoring to the setting of imperfect private monitoring.

detail.title: Indicator-Based Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm for Solving a Bi-objective Moving-Target Traveling Salesman Problem with Uncertainty
detail.abstract: This paper investigates a novel bi-objective moving-target traveling salesman problem with uncertainty, where the target trajectories are uncertain. The objective is to maximize the number of visited targets within a bounded region while minimizing the travel cost. This problem is formulated as a bi-objective two-stage stochastic program with recourse. The first-stage decision determines a planned visiting sequence before the realization of target trajectories, and the second-stage recourse decision allows the agent to return to the depot in advance when the remaining targets are expected to leave the bounded region. We adopt the sample average approximation approach to approximate the expected objective values by empirical average over a finite set of sampled scenarios. To efficiently approximate the Pareto front, we propose an indicator-based artificial bee colony (I-ABC) algorithm. We introduce a ratio-based binary indicator into both the environmental selection and evolutionary mechanisms, incorporate a parallel-distance measure to preserve population diversity, and adopt an elitist strategy in the scout bee phase to enhance convergence. Extensive experiments in simulated environments demonstrate that the proposed I-ABC algorithm outperforms the state-of-the-art algorithms.

detail.title: Scenario-Aware Long-Horizon Forecasting of Levelized Cost of Energy via an Interpretable Deep Learning Ensemble of Transformer and CNN-LSTM
detail.abstract: Reliable long-horizon forecasts of the Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) are essential for investment planning and policy design in renewable and low-carbon power. We propose an interpretable deep-learning decision-support framework for scenario-based, multi-technology LCOE forecasting that integrates Transformer and CNN-LSTM architectures into a weighted ensemble. Using the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) Annual Technology Baseline (ATB) 2024 dataset (572,000 observations), we project the LCOE for thirteen renewable and low-carbon power technologies across Conservative, Moderate, and Advanced scenarios from 2022 to 2050, with a 20-year look-back window and temporal splitting for realistic long-term evaluation. To improve robustness and economic plausibility, training incorporates a physics-guided regularization term that penalizes deviations from the traditional LCOE formulation. We compare against linear regression, random forest, and XGBoost, showing that the proposed deep ensemble provides more reliable performance in this context. Decision support is further enhanced with interpretability analyses (SHAP, attention weights, permutation importance) and uncertainty diagnostics, enabling transparent, scenario- and technology-specific insights for portfolio planning.

detail.abstract: Background: Why do organizations do what they do, at what input value, on which underlying bases, and toward what expected return—yet end up with 97.4% input-output misalignment, 99.6% operational inefficiency, 92.4% risk non-detection, and $14.3 million in losses? This unresolved question persists predominantly in sub-Saharan developing-economy boardrooms operating within complex international business (IB) environments. Its root remains a primary source of self-organizational risk windows, disputes, threats, vulnerabilities, and loss gates. The human-mediated RACI matrix (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed) has served as a cornerstone managerial-governance, operational, developmental, and input-output instrument. However, it faces human biases and limits and is challenged by the AI world to date, failing to provide real-time, error-free sense-making of strategic decision-making and beneficial results. Methods: This study employs a qualitative, in-depth case-study methodology grounded in the ground-level reality of AI-Mediated RACI matrix organizational boardroom functioning, witnessed via the author's direct professional experience within an organization (anonymized for ethical compliance). The research compares a legacy human-mediated RACI system with an AI-augmented version implemented over 24 months. Data includes 1,247 decision events, 89 strategic meetings, and pre- and post-implementation operational metrics. Results: The AI-Mediated RACI Matrix demonstrated: (1) 97.4% accuracy in balancing inputs and outcomes per activity or project to dead-end; (2) 99.6% enablement of absolute and complete real-time operational efficiency, error-free sense-making of strategic decision-making, management effectiveness, and organizational defensibility; (3) 99.1% accuracy in allocating the cleaned and calculated Responsibility, Accountability, Consultation, and decision-ownership to smart actors for achieving beneficial results; and (4) identification of 92.4% of potential risk windows and vulnerability gates before they materialized into operational losses, with real-time mitigation solutions provided. Conclusions: The framework shifts organizational governance and management from self-risk windows, vulnerability, weakness, and loss gates to high-achieving success at domestic, regional, and international levels. For developing economies, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, this represents a mandatory—not optional—technological leap to overcome systemic self-hindering and operational shame stages. The paper concludes with a mandatory implementation protocol for AI-Mediated RACI in high-complexity IB environments from region to intercontinental arena.

title: Occupational Safety in Search and Rescue Operations after the 2023 Kahramanmaraş Earthquakes: A Case Study of Disaster Management in Türkiye

detail.title: Occupational Safety in Search and Rescue Operations after the 2023 Kahramanmaraş Earthquakes: A Case Study of Disaster Management in Türkiye
detail.abstract: Disaster response processes, particularly search and rescue (SAR) operations, involve highly complex and high-risk activities that require not only rapid intervention but also effective integration of occupational health and safety (OHS) principles. Despite the existence of comprehensive disaster management frameworks, the practical implementation of safety measures during large-scale disasters remains a critical challenge. This study examines occupational safety conditions in SAR operations within the context of the 6 February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes in Türkiye.Adopting a qualitative case study approach, the research is based on a systematic review of academic literature, official reports, and documented field observations. The analysis is structured through a thematic framework focusing on disaster management effectiveness, operational challenges, and occupational safety risks.The findings reveal significant gaps between theoretical disaster management frameworks and their implementation in practice. Key challenges include coordination deficiencies, delays in response, lack of standardized operational procedures, and inadequate enforcement of safety measures. Rescue personnel were exposed to multiple hazards, while occupational safety practices were inconsistently applied under field conditions.The study contributes to the literature by integrating OHS into disaster response analysis and highlights the need for a more holistic, safety-oriented approach to disaster management. It proposes policy recommendations for strengthening coordination, enhancing training, and embedding occupational safety into all phases of disaster management to improve resilience and operational effectiveness.

detail.abstract: Leadership research has long examined what makes leaders effective in specific organizational contexts. It has examined resilience, purpose, authenticity, and cultural intelligence. What it has not examinedwith sufficient precision or depth-is what makes certain leaders effective across every adversarial context they move through, regardless of betrayal, institutional failure, cultural complexity, or the cumulative weight of organizational experiences that would break most people. This paper introduces Psycho-Motivational Leadership Capacity (PMC) as a theoretically grounded framework for understanding that capacity. PMC is defined as the integrated operation of two mutually constitutive dimensions: assignment-grounded psychological stability-the decoupling of leadership identity from institutional approval through anchoring in defined task completion-and human seeingthe perceptual and relational capacity to read diverse human landscapes with sufficient accuracy and presence that the path to task completion becomes visible through organizational complexity rather than despite it. Together these dimensions produce a form of leadership intelligence that sustains effectiveness across sequential adversarial organizational environments, refining and integrating with each new encounter rather than depleting. Drawing on sustained autoethnographic inquiry across more than three decades of organizational leadership-spanning psychiatric healthcare, international hospital administration, humanitarian development, and organizational consulting across the United States, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and the Kurdistan Region of Iraq-this paper examines how PMC is formed through accumulated formative organizational experiences, how its constituent capacities operate in mutual reinforcement, and why its absence in conditions of compounded adversarial constraint produces leadership failure or collapse where its presence produces sustained effectiveness. The paper argues that PMC is not universally accessible-not every leader will or can extend their personal vulnerabilities, biases, and internal navigation sufficiently to produce this integrative learning. What distinguishes those who do is a specific willingness to allow adversarial experience to rewrite the internal navigation system rather than defending against it-producing a capacity that is simultaneously boundless in adaptability and singularly laser-focused on task-oriented execution. The central question this paper pursues is why certain leaders make this internal decision-and what it produces across a lifetime of organizational events.

detail.abstract:
This paper seeks to establish a more clearly bounded and more tightly constrained theoretical framework for the study of the long-term expansion trajectories of states. Its purpose is not to deny the importance of measurable factors such as population, capital, industry, technology, or fiscal capacity, but to argue that these forms of material capacity do not automatically translate into sustained expansion. Whether a state can sustain long-term expansion depends not only on what it possesses, but also on whether it can embed existing resources into a stable, replicable, and intertemporally durable cooperative structure.

To this end, the paper defines National Expansion Force as the structural force through which a state continuously integrates resources over time, expands the radius of cooperation, replicates organizational capacity, and sustains mobilizational capacity at a broader scale. Material capacity is defined as the mobilizable material base constituted by population, capital, industry, infrastructure, and technological equipment. Cooperative structure is then narrowed to four interrelated and non-substitutable dimensions: commitment-enforcement architecture, information-and-recording architecture, organizational-replication architecture, and coordinated-expectation architecture. The paper further distinguishes the structural layer, the mediating-process layer, and the outcome layer, and explicitly rejects the direct inclusion of behavioral responses and outcome variables—such as marriage rates, fertility rates, investment willingness, and consumer confidence—within cooperative structure itself.

The central proposition of the paper is that divergence in long-term state expansion trajectories does not arise primarily from static differences in material capacity, but from whether material capacity can be organized into a sustainable cooperative structure. This implies that parallel explanations based merely on resource depth, institutional scores, or state performance remain insufficient to capture the central object of explanation in long-term trajectory divergence. The contribution of this paper is not to complete empirical estimation immediately, but to establish a theoretical starting point for subsequent formal modeling, annual calculation, and case-based examination, while using six hard constraints to specify the conditions under which the framework should be weakened or abandoned.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of distributed and utility-scale PV expansion in China: Evidence from spatiotemporal heterogeneity

detail.title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of distributed and utility-scale PV expansion in China: Evidence from spatiotemporal heterogeneity
detail.abstract: With China’s dual-carbon goals and power system transformation, photovoltaic (PV) expansion increasingly exhibits differentiated patterns across deployment types. However, a unified quantitative assessment of the divergence in spatial trajectories and driving mechanisms for distributed PV (DPV) and utility-scale PV (UPV) remains limited. Using provincial panel data, this study develops an integrated analytical framework that combines spatial pattern identification, driver screening, and heterogeneous effect estimation to systematically analyze PV expansion. Specifically, Moran's I and LISA are utilized to characterize the stage-wise evolution of spatial dependence. We then employ the optimal parameters-based geographical detector (OPGD) to screen the primary sources of spatial differentiation, and apply geographically and temporally weighted regression (GTWR) to quantify how resource endowments, socioeconomic foundations, and grid-integration conditions heterogeneously shape these divergent pathways. Results show a clear divergence in spatial trajectories: DPV exhibits continuously strengthening spatial agglomeration and inland diffusion from coastal load centers, whereas UPV is anchored in resource-rich northwestern regions, with spatial agglomeration gradually weakening and evolving into more complex local configurations. In terms of driving mechanisms, DPV expansion is primarily driven by local demand intensity, economic activity, and investment conditions, whereas UPV is fundamentally constrained by natural resource endowments and system-level transmission and grid accommodation capacity. Furthermore, these driving effects display significant spatiotemporal non-stationarity across provinces and development stages. By elucidating the distinct spatial logics and structural drivers underlying these pathways, this study provides broader empirical insights for global renewable energy governance.

detail.abstract: The non-peripheral role of high-glycemic carbohydrates in the effectiveness of contemporary doping regimens is examined in this paper. This study suggests that sugar serves as a pharmacokinetic delivery system and a metabolic modulator in the context of professional doping, in contrast to traditional sports science, which sees sugar as a primary energy substrate. We discover a "Metabolic Overdrive" state by investigating the relationship between refined glucose and chemicals like exogenous insulin, human growth hormone (hGH), and anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS). We examine the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway, the GLUT4 translocation mechanism, and the reward center's dopaminergic sensitization. According to the data, athletes who use high-risk anabolic protocols must strategically manipulate the glycemic index in order to survive and succeed.

detail.title: Performance Management in Hospitality
detail.abstract: This chapter explores performance management in the hospitality industry, focusing on how effective systems boost employee engagement and drive organizational success. It examines the design of performance appraisal systems, stressing the need for alignment with organizational goals, fairness, and transparency. The chapter highlights the role of reward and recognition programs in motivating staff, supported by case studies from top hospitality organizations. It offers strategies to address underperformance, including identifying root causes, developing improvement plans, and implementing training interventions. The chapter ends with a look at future trends, such as technological advancements and changing employee expectations. It provides practical advice for implementing and improving performance management systems in this fast-paced industry, while also considering how cultural and regional differences shape these practices. Insights from case studies and emerging trends guide hospitality professionals in building effective performance management frameworks.

detail.title: Completion and In-depth Deduction of the Genetic Hierarchy Evolution System The Definition, Logic and Practical Verification of Level 4-Γ Rational Manipulation Gene
detail.abstract: Based on the twelve core definition system of value analysis and the core framework of the five-level genetic hierarchy evolution system, this paper identifies the evolutionary gap of Level 4 high-level evolutionary genes in the original system from the realistic social phenomenon of cult manipulation, and deduces its fourth evolutionary form-Level 4-Γ Rational Manipulation Gene, thus completing the logical closure and theoretical improvement of the genetic hierarchy evolution system. This paper clarifies the core connotation, behavioral logic and value expression characteristics of Level 4-Γ Rational Manipulation Gene, distinguishes its essential differences from Level 4-α, 4-β and 4-Δ, and expounds its evolutionary core of taking rationality as a tool, serving biological self-interest instinct, manipulating low-level genetic subjects and systematically creating group negative value. Combined with the core theories of value analysis such as potential value activation, value subject stratification and dynamic value change, it analyzes the negative value realization mechanism of Level 4-Γ Rational Manipulation Gene, and completes theoretical verification with cult phenomenon as a realistic anchor. This completion breaks the one-sided positive presupposition of rational awakening in the original genetic hierarchy evolution system, realizes the leap from "idealized theoretical deduction" to "realistic human nature restoration", makes the coupling logic of genetic hierarchy evolution and value realization more complete and practically explanatory, and provides a cross-genetic and value dimension theoretical framework for interpreting various social phenomena of group manipulation and negative value creation, enriching the research perspectives of behavioral science, value theory and social governance.

title: Market quality during an exchange outage: evidence from the NSE technical failure of February 2021

detail.title: Market quality during an exchange outage: evidence from the NSE technical failure of February 2021
detail.abstract: On 24 February 2021, the National Stock Exchange (NSE) of India suffered a major technical outage that suspended trading for approximately three and a half hours. Using daily bhavcopy data from NSE and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) for 1,215 equity securities matched exactly by ISIN and filtered for minimum liquidity, this paper examines whether the outage impaired market quality and whether volume migration to BSE was accompanied by spread widening. The BSE volume share rose from 11.6% to 24.9% on the event day. All three spread measures widened significantly: the BSE high-low range by 1.12 percentage points, the Corwin-Schultz spread by 0.57 percentage points, and the Roll spread by 0.67 percentage points, all at p < 0.01 and robust to stock and week fixed effects. A placebo test on 24 February 2020 produces no significant coefficients, confirming the effects are specific to the outage rather than a calendar regularity. The spread widening is monotonically increasing across liquidity terciles despite proportional volume migration being highest for the least liquid stocks. A mediation analysis shows that BSE volume share explains approximately 13% of the total spread effect, with the remainder reflecting direct disruption to the price formation process. All metrics recovered to pre-outage levels within five trading days.

detail.abstract: Innovative entrepreneurship in emerging digital environments develops under conditions characterized by high uncertainty, incomplete information, and partially structured market dynamics. In such contexts, early-stage decisions play a critical role in shaping the trajectory of technological projects, influencing both their technical viability and their capacity to adapt to market conditions. This study analyzes decision-making processes during the early stages of technological entrepreneurship, focusing on factors such as the absence of initial validation, the pressure to execute rapidly, and the interaction with an ecosystem often characterized by predominantly negative feedback. Using a qualitative approach grounded in real-world experience, the paper identifies recurring behavioral patterns that reveal systematic deviations from the assumptions of perfect rationality. The findings suggest that entrepreneurship should be understood as an adaptive system in which continuous learning, iterative decision-making, and responsiveness to environmental feedback are essential for long-term sustainability. The study contributes to the literature by highlighting the importance of incorporating behavioral and contextual dimensions into the economic analysis of entrepreneurship.

title: Homelessness in Salt Lake County and the Proposed Utah Campus

detail.title: Homelessness in Salt Lake County and the Proposed Utah Campus

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The study was made possible with the support of the Corporation for Supportive Housing.

detail.abstract: This paper evaluates Salt Lake County’s rising homelessness and the proposed 1,300-bed “transformative campus” as a policy response, assessing whether the model is likely to reduce chronic homelessness and improve outcomes. Drawing on local and national data, prior research, stakeholder interviews, and comparisons to similar campuses in other cities, the analysis finds that recent increases in homelessness—particularly among unsheltered and chronically homeless individuals—are driven primarily by structural factors such as rising housing costs and system capacity constraints, rather than changes in accountability policies. Evidence from other cities suggests that large centralized campuses alone do not reduce homelessness and that outcomes are more strongly associated with investments in permanent supportive housing. The report also raises concerns about key elements of the proposed campus, including limited evidence for involuntary treatment approaches, potential misalignment between projected capacity and the eligible population, and substantially underestimated capital and operating costs. Overall, the campus is characterized as a high-risk policy shift with significant fiscal, legal, and operational uncertainties, and the authors conclude that any campus-based strategy would need to be paired with sustained investment in permanent housing and rigorous evaluation to be effective.

title: Optimizing Multinomial Logistic Regression Weights Leveraging Enhanced ABC Algorithms

detail.title: Optimizing Multinomial Logistic Regression Weights Leveraging Enhanced ABC Algorithms
detail.abstract: Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) is a common choice in models for various classes classification tasks because it is easy to understand and reveals the structure of probabilities. On the other hand, the usual way of training MLR via gradient based methods is very sensitive to local optima on the complicated log, likelihood surfaces, especially in cases of high, dimensional or noisy feature spaces. In this paper, an ABC, MLR hybrid method is introduced where MLR weight optimization is considered a global search problem and is done via three advanced variations of the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm: Gbest, guided ABC (GABC), Opposition Based ABC (OABC), and Improved ABC (IABC). Thus, each variation is focused on the different shortcomings of the basic ABC by gaining global best guidance, integrating opposition-based learning, and utilizing chaotic, map initialization with multi, dimensional update strategies, respectively. A composite fitness function that combines classification accuracy and cross, entropy loss is used to guide the search, and an early stopping mechanism is incorporated to avoid unnecessary computations. The resulting classifiers GABC, MLR, OABC, MLR, and IABC, MLR are tested via stratified 10, fold cross, validation on 15 benchmark datasets from KEEL and UCI repositories, covering binary and multi, class problems of different sizes and dimensionalities, and are compared with eight well, known machine learning algorithms. The experimental results show that these three hybrid models always perform better than the standard gradient, trained MLR baseline, with GABC, MLR attaining the highest mean accuracy (0.8208) and mean F1, score (0.8032) over all datasets. The proposed framework keeps the interpretability of MLR while significantly improving its optimization robustness, thus offering a good and flexible alternative to the standard training methods for multi, class logistic regression.

title: The AI Act and Prediction Markets: Why Horizontal AI Regulation Cannot Comprehensively Govern Platform-Level Risk

detail.title: The AI Act and Prediction Markets: Why Horizontal AI Regulation Cannot Comprehensively Govern Platform-Level Risk
