detail.abstract: Can the EU Artificial Intelligence Act govern consumer-facing prediction markets? The short answer is: partially, but not primarily, and not comprehensively. Under current lex lata, the Act regulates the behaviour of discrete AI system components, whereas the principal risks that prediction markets pose-market manipulation, gamblified participation, epistemic distortion, democratic feedback-arise at the level of product design, market architecture, and sectoral classification. These are different levels of a complex regulatory problem, and a horizontal AI instrument is not designed to govern at all of them. To map this mismatch, the article develops a four-step AI Act Applicability Matrix and runs it across the four harm pathways. The Act performs genuine work at the component level: it constrains AI-enabled deception, vulnerability exploitation, and synthetic-content risks. What it does not address are the structural determinants of harm embedded in trading conduct, interface design, and platform-wide information dynamics. That work falls to MiCA, the Digital Services Act, the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive, the GDPR, and national gambling law-regimes the AI Act complements but cannot, under current law, replace. The article makes three contributions. It offers a doctrinal account of the AI Act's systematic incompleteness in this domain, distinguishing incompleteness from incapacity. It introduces the Applicability Matrix as a transferable diagnostic tool for any AI-enabled but structurally sectoral product. And it provides a comparative analysis explaining why each sectoral alternative is currently better suited than the AI Act to each primary harm dimension. The framework extends beyond prediction markets: the interaction between horizontal AI regulation and sector-specific product governance is one of the foundational design challenges of the EU's emerging digital regulatory order, and this article offers a method for approaching it. The conclusions are grounded in law and enforcement practice as of mid-2026, and identify the concrete conditions under which the incompleteness analysis would need to be revised.

title: Adaptively trained Physics-informed Radial Basis Function Neural Networks for Solving Multi-asset Option Pricing Problems

detail.title: Adaptively trained Physics-informed Radial Basis Function Neural Networks for Solving Multi-asset Option Pricing Problems
detail.abstract: The present study investigates the numerical solution of Black-Scholes partial differential equation (PDE) for option valuation with multiple underlying assets. We develop a physics-informed (PI) machine learning algorithm based on a radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) that concurrently optimizes the network architecture and predicts the target option price. The physics-informed radial basis function neural network (PIRBFNN) combines the strengths of the traditional radial basis function collocation method and the physics-informed neural network machine learning approach to effectively solve PDE problems in the financial context. By employing a PDE residual-based technique to adaptively refine the distribution of hidden neurons during the training process, the PIRBFNN facilitates accurate and efficient handling of multidimensional option pricing models featuring non-smooth payoff conditions. The validity of the proposed method is demonstrated through a set of experiments encompassing a single-asset European put option, a double-asset exchange option, and a four-asset basket call option.

title: Gene Five-Level Theory Evolution System: Final Formulation and Value Analysis Adaptation Research

detail.title: Gene Five-Level Theory Evolution System: Final Formulation and Value Analysis Adaptation Research
detail.abstract: The Gene Five-Level Theory is an interdisciplinary behavioral analysis system constructed on the laws of biological instinct and consciousness evolution, and deeply integrated with the Twelve Core Definitions of Value Analysis. As the finalized achievement of this theoretical system, this research supplements the α/β/Γ/Δ behavioral subdivision of the Level 1-3 basic biological gene layers on the basis of the preliminary phased research, unifies the behavioral analysis scale for all hierarchical levels with the four behavioral tools of self-benefiting, groupbenefiting, group-harming and non-value, and accurately calibrates the definitions of the four subtypes of Level 5 ultimate awakening genes. It thus realizes a complete logical closed loop from "core gene attributes-behavioral analysis tools-value behavioral results". Grounded in the Twelve Core Definitions of Value Analysis, this study clarifies the value essence, trigger mechanisms and evolutionary boundaries of behaviors at all levels and their internal subdivisions, and constructs a complete evolutionary main line of "instinctive survival < gene transmission < perceptual group < rational dominance < spiritual autonomy". The system realizes the in-depth integration of gene evolution and value analysis, providing a standardized genebehavior-value analysis framework for behavioral science, sociology, public governance and other fields. With its theoretical originality, logical rigor and practical applicability, it can serve as a basic theoretical tool for interdisciplinary research on human behavioral evolution.

title: From Adoption to Accountability: A Civic AI Governance Framework for Public Sector Systems
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: From Adoption to Accountability: A Civic AI Governance Framework for Public Sector Systems
detail.abstract: Governments worldwide are accelerating AI adoption in public services. Yet prevailing governance frameworks remain oriented toward implementation-addressing how AI should be deployed, rather than whether specific decisions should be delegated to AI systems at all. This paper argues that the central governance challenge is not adoption but accountabilityspecifically, how governments can ensure that AI-enabled decisions in public systems remain traceable, contestable, and institutionally owned, particularly where those decisions carry long-term or irreversible consequences for citizens. The paper introduces the Civic AI Governance Framework (CAGF)-a practical decision lens to help governments determine whether and how AI should be used in public sector systems, particularly where those systems-whether citizen-facing or operating as backend processes-affect citizen outcomes, rights, or entitlements, and where decisions carry long-term consequences. A central concern of the framework is the risk of institutionalised decision stratification-the process by which AI systems, operating at scale in civic contexts, classify citizens into decision categories that may encode historical inequalities, become invisible to those affected, and acquire an institutional permanence that undermines the constitutional obligation to treat citizens as individuals rather than as members of algorithmically assigned groups. CAGF is structured around five governance dimensions: Use Case Suitability, Risk and Impact, Governance and Accountability, Controls and Assurance, and Operational Readiness. It is designed to complement existing AI governance frameworks by addressing the admissibility question they leave unresolved-not how to optimise AI deployment, but whether specific civic decisions should be delegated to AI at all, and what governance structures must exist when they are. CAGF reframes AI governance in public systems from a problem of optimisation to one of decision admissibility-where institutional accountability and social consequence are the governing constraints.

title: Socioeconomic Drivers of Matrilocality and Community Perceptions Towards Men’s  Living Matrilocally in the Amhara Region, Ethiopia
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of South Africa

detail.title: Socioeconomic Drivers of Matrilocality and Community Perceptions Towards Men’s  Living Matrilocally in the Amhara Region, Ethiopia
detail.abstract: Post-marital residence choice considers social, cultural, economic, ecological, gender and kinship roles to determine the wellbeing of couples and their families. This ethnographic study explored the socioeconomic factors driving matrilocality and community feelings towards men’s living matrilocally in the Amhara region, Ethiopia. Using qualitative research design, data was collected from June - December 2025. Document review and participant observation served to triangulate data collected through two group discussions with 19 participants, and interviews with 27 purposively selected participants. Thematic analysis was conducted in line with the aim of the study. The findings revealed that beyond economic reasons, matrilocality is favored if women’s families needed a male labor, protection services, and if the man/the woman or both could not peacefully live patrilocally. It reveals that matrilocality becomes a survival strategy for men who were accused of murder in their natal villages and if they feared Dem memeles (a revenge killing) by the relatives of the deceased. It shows that men living matrilocally were given low socioeconomic status which emanates from their lower economic positions and social networks. Policy actions on enhancing employment opportunities, considering fair land reforms, and awareness against cultural norms undermining men living matrilocally are recommended.

title: Demographics and Monetary Policy: Transmission, Regime Breaks, and the Post-QE Question

detail.title: Demographics and Monetary Policy: Transmission, Regime Breaks, and the Post-QE Question
detail.abstract: This paper documents three channels through which demographic structure shapes monetary policy environments --- interest rate levels, inflation dynamics, and monetary transmission --- and shows how their interaction creates a systematic "demographic monetary trap" for aging economies. Using a panel of up to 237 countries from 1970 to 2024, we find that the Higgins (1998) demographic polynomial Z_1 robustly predicts real bond yields ( Z_1 = 57.1 , p < 0.001 on 10-year rates; 55.2 , p < 0.05 on 3-month rates), with 5-year lagged demographics also significant ( Z_1 = 51.3 , p < 0.001 ) and predetermined demographics (OADR projected 20 years forward) significant at -21.3 ( p < 0.001 ). A confirmed structural break at the Global Financial Crisis (Chow F = 50.2 , p < 0.001 ) is not an exogenous shock but the endpoint of decades of demographic compression of the neutral rate: non-QE countries retain a robust demographic-rate relationship ( Z_1 = 103.5 , p < 0.001 ), while QE countries --- those where demographic compression was most advanced --- show attenuated coefficients ( Z_1 = 54.2 , p < 0.05 ). Among institutional moderators, the zero lower bound suppresses rate levels (near\_zlb = -0.78 , p < 0.001 ) but does not differentially moderate the demographic component ( Z_1 × ZLB = +0.25 , NS); and central bank independence is associated with stronger rather than weaker demographic pass-through to inflation ( Z_1 × CBI = +71.7 , p < 0.05 ), consistent with high-CBI institutions responding to demographic signals rather than insulating from them. Reduced-form local projections suggest that rate changes in older economies co-move with larger output responses ( Z_1 × Δ r negative and significant at h = 2 ), though we cannot identify exogenous monetary shocks. Post-QE normalization (2022--2024) provides tentative evidence that the demographic gradient re-emerges as the policy ceiling lifts. The findings imply that aging economies face a narrower operating corridor for conventional policy: potentially amplified transmission effects but a lower neutral rate, a flatter Phillips curve, and diminished inflation signals to guide calibration. Baseline controls follow the income-conditioned standard: fiscal balance, lagged NFA, GDP growth, log GDP per capita, and the Z₁ × log GDP/cap interaction; R² on 10-year bond yields rises to 0.40.

title: Demographic Divergence and Safe Asset Scarcity

detail.title: Demographic Divergence and Safe Asset Scarcity
detail.abstract: Population aging increases demand for safe assets while the supply of safe sovereign debtconcentrated in a few AAA-rated economies-grows only with the fiscal capacity of those same aging issuers. We bridge the demographic-current account literature with the Caballero-Farhi-Gourinchas safe asset framework using a 237-country panel (1990-2024). We find: (1) demographics depress safe sovereign yields (Z_1 ≈ 57.1, p < 0.01, 10-year bonds) but the effect concentrates among safe-rated issuers; (2) aging countries tilt portfolios toward debt over equity and disproportionately allocate to safe-rated destinations; (3) global safe supply relative to demographic demand has declined secularly, compressing convenience yield proxies; (4) bilateral gravity estimates confirm safe-seeking-the demographic distance effect is stronger when the destination holds AA-or above rating; (5) forward projections show a widening "safe asset gap" through 2050, as demographic demand accelerates while several current safe issuers face downgrade risk from fiscal pressure. The paradox is self-reinforcing: aging raises safe asset demand while simultaneously undermining the fiscal foundations of safe asset supply.

title: Does ESG Engagement Constrain Corporate Tax Avoidance? Evidence From Developing Economies: A Narrative Review
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Delaware

detail.title: Does ESG Engagement Constrain Corporate Tax Avoidance? Evidence From Developing Economies: A Narrative Review
detail.abstract: Corporate tax avoidance erodes fiscal capacity in developing economies, where tax-to-GDP ratios already trail OECD benchmarks by wide margins, and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) engagement has been proposed as a market-based check on aggressive tax behavior. Whether that check operates outside the high-income settings where most evidence originates remains uncertain. Twenty-one empirical studies published between 2015 and 2025 address this question in World Bank-classified low-and middle-income countries; the present narrative review organizes their findings by ESG pillar rather than treating ESG as a single composite. Governance mechanisms, including board independence, audit committee composition, and institutional ownership, show the most consistent negative association with avoidance, documented across ten studies spanning eight countries. Environmental and social pillars receive far less empirical attention (three and two dedicated studies, respectively) and produce no reliable standalone effects; one Nigerian study finds CSR expenditure positively associated with avoidance, opposite to the direction stakeholder theory predicts. Composite ESG scores yield mixed results: four studies report a negative association and two a positive one. National institutional quality emerges as the key moderator; in a 14-country panel, the ESGavoidance association holds where rule of law and regulatory enforcement are strong and disappears where they are weak. Three Chinese studies using the same ESG rating provider reach opposing conclusions, underscoring the sensitivity of composite measures to sample period and model specification. The evidence base draws exclusively on exchange-listed firms, leaving unlisted businesses and the informal sector unexamined. Regulators in developing economies should prioritize governance-focused requirements (audit oversight composition, independent director thresholds, ownership transparency) over composite ESG frameworks, and pair those requirements with the enforcement infrastructure on which their effectiveness depends.

title: Optimizing bio-based SCM concrete for sustainable construction through structural and environmental evaluation driven by explainable surrogate modeling
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong, Roma Tre University, Roma Tre University, Roma Tre University, The University of Hong Kong and Zhejiang University

detail.title: Optimizing bio-based SCM concrete for sustainable construction through structural and environmental evaluation driven by explainable surrogate modeling
detail.abstract: The decarbonization of the construction sector requires renewable and low-carbon binders, among which bio-based supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) are a promising option. However, their broader adoption is hindered by fragmented datasets, limited model interpretability, and weak linkage between mixture optimization and engineering-scale application. This study presents a reproducible surrogate-based framework for optimizing bio-based SCM concrete with respect to mechanical performance and embodied carbon. Three curated datasets were assembled for compressive strength (fc), flexural strength (ff ), and split tensile strength (ft), comprising 1665, 446,and 352 records, respectively. Four surrogate models were benchmarked using a multi-fidelity successive-halving hyperparameter strategy with explicit regularization and trend checks. XGB remained the preferred regularized surrogate model for fc and ff , whereas ANN provided the best predictive fit for ft. The verified test performance reached R2 = 0.956 for fc, 0.949 for ff , and 0.957 for ft. SHAP and LiNGAM were integrated to reveal target-specific governing variables and directed dependencies. Building on these validated surrogates, multi-objective optimization was employed to quantify the trade-offs between mechanical performance and concrete embodied carbon intensity (CFv). To advance beyond black-box optimization, two-objective parametric Pareto-front fitting and three-objective regularized parametric surface fitting were established, providing transparent visualization and explicit mathematical representation of the strength–carbon relationship. The framework is further extended to engineering-scale decision support, enabling the translation of material-level optimization into building- and beam-scale structural applications. Notably, at the building scale, replacing conventional concrete classes with Pareto-selected bio-based SCM mixes reduced embodied carbon by up to 31%. Overall, the study delivers a transparent and reusable computational workflow for screening, interpreting, optimizing, and practically deploying bio-based SCM concrete in sustainable construction.

title: Trade-offs Between Equity and Efficiency in Prioritizing Critical Infrastructure Investments: A Case of Stormwater Management Systems
affiliations: Florida Atlantic University - Department of Information Technology & Operations Management, Virginia Tech - Pamplin College of Business,  and Florida Atlantic University

detail.title: Trade-offs Between Equity and Efficiency in Prioritizing Critical Infrastructure Investments: A Case of Stormwater Management Systems

publicationDetails.detailsText: Production and Operations Management, volume 34, issue 4, 2025[10.1177/10591478241243387]

detail.abstract: Critical infrastructures in many countries face the problem of aging and, thus, require significant upgrades to continue serving their purpose for the next few decades, especially in the face of extreme weather events caused by global climate change. Given the urgent need for such improvements and the substantial funding gaps being experienced, prioritizing investments in critical infrastructures is a challenging task for governments. Furthermore, the need to assure equitable solutions, as well as to consider deep uncertainty due to climate change, adds to the complexity of the problem. We seek to address this complexity by developing a set of models that explicitly consider both horizontal and vertical equity, along with efficiency, in prioritizing stormwater infrastructure improvement projects. While horizontal equity seeks to provide equal resources to everyone, vertical equity aims to allocate relatively more resources to vulnerable groups who are disproportionately susceptible to shocks and are more likely to fall into chronic poverty. By differentiating between losses in horizontal equity and vertical equity due to efficiency considerations, the models provide a practical approach to find the right balance among efficiency, horizontal equity, and vertical equity. The initial models are then extended into regret-based optimization models to help address the issue of deep uncertainty. A case study of stormwater infrastructure improvement in the City of Miami is presented, through which the performance of the models is explored both with and without the projected sea-level rise scenarios. The findings highlight the value of the proposed approach in promoting equity while maintaining efficiency.

detail.abstract: Sustainable development currently occupies a central place on the international agenda, as our sustainable future depends on its implementation. The concept of sustainable development was first defined on August 4, 1987, in the report "Our Common Future," presented by the World Commission on Environment and Development at the forty-second session of the UN General Assembly. The concept of sustainable development is enshrined in key international documents: the Rio Declaration (1992), the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (1992), the Kyoto Protocol (1997), and the Paris Agreement (2015), which is a legally binding treaty for participating countries. The UN General Assembly also developed a new institutional framework for global environmental governance-the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), set in 2015 for 2030. However, given the numerous environmental problems and the constant violations of existing conventions, protocols, and declarations by countries, it becomes clear that the primary solution to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals is the legal implementation of sustainable development at the level of regional integration associations and the incorporation of this concept into the legal frameworks of their member countries. Therefore, this report will identify the key legal gaps in environmental integration among EAEU member states that require further regulation.

title: Machine Learning-Informed Scheduling of Electric Vehicle Charging with Emergency-Priority Control and Route-Aware Reallocation
affiliations: BRAC University, BRAC University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology, Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology and BRAC University

detail.title: Machine Learning-Informed Scheduling of Electric Vehicle Charging with Emergency-Priority Control and Route-Aware Reallocation
detail.abstract: The intensive diffusion of electric-vehicles (EVs) has posed serious challenges to power distribution networks, especially in urban charging settings where uncoordinated charging may cause peak-hour congestion, transformer overloading, and poor service delivery. A major challenge in EV charging management is the uncertainty in arrival state-of-charge (SOC), charging duration, and energy demand, which complicates both day-ahead planning and real-time decision-making. Existing scheduling approaches primarily focus on optimization and policy design but often assume that these parameters are known or can be approximated using simple heuristics, limiting their effectiveness under real-world variability. To fill this gap, this paper suggests a combined machine-learning-based EV charging scheduling system that explicitly links predictive intelligence and policy optimization. The proposed solution would involve using supervised machine learning models to effectively forecast the SOC of EVs at arrival, charging time, and energy consumption with reference to past charging data. Such predicted values are subsequently inscribed into a multi-layered scheduling that facilitates not only a route-based charging station shifting but also provides user-preference-conscious slot allocation while processing priority of emergency vehicles in real-time. Additionally, a demand-based time-of-use (TOU) tariff is introduced to reduce peak-hour grid stress. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms non-predictive methods, achieving approximately 98.9% higher energy throughput and 40% more vehicle allocation, while also reducing peak load, shortening waiting times, and improving emergency response. The most significant outcome of this work is a single framework that can be easily scaled and applied to create an effective solution for managing intelligent EV charging.

title: Spatially Resolved Techno-Economic and Life Cycle Assessment of Power-to-Methanol Systems: A Multi-Regional, Multi-Technology Comparison Across 27 Configurations
affiliations: Pukyong National University, Chung-Ang University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Chung-Ang University and Pukyong National University

detail.title: Spatially Resolved Techno-Economic and Life Cycle Assessment of Power-to-Methanol Systems: A Multi-Regional, Multi-Technology Comparison Across 27 Configurations
detail.abstract: Decarbonizing methanol production requires deploying renewable hydrogen-based pathways, yet their techno-economic and environmental performance varies dramatically across regions. Existing assessments rely on national-average assumptions and single-technology evaluations, failing to capture spatial variability in renewable resources, water availability, and infrastructure costs that determine deployment feasibility. This study develops a geographically resolved Power-to-Methanol (PtM) framework by integrating spatial techno-economic analysis (S-TEA), spatial life cycle assessment (S-LCA), and water scarcity evaluation across 27 configurations, combining three electrolyzer technologies with three renewable energy sources across three representative regions. Regional renewable electricity cost, carbon intensity, and water availability create substantial performance variation, with minimum methanol selling price (MMSP) ranging from $0.84 to $2.18/kg methanol. The solar-powered polymer electrolyte membrane (PEM) electrolyzer systems achieved the lowest MMSP in the United States ($0.84/kg methanol) and Australia ($0.86/kg methanol), while the wind-powered solid oxide electrolyzer cell (SOEC) systems delivered the lowest global warming potential (0.48 kg CO2-eq/kg methanol) in both countries. Water scarcity potential varied substantially (0.09 to 1.85 m3 world-eq/kg methanol), with solar-based systems in Australia exhibiting the highest water stress. Pareto analysis identified four optimal configurations balancing cost-carbon trade-offs. In renewable-rich regions, PEM–solar systems can approach cost parity with fossil methanol, whereas resource-constrained regions require alternative strategies such as SOEC–hybrid systems, carbon pricing, or hydrogen imports. The proposed framework provides decision-makers with quantitative insights for multi-criteria site selection and supports region-specific strategies for PtM deployment.

detail.title: Construction disputes remain a persistent challenge in project delivery, yet empirical research focuses on the execution stage, leaving dispute causation during the Closeout phase underexplored
detail.abstract: Construction disputes remain a persistent challenge, yet most empirical research focuses on the execution stage, leaving dispute causation during the Closeout phase underexplored. This study addresses that gap by identifying Closeout‐specific dispute causes and examining stakeholder differences in their perceptions. Causes were derived from the literature and evaluated through a survey of construction professionals, with responses analyzed using established statistical procedures. Findings show that the most frequent Closeout disputes stem from procedural delays, unclear post‐completion responsibilities, and coordination breakdowns. Stakeholders showed strong internal agreement and broad cross‐group alignment, except for insurance‐related disputes, which contractors perceived as more frequent.

title: TITTLE: Understanding AI-Driven Personalization: A Guide to the New Digital Marketplace

detail.title: TITTLE: Understanding AI-Driven Personalization: A Guide to the New Digital Marketplace
detail.abstract: AI-driven personalization is transforming the digital marketplace by shifting commerce from generic interactions to real-time, individualized experiences. This evolution positions AI as a proactive decision-maker, leveraging data such as search behavior, purchase patterns, and inventory levels to optimize customer engagement and drive conversions. Techniques like dynamic pricing and targeted incentives enhance efficiency but also raise concerns around transparency and trust. The paper distinguishes between Generative AI, which focuses on reactive content creation, and Agentic AI, which enables autonomous, proactive decision-making across systems. While organizations report significant gains in lead generation, retention, and productivity, a notable gap remains between technological capability and consumer comfort, particularly regarding autonomous purchasing decisions. From a value perspective, AI reduces cognitive effort for consumers and enhances convenience, yet ethical challenges persist. Issues such as price discrimination, data privacy, and perceived unfairness highlight the importance of transparency and trust in sustaining long-term relationships. Case studies from global brands demonstrate that strategies centered on price integrity and clarity can strengthen consumer confidence. Looking ahead, the future of personalization lies in anticipatory commerce, though progress is constrained by data integration challenges and the need for human involvement in complex interactions. Ultimately, successful AI adoption depends on balancing technological efficiency with fairness, transparency, and human-centric design to deliver meaningful and trustworthy customer experiences.

title: Net vs Gross External Adjustment: Demographics as a Latent Factor

detail.title: Net vs Gross External Adjustment: Demographics as a Latent Factor
detail.abstract: Does demographic structure predict net external positions? Using a 185-country panel over 1970-2024 with income-conditioned controls (log GDP per capita and Z₁ × log GDP/cap), the answer in aggregate is no: the Z₁ coefficient on the income balance is 10.6 (NS, p=0.66), and on the full-sample current account is-18.7 (NS). The prior finding of "income balance dominance" was confounded by development-level differences. Two genuine channels survive income conditioning. First, FX reserve accumulation is the demographic vehicle: Z₁ = 95.9*** (p=0.001) in the full sample, 96.1*** excluding financial centers, and 88.4*** winsorized. No other gross position instrument achieves consistent significance. Second, within the OECD, demographics predict a striking mirror pattern: Z₁ =-63.8*** (p=0.009) on the current account and Z₁ = +63.7*** (p=0.006) on the valuation residual, meaning aging economies simultaneously generate current account surpluses and valuation losses that nearly cancel at the NIIP level. Rolling-window evidence shows the income balance coefficient evolving from 275*** (1985-1994) to near-zero during the QE era, with a short-window cross-section for 2022-2024 yielding 68.6** (p<0.05). Rate mediation is directionally consistent: controlling for real bond yields shifts the pre-GFC income balance Z₁ from 38.0 to-52.7, a-239% attenuation, though both endpoints lack individual significance. The net/gross decomposition matters: aggregate external positions hide heterogeneous asset-class responses in which FX reserves are the only consistent demographic channel and the lifecycle savings story operates through official reserve accumulation rather than private portfolio flows.

title: Fiction as External Lens: What Stories May Reveal About the Patterns We Cannot See in Real Life

detail.title: Fiction as External Lens: What Stories May Reveal About the Patterns We Cannot See in Real Life
detail.abstract: There is a well-documented phenomenon in experimental economics: offer someone ten dollars, keep seven for yourself, and most people will reject it. Not because the math is wrong. Because something in the body refuses before the mind can intervene. This paper begins there, with the gap between what we know and what we actually do, and asks whether fiction may be one of the few places where that gap is shown without penalty. When stories like Dark, The OA, and Primer present characters who cannot choose, who deceive themselves without knowing it, who cause harm while trying to prevent it, audiences frequently report recognition rather than surprise. That recognition appears to be data. This paper treats it as such.

detail.abstract:
This paper argues that in the Fifth Industrial Revolution (5IR), art and culture move from peripheral "content" to core infrastructure shaping technology, economics, and governance.
Rather than treating creativity as a decorative add-on to AI, robotics, and biomanufacturing, we conceptualize culture as (1) training data and value-alignment layer for intelligent systems, (2) interface between complex sociotechnical systems and citizens, (3) ethical operating system translating abstract principles into lived norms, and (4) a resilient employment frontier in an age of automation.
Drawing on emerging literature on 5IR and participatory design, case studies of Asian digital public infrastructure, organizational transformation models, and speculative scenarios, we develop an original framework-the Cultural Operating System (C-OS)-and a policy-relevant agenda for governments, firms, and multilateral institutions. We advance a contrarian claim: without deliberate cultural strategy, 5IR will quietly default to a "Fourth Industrial Revolution 2.0," technologically upgraded but humanly hollow.

detail.title: Assessing the Charging Flexibility and Demand Response Potential of Multi-Type Electric Vehicles for Fine-Grained Urban Power Grid Regulation: Evidence from Charging Big Data in Shenzhen
detail.abstract: As electric vehicles (EVs) continue to proliferate, their charging demand poses increasing challenges to the secure operation and fine-grained regulation of urban power grids. Based on city-scale real-world charging big data from Shenzhen, China, this study develops a four-dimensional framework to assess the charging flexibility of 12 vehicle-use categories in terms of temporal, spatial, power, and energy dimensions, and further evaluates the effects of time-of-use (TOU) pricing and the potential of grid-cell-level demand response. The dataset covers more than 21 million charging events, 931549 anonymized vehicles, and over 4500 vehicle models. The results reveal pronounced heterogeneity across vehicle categories: private passenger cars exhibit relatively high temporal flexibility, taxi passenger cars and logistics special vehicles show comparatively high spatial flexibility, and engineering special vehicles demonstrate the strongest power and energy regulation capability, supporting differentiated control strategies. Under the existing TOU pricing scheme, Shenzhen’s average daily charging demand reaches about 6656 MWh, of which 4029 MWh occurs during valley periods. Compared with the immediate-charging baseline, current TOU pricing has already shifted about 644 MWh/day to valley periods, while smart charging could further raise valley charging demand by 275 MWh/day to 4304 MWh/day. Further demand response simulations on the top 50 most charging-active grid cells show that, under a system-level criterion, the reduced-power charging experiment supports a uniform acceptable reduction rate of about 17%. In the spatial transfer experiment, achieving a 500 kW peak reduction requires at least 72 participating vehicles, and the required number of vehicles increases by about 12 for every additional 100 kW. These findings provide quantitative support for fine-grained urban demand response design and flexible resource management for urban power grids.

O episódio do podcast O Marketeiro, com entrevista de Diego Oliveira, discute a importância da diversidade e da inclusão na comunicação institucional como elementos centrais para a transformação social. O entrevistado ressalta que tais práticas não devem ser tratadas como estratégias superficiais de marketing, mas como mudanças estruturais que precisam estar enraizadas na cultura organizacional. Ele critica empresas que buscam apenas certificações ou prêmios, sem compromisso real com a inclusão, e defende a adoção de métricas concretas para avaliar resultados.

Como exemplo prático, ele menciona o I Censo de Diversidade e Inclusão no mercado de comunicação da Bahia, que revelou falhas nas lideranças e a necessidade de campanhas com pessoas reais.

Entre as recomendações, o entrevistado sugere o uso de linguagem neutra, a ampliação de fontes diversas e a atenção aos novos comportamentos digitais, como formas de construir conexões autênticas e prevenir crises de imagem. detail.abstract: This study examined the role of barangay Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) operations in crime prevention and emergency response in selected barangays in Mandaluyong City. Specifically, it explored stakeholder experiences, operational challenges, and recommendations for improving the effectiveness, sustainability, and acceptability of barangay CCTV systems. Using a qualitative phenomenological design, the study gathered data through semi-structured interviews with ten purposively selected participants, including barangay officials, CCTV operators, barangay tanods, and community members. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis guided by Rational Choice Theory, Routine Activity Theory, and Systems Theory. Findings revealed that CCTV systems improved situational awareness, strengthened crime investigation, enhanced emergency response coordination, and increased perceived safety in the community. However, their effectiveness was constrained by technological limitations, lack of continuous monitoring, insufficient personnel training, budgetary constraints, and governance concerns related to coordination, privacy, and public trust. The study concludes that barangay CCTV systems are most effective when supported by reliable infrastructure, active monitoring, trained personnel, adequate funding, and transparent governance. It is recommended that barangays strengthen technological capacity, improve operational protocols, increase budget allocation, enhance personnel training, and integrate CCTV systems with crime mapping and intelligence-led policing strategies to maximize their effectiveness in community safety.

title: Data-driven Optimization of Aircraft Sequencing and Descent Trajectories for Fuel Efficiency in the Terminal Manoeuvring Area

detail.title: Data-driven Optimization of Aircraft Sequencing and Descent Trajectories for Fuel Efficiency in the Terminal Manoeuvring Area
detail.abstract: The airspace surrounding an airport — known as the Terminal Maneuvering Area (TMA) — is the primary locus of air traffic interactions, where the simultaneous coordination of arrivals and departures poses significant challenges for air traffic management (ATM). Under the current Time-Based Management (TBM) paradigm, flights within the TMA are managed by first assigning fixed crossing times at designated waypoints while satisfying separation requirements (i.e., multi-aircraft flow-level optimization), followed by optimizing individual aircraft trajectories to generate feasible four-dimensional profiles — position, altitude, and time (i.e., single-aircraft trajectory optimization). However, most existing flow-level optimization approaches focus solely on minimizing airborne delays, without explicitly accounting for the environmental implications of how these delays are distributed across the TMA. Consequently, the optimized waypoint crossing times derived from multi-aircraft flow-level optimization may result in fuel-inefficient aircraft trajectories (as demonstrated in this paper). To address this limitation, we propose a bi-objective, fuel-aware, stochastic TMA flow-level optimization framework that jointly minimizes airborne delay and fuel consumption. The modeling strategy integrates three main components: (i) a data-driven approximation of fuel consumption and its endogenous uncertainty as a function of link travel time; (ii) an optimization-based matheuristic that combines linear programming and a genetic algorithm to optimize waypoint sequencing and scheduling; and (iii) a waypoint-time-constrained optimal control model that generates realistic aircraft trajectories. This integrated approach produces optimized waypoint sequencing and scheduling alongside fuel-efficient trajectories. Results from a full day of operations at Singapore Changi Airport indicate that the proposed framework reduces total fuel consumption by 6.2% compared to a First-Come-First-Served (FCFS) baseline and by 5.5% relative to a delay-minimization approach, demonstrating its potential to enhance TMA sustainability without compromising operational efficiency.

title: Financial Misconduct and Import Competition

detail.title: Financial Misconduct and Import Competition
detail.abstract: We document an overlooked real cost of financial misconduct: the erosion of domestic firms’ competitive position in the U.S. product markets. Using a generalized stacked difference-in-differences design, we find that import penetration increases significantly after SEC enforcement actions (AAERs) reveal misconduct at U.S. firms. Supporting a reputational mechanism driven by counterparty responses, the increase in import penetration is concentrated in industries where counterparty trust is economically consequential: those where customers face high product quality uncertainty, suppliers engage in complex input relationships, and firms depend heavily on external capital providers. Consistent with these reputational costs extending beyond the fraudulent firm to the domestic industry, the post-AAER increase in import penetration is amplified in industries with multiple AAER cases, greater public firm presence, and a larger fraction of firms experiencing negative stock returns around the AAER announcement. Finally, using granular transaction-level trade data, we show that foreign firms from countries with strict disclosure regimes, as well as more productive foreign firms, are better positioned to expand into U.S. product markets following domestic misconduct revelations. These results indicate that the revelation of financial misconduct has real consequences for competitive dynamics between domestic and foreign firms, reallocating demand from domestic producers to foreign rivals.

detail.abstract: The number of foreigners in Japan has increased significantly in recent years due to the strategies the government has applied as a solution for labor shortage. However, the largely monocultural Japanese society has started expressing dissatisfaction highlighting the crimes committed by foreigners. Meanwhile, the number of Sri Lankans who migrate to Japan for study and work purposes has been largely increasing. Consequently, this research was conducted to understand current situations experienced by Sri Lankan students and workers in Japan and to explore the vulnerabilities and risk factors for them and suggest recommendations to mitigate such difficulties. Using convenience sampling, primary data was collected through a structured online questionnaire completed by 112 Sri Lankan migrants residing in Japan. Qualitative data were generated from 15 semi-structured interviews with Sri Lankan students, SSW workers, long-term residents, and Japanese-language instructors in Sri Lanka. The interviews were thematically analysed to identify recurring patterns of vulnerability and adaptation. The research concludes that Unwelcome, Foreigners as Temporary Outsiders, Ignorance, Insecure, Cheated-which in other words vulnerability can play some role in Crime, indicating that if the migrants are less vulnerable, apart from the organised crimes, some of the crimes too might decline to some extent. Further concluded that given Japan's labor shortages and opening doors to foreigners, the Japanese people should be made aware of the need of foreigners and how to tolerate different cultures. Intercultural events and seminars for Japanese citizens to understand how to accept differences and eliminate prejudice against foreigners and explanatory sessions of current rules and regulations to foreigners in easily understandable languages are recommended. Further, recommendations to Sri Lanka include a carefully planned curricular for Japanese language education, establishment of a proper channel between the two countries to regularise the visa process, and training programs that provide awareness of sociocultural background and legal system in Japan. These measures would prepare those who migrate to Japan for study or work purposes, ultimately contributing to sustainable development with focus on SDG4 and SDG13.

detail.title: International comparison of Environmental performance
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes environmental productivity dynamics by integrating undesir able outputs into a Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) framework using directional distance functions. It compares the standard Malmquist-Luenberger (ML) pro ductivity index with its sequential extension (SML), emphasizing the impact of methodological choices on productivity measurement. Using a panel of European countries and the United States over the period 1995–2010, the empirical analysis shows that technological progress is the main driver of productivity growth, while efficiency changes remain limited or negative for several countries. The results also demonstrate that the sequential approach eliminates artificial technological regress, leading to more consistent and robust measures of productivity dynamics. Furthermore, the study provides evidence of beta-convergence, although signifi cant heterogeneity persists across countries. The findings highlight that environmen tal constraints interact with structural economic characteristics and may reinforce differences in performance. Finally, the paper proposes an interpretation of environmental productivity in terms of environmental resilience, defined as the ability of economies to sustain long term growth while reducing environmental pressures. This perspective contributes to bridging the gap between productivity analysis and the broader literature on sustainable economic development.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a New Keynesian model with financial intermediaries and a repo market in which a stress regime tightens rollover capacity while private haircuts are determined endogenously by collateral liquidation risk. The model implies that secured funding stress raises haircuts, forces asset sales, weakens liquidation recovery values, and tightens investment. It also implies that margins can tighten before realized run-induced deleveraging episodes, because weaker expected liquidation values reduce borrowing capacity before forced sales materialize. Nonlinear quantitative exercises show that a central bank backstop is most effective when it relaxes secured borrowing directly through softer collateral terms, whereas higher facility spreads weaken stabilization; fixed haircut counterfactuals show that time variation in margins is itself an important source of amplification. These results provide a New Keynesian theory of repo-run amplification in which funding quantities, liquidation values, and margins are jointly determined, and they clarify how lender-of-last-resort policy can contain secured funding crises.

detail.abstract:
The valuation paradox of nature represents the central dilemma of contemporary environmental governance: the very mechanisms designed to protect ecosystems from market destruction-monetary valuation and market-based conservation paradoxically enable continued degradation through commodification, offsetting, and financialization. This policy paper synthesizes 40+ years of implementation evidence from Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) in England, Payments for Ecosystem Services (PES) globally, and emerging Corporate Natural Capital Accounting (CNCA) to demonstrate that market-based conservation delivers negligible biodiversity outcomes while creating institutional lock-in perpetuating failed approaches. 
Through analysis of empirical case studies and contrarian literature, this paper argues that the fundamental incompatibility between irreversible ecosystem functions and market logic cannot be resolved through improved monetization alone. We propose a differentiated governance framework allocating market mechanisms only to provisioning services with demonstrated substitutes and low irreversibility; mandating regulatory hard constraints for critical natural capital; and centering Indigenous rights-based approaches for culturally significant ecosystems. 
This hybrid model reconciles market and regulatory tools while preventing commodification of irreplaceable functions. Strategic recommendations target policymakers implementing the Global Biodiversity Framework (2026-2030), emphasizing regulatory prioritization over financial disclosure, Indigenous land rights recognition, and abandonment of offset-based policy architectures. Implementation requires reframing biodiversity protection from an economic optimization problem to a regulatory preservation imperative.

detail.abstract:
This dissertation investigates the issue of biopiracy and the meaning of the issue to the protection of the traditional knowledge, specifically the legal response of India to the issue and the weakness of the international legal system. The fields of medicine, agriculture, biodiversity conservation and cultural practice all center around traditional knowledge, which is developed, preserved and transmitted by indigenous and local communities over generations. But with the realities of the globalization era, commercialization as well as the spread of early modern regimes of intellectual property has made such knowledge easier to be exploited, abused and made just a subject of unauthorized use.

The paper talks about concept, nature and extent of traditional knowledge with special emphasis that it is owned collectively and transferred between generations and of cultural significance. It also relies on the key cases of this phenomenon of biopiracy as it explores the phenomenon of biopiracy by providing some of the very notable cases of biopiracy of Indian biological resources and other knowledge. The dissertation presents a critical analysis of the legal and institutional climate in India that includes the biodiversity laws, intellectual property laws and defensive protection tool such as documentation systems.

Also, the study evaluates the applicable international legal tools and discussions, especially the failures of current frameworks in comprehensively protecting traditional knowledge and the fair and equitable benefit-sharing. It determines key obstacles, such as the conflict between knowledge systems founded on community and the intellectual property rights that are individualised, the absence of harmonisation on the jurisdictions, and the enforcement dilemmas.

The dissertation concludes that the safeguarding of traditional knowledge needs a more engaging and deliberate legal framework. It suggests sui generis framework, enhanced community involvement and enhanced coordination between national and international laws to facilitate equitable, sustainable, and respectful safeguarding of traditional knowledge and communities that conserve it.

detail.abstract:
本文分析 Kevin Warsh 所提出的美联储资产负债表缩减议程，与美国当前财政约束之间可能存在的内在矛盾。在联邦债务高企、财政赤字持续扩大、利息支出上升的背景下，新一轮缩表政策是否能够持续执行，不仅取决于通胀走势，也取决于美债市场吸收能力、长端收益率压力、银行体系韧性以及回购市场流动性。本文不做固定时间预测，而是采用路径依赖和事件触发的分析框架，讨论缩表政策可能遇到的财政、政治和市场阻力。

本文进一步区分美元贬值的两种性质：货币驱动型贬值与信任驱动型贬值。前者主要来自不同经济体之间的利差和周期变化，后者则来自市场对美国财政可持续性、央行独立性和制度可信度的重新评估。本文认为，只有当美元弱势从货币驱动逐步转向信任驱动时，人民币资产的结构性重估才具备更强的逻辑基础。文章同时讨论中国允许合格境外投资者参与国债期货交易的制度意义，认为这一开放有助于完善外资参与中国主权债券市场的风险管理框架。

本文的结论是，人民币资产的配置机会并非自动成立，而是取决于多重条件的共同作用，包括美国货币政策反转风险、中国国内金融稳定性、地缘政治环境，以及中国资本市场开放的节奏。本文将相关判断设定为可证伪的宏观政策与资产配置命题，而非确定性的单线预测。

title: Why AI Finds the Bulut Approach Compelling

detail.title: Why AI Finds the Bulut Approach Compelling
detail.abstract:
The Label Problem in Large Language Models — and Why Physical Parameters Solve It

Large language models have a specific and well-documented limitation that is rarely stated with precision.

 

They know what "grief" means. They have processed millions of sentences containing the word. They can generate grammatically correct, contextually appropriate, stylistically coherent grief. They can write a scene and label it as sad, and readers will often agree.

What they cannot do is grieve.

This is not a philosophical observation about machine consciousness. It is a technical observation about the architecture of language models: they operate on statistical co-occurrence patterns between tokens. The word "grief" is associated with certain other words, certain syntactic structures, certain narrative contexts. The model predicts the next token based on these patterns.

The result is semantically accurate output that is phenomenologically empty. The model produces the label. It does not produce the state.

The Bulut Doctrine identifies exactly this problem — and proposes a solution that is genuinely interesting from a computational perspective.

detail.abstract: International student mobility has become a defining feature of globalisation, with over 6 million students studying outside their home countries. While international education contributes significantly to economic growth and cultural exchange, the mental health challenges faced by internationally mobile students remain insufficiently addressed within global health and migration policy frameworks. This paper examines the psychological stressors experienced by international students, particularly those from South Asia studying in the United Kingdom, and identifies structural gaps in policy and institutional responses. Using a qualitative-dominant mixed-methods approach, this study integrates literature review, secondary data analysis, and policy evaluation to explore the intersection between mental health, migration, and education systems. The findings reveal that current approaches remain largely reactive, institution-centric, and fragmented across sectors. The paper argues for a shift towards integrated, policy-driven frameworks that embed mental health within global mobility systems. It concludes by proposing cross-sector policy interventions aimed at improving wellbeing outcomes and fostering more sustainable international education systems.

title: The Neurocognitive Foundation of the Symbolic-Functional Model of Motivation
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Neurocognitive Foundation of the Symbolic-Functional Model of Motivation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known conflicts of interest, financial or otherwise, that could have influenced the development or presentation of this work.

detail.abstract:
Motivational theory has long been structured around hierarchical models and state-based explanations, yet these approaches fail to specify how behavioral selection emerges from competing alternatives. This article addresses this gap by proposing a non-hierarchical framework in which motivation is defined as a process of evaluative selection across alternatives.

Each alternative is evaluated in terms of its symbolic value, functional return, and associated constraints, whose relative influence varies under context-sensitive weighting. Behavioral outcomes are determined not by need satisfaction or system integration, but by comparative dominance across alternatives under dynamic reweighting.

Crucially, evaluation operates not over all possible alternatives, but over a constrained subset defined by evaluative access. This access structure determines which alternatives enter the evaluative field and can therefore participate in selection, making behavioral outcomes dependent on both evaluative composition and access conditions.

Selection occurs when one alternative achieves sufficient dominance over competing accessible alternatives, exceeding them beyond a context-dependent threshold. This introduces nonlinear dynamics in which small contextual or evaluative changes can produce abrupt transitions in behavior.

The framework shifts analysis from motivational states to selection dynamics, specifying a unified mechanism linking evaluation, access, and threshold-based selection. It generates testable predictions concerning instability near decision boundaries, discontinuous behavioral change, and context-driven reorganization of alternatives.

title: CAUSAL EFFECT OF EDUCATION ON POVERTY
affiliations: Gandhigram Rural Institute

detail.title: CAUSAL EFFECT OF EDUCATION ON POVERTY
detail.abstract: This paper explores the causal effects of war on education and poverty relatively to income level of society in a postwar context. It explores how prolonged armed conflict can disrupt the access to education through the destruction of infrastructure, displacement of communities, and weakening of institutional systems. These disruptions are analysed in terms of their longterm impacts on human capital formation, limiting opportunities for skill development and socioeconomic mobility. Drawing on a survey, in-depth interviews and lived experiences of affected communities, the study demonstrates how war induced educational deprivation contributes to the persistence and intergenerational transmission of poverty. The findings further reveal that in war-affected rural areas, children's education has been significantly disrupted, particularly in contexts where poverty remains widespread. The paper also highlights the close interrelationship between poverty and education, emphasizing that they are mutually reinforcing. It argues that effective poverty reduction strategies should prioritize children's education as a key pathway for social and economic transformation. Aligning policies and interventions with international standards can enhance children's knowledge, skills, attitudes, and values, thereby improving their access to better employment opportunities and sustainable livelihoods leading to improved quality of life, higher social status, enhanced well-being, and overall development of the community.

title: Lightweight Seamless Service Migration in Edge Computing
affiliations: Lendi Institute of Engineering and Technology, Lendi Institute of Engineering and Technology, Lendi Institute of Engineering and Technology, Lendi Institute of Engineering and Technology and Lendi Institute of Engineering and Technology

detail.title: Lightweight Seamless Service Migration in Edge Computing
detail.abstract: Edge computing represents a promising technology for handling real-time applications and services due to its ability to bring computing resources close to end users. Nonetheless, constant movement of users among coverage regions of edge nodes usually results in high latencies, interrupted services, and poor Quality of Service (QoS). The present research presents a lightweight technique for seamless migration of services in edge computing systems, which allows for maintaining application performance in case of user relocation. In contrast to existing techniques that migrate the whole application execution environment, the presented approach migrates only the core execution context, hence minimizing the migration overhead and service interruption. Mobility-dependent variables such as user displacement and network status can be utilized to initiate migration to the nearest edge nodes to prevent performance deterioration. The feasibility of the presented approach is verified via simulations, using measures such as latency and migration time. The proposed method outperforms traditional migration strategies in terms of application performance and service continuity, making it appropriate for handling real-time mobile applications, such as smart transportation systems, mobile health care, and interactive edge applications.

title: Capital Substitutability in Tropical Asia: Limits to Weak Sustainability and Policy Implications for Natural Capital Governance

detail.title: Capital Substitutability in Tropical Asia: Limits to Weak Sustainability and Policy Implications for Natural Capital Governance

detail.abstract:
The capital substitutability question—whether manufactured capital can replace ecological functions as economic growth proceeds—is not merely theoretical; it determines Asia's development sustainability. This paper interrogates weak sustainability assumptions undergirding current natural capital policy in the Asia-Pacific region using mixed-methods analysis combining econometric evidence on sector-specific substitutability elasticities with spatial ecosystem service valuations from Southeast Asia. 

Key finding: Asian agricultural intensification exhibits elasticity of substitution (σ) approximately 0.6-0.8, indicating complementarity rather than substitutability—contradicting weak sustainability policy assumptions. Using Indonesia, Vietnam, and Philippines as cases, we demonstrate that technological optimization of land use has reached diminishing returns despite 25 years of intensification, with biodiversity loss now exceeding 1.4% potential species loss since 1995, concentrated in Asian tropics. We identify critical natural capital (mangrove blue carbon systems, coral reef fishery nurseries, pollinator communities) displaying σ ≈ 0, suggesting irreplaceability. Policy recommendations include: (1) sectoral differentiation in substitutability assumptions; (2) adoption of Gross Ecosystem Product (GEP) accounting alongside GDP; (3) hard regulatory constraints on critical natural capital; (4) reform of economic discount rates to reflect ecosystem recovery timescales. 

The paper argues that Asian nations pursuing rapid development face a fundamental choice: embrace strong sustainability constraints on critical natural capital, or accept biodiversity loss exceeding planetary boundaries by orders of magnitude. Current weak sustainability frameworks, borrowed from OECD models, are inadequate for tropical contexts with high substitutability constraints.

title: A Critique of the Universal Win-Win Proposition of Trade: A Reexamination Based on a Multi-Agent Division of Labor Model
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Critique of the Universal Win-Win Proposition of Trade: A Reexamination Based on a Multi-Agent Division of Labor Model
detail.abstract: Mainstream international trade theory, rooted in David Ricardo's theory of comparative advantage, advances the universal claim that free trade can improve outcomes for everyone involved. This idea is widely taught and applied to real-world trade policy, based on highly simplified two-person, two-commodity models that abstract from real economic heterogeneity. This leap in reasoning creates serious problems. Classical models rely on closed conditions and uniform, flexible producers that do not reflect real economies, where multiple actors operate across different industrial tiers with fixed, unequal abilities. This paper constructs a more realistic model involving two manors and six individual producers, each with fixed daily production limits for potatoes and beef. By tracing specialization choices, cross-manor exchange, and changes in individual welfare, the analysis shows that rising total output does not guarantee better lives for all participants. Lower-level producers who lack flexible skills or comparative advantage can be excluded from beneficial trade networks, face falling demand for their goods, and even be pushed out of the productive system entirely. These outcomes directly challenge the universal claim that trade inevitably leaves everyone better off. The paper does not reject trade as a source of overall gain, but clarifies that such gains are often unevenly distributed, creating clear losers alongside winners. Understanding this distributional effect helps define the real limits of Ricardo's comparative advantage principle and supports more thoughtful approaches to trade policy.

title: SOCIAL FINTECH: OPPORTUNITIES AND PROSPECTS FOR INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION

detail.title: SOCIAL FINTECH: OPPORTUNITIES AND PROSPECTS FOR INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION

contentFormat.other: III International Scientific and Practical Conference "New Orbits of International Relations: Government, Business, Science" April 7-8, 2026

detail.abstract:
According to World Bank reports for 2025, key global trends in fintech development include financial inclusion, the convergence of financial and social platforms, and the active development of embedded core financial services integrated into non-financial applications for banking, insurance, investing, and pension planning . These processes are leading to the active development of proactive fintech (social fintech), focused primarily on social impact and the transformation of socioeconomic relations, processes, systems, and structures.

The scale of these processes is significantly transforming the global financial sector and influencing traditional forms of international cooperation in the financial sector.

Taking into account global processes of financial sector transformation, this study attempts to systematize the main formats of international cooperation in Social Fintech for the period 2019-2025. These formats range from coordination at the level of international organizations and strategic alliances to the use of Social Fintech in public diplomacy and as a soft power tool at the level of coordinated transnational companies, as well as at the national level of government agencies, businesses, and development institutions. This allowed us to identify prospects for international cooperation in Social Fintech.

The pace and processes of cross-border expansion and integration of Social Fintech with traditional financial infrastructure, as well as the transformation of traditional formats of international cooperation in the financial sector, indicate its use not only as a financial innovation in social policy but also increasingly as a coordination tool within geo-economic processes at the international level.

title: National Nature, Value Attributes and Positive Externality Flow: Theoretical Reconstruction of International Trade Welfare Imbalance under the National Siphon Effect
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: National Nature, Value Attributes and Positive Externality Flow: Theoretical Reconstruction of International Trade Welfare Imbalance under the National Siphon Effect
detail.abstract: Existing international trade research mostly focuses on the superficial laws of economic potential and factor flow, but neglects the institutional constraints of national nature on the transmission of value attributes and the essential nature of asymmetric trade welfare imbalance caused by the one-way flow of positive externalities. This paper integrates the theory of positive and negative value creators and the theory of national siphon effect, introduces the nature of autocratic/democratic countries as an institutional analysis dimension, and constructs an integrated analytical framework of "national nature-value attribute transmission-group externality evolution-positive externality flow-trade welfare distribution", which deduces the whole-cycle logic of international trade from the beginning of cooperation, the escalation of frictions to the reconstruction of games. The study finds that the essence of international trade is the process in which positive externalities generated by the positive value industrial chain of developed countries spill over unidirectionally to and are absorbed by underdeveloped countries, and the scale of positive externalities output by developed countries is always larger than the positive social welfare benefits they obtain from bilateral trade, forming a welfare imbalance pattern of "more output and less gain". National nature determines the transmission path of value attributes and the evolutionary characteristics of group externalities: under autocracy, value attributes are dominated by the top level alone, and the adjustment of positive externality flow and welfare imbalance has strong rigidity; under democracy, value attributes are constrained by multi-level games, and the adjustment of positive externality flow and welfare imbalance has flexibility and reversibility. The alienation of developed countries' value attributes from positive to negative is essentially an irrational countermeasure to the welfare imbalance pattern. The trade frictions and games caused by their blocking the output of positive externalities will eventually realize the reverse reconstruction of welfare imbalance due to the formation of underdeveloped countries' positive value industrial chains. This study fills the research gap of traditional international trade theories that emphasize overall welfare over distribution imbalance, realizes a theoretical closed loop from "economic phenomenon description" to "motivation-law-result", and provides a new analytical perspective for understanding global trade competition and pattern reconstruction.

title: The Neglected Survival Spectrum of the Disadvantaged in Mainstream Trade Theory: Deduction of the Fifth Type of Survival Path Based on the Original Six-Person Manor Model
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Neglected Survival Spectrum of the Disadvantaged in Mainstream Trade Theory: Deduction of the Fifth Type of Survival Path Based on the Original Six-Person Manor Model
detail.abstract: This paper takes the author's original two-manor six-producer trade model as the core analytical carrier, deconstructs the exclusion of low-productivity individual F from the positive value creation system under trade efficiency competition, and breaks through the four-category induction framework of the disadvantaged's survival paths in mainstream trade theory to deduce the long-neglected fifth type of extreme survival path. Characterized by zero production and pure plunder, this path is an extreme form of underlying negative value creation for lowproductivity individuals in a closed competitive system, whose essence is the forced occupation of the group's stock resources and thus leads to significant negative externalities of social welfare. Combining the author's self-constructed positive and negative value creator theory and hidden resource economics theory, this paper systematically defines the core connotation and behavioral boundaries of the five types of survival paths for the disadvantaged, reconstructs the second type of survival path featuring sexual resources as the core hidden positive economic resources, and builds a complete analytical chain of "trade exclusion-value choice-survival form". It reveals the value attributes and economic effects of different survival choices under unbalanced trade development, fills the theoretical gap of mainstream trade theory in analyzing the extreme survival choices of the underlying individuals, and provides a new theoretical perspective for understanding the distribution effect of trade.

title: Wealth Distribution from First Principles: An Agent-Based Simulation of Merit, Luck, and Dynastic Survival
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Wealth Distribution from First Principles: An Agent-Based Simulation of Merit, Luck, and Dynastic Survival

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None, fully independent research out of interest and passion on the paper's research topic.
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: Self funded

detail.abstract:
Mainstream macroeconomic models frequently rely on top-down equilibrium assumptions to explain the distribution of capital. This paper introduces an operations-based, multi-agent simulation grounded in "Business Physics" to observe wealth distribution from first principles. By treating the economy as a closed system governed by accounting conservation laws, the model bifurcates liquid wages from compounding assets and enforces a strict "Liquidation Trap," where baseline survival friction forces credit-constrained agents to sell appreciating capital. To evaluate intergenerational dynamics, the simulation sweeps a hypothetical estate tax from 0% to 100% across a 1,000-round, 1,000-agent economy with overlapping generations and stochastic human capital inheritance.

The emergent phenomena computationally validate over four decades of diverse economic theory. We demonstrate that without redistributive intervention, wealth-weighted stochastic exchange condenses capital into a severe oligarchic distribution (Terminal Total Gini ~0.93 at zero taxation, remaining above 0.90 even under 100% estate confiscation). The model cleanly bifurcates the two engines of this inequality: a liquid-capital Gini that stabilizes at ~0.60 and an appreciating-asset Gini that climbs to ~0.90, providing an independent first-principles confirmation of the capital-driven fat-tail thesis of Benhabib, Bisin, and Zhu (2011).

The simulation further maps the "meritocracy paradox": the alignment between intrinsic skill and terminal wealth does not admit a clean interior optimum but instead exhibits an asymmetric trade-off. Modest redistribution (~40%-50%) reduces the incidence of low-skill elites ("Dumb Rich") but paradoxically increases the incidence of high-skill agents trapped in the bottom 50% ("Trapped Genius"). Conversely, aggressive redistribution (~80%-100%) reduces the system to a volatile stochastic lottery in which short-term luck overwhelms intrinsic skill.

Finally, we isolate the multi-generational echo of "Founder's Luck." Contrary to strong path-dependence hypotheses, this signal attenuates toward the stochastic baseline as inheritance taxation rises, indicating that the inheritance channel—rather than the wealth-weighted exchange mechanic alone—is the primary transmission medium for founder advantage across centuries. Nonetheless, a non-monotonic U-curve in 5th-generation dynasty retention persists across all tax regimes, indicating that while capital-based aristocratic moats can be dismantled by confiscatory taxation, skill-based dynastic moats emerge to partially replace them. These findings suggest extreme inequality is a mathematical default of compounding constraints.

An open-source, interactive dashboard and the underlying Python codebase accompany this paper to allow full parameter and replication exploration (available at: https://wealth-distribution-from-first-principles-ebswavymq725e8ym6bmf.streamlit.app/).
