detail.abstract: In recent years, many developed ports have implemented modifications to their bunkering procedures and, instead of supplying marine fuels that release high amounts of emissions during vessel combustion, now provide electricity through a shore-based connection known as Cold Ironing (CI) or On-Shore Power Supply (OPS). To that end, several regulations and constraints must be defined to ensure the effective operation of the OPS system. One of these regulations concerns the pricing and tariff structure for vessels using the OPS service while at berth. The OPS price determines the distribution of profit between the vessels and the port. Therefore, this paper evaluates several tariff schemes for the OPS system and applies a Nash bargaining game model to determine the service tariff that maximizes the benefits for both parties.

title: Deep Neural Network Approach for Face Detection and Facial Region Segmentation
affiliations: , Bharath Institute of Higher Education and Research, Chennai and Bharath Institute of Higher Education and Research, Chennai

detail.title: Deep Neural Network Approach for Face Detection and Facial Region Segmentation
detail.abstract: Face detection and segmentation of facial regions are vital components in the field of computer vision, playing a significant role in applications such as facial expression recognition, biometric authentication, and human-computer interaction. Conventional image processing techniques frequently encounter challenges due to variations in lighting, facial angles, partial obstructions by objects, and intricate backgrounds. To address these challenges, this research presents a framework based on deep learning that employs a deep neural network to effectively detect faces and segment key facial regions. The approach begins with the identification of faces in input images through a convolutional feature extraction method, followed by pixellevel segmentation to pinpoint features such as the eyes, nose, mouth, and facial contours. The deep neural network is trained to recognize complex features from extensive datasets, resulting in enhanced detection accuracy and more precise segmentation when compared to traditional methods. To enhance the model's performance and flexibility, preprocessing techniques such as normalization and data augmentation are implemented. The results of the experiments indicate that the system significantly improves both accuracy and efficiency in detecting faces and segmenting facial regions across various environments. This methodology can be effectively applied in fields such as security systems, emotion analysis, medical imaging, and intelligent surveillance.

title: Economic Methods for Balancing Capital and Operational Costs in Power System Capacity Expansion Modeling
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Colorado at Boulder and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Economic Methods for Balancing Capital and Operational Costs in Power System Capacity Expansion Modeling
detail.abstract: Capacity expansion modeling (CEM) for power systems provides vital information to system planners and grid market investors. The recent large-scale additions of renewable resources and energy storage systems into bulk-electric grids complicate long-term planning models due to their negligible marginal costs. The weight applied to operational costs in a CEM changes the model’s capacity investments. Four approaches with varying simulation horizons and weighting of operational costs are compared. The proposed Iterative approach represents minimum future visibility with single-year simulation horizons, while the Cumulative approach represents low decision frequency with a single 50-year simulation. The proposed Net Present Value (NPV) and Levelized Plant Lifetime (LPL) approaches combine visibility with high decision frequency. The LPL approach best matches actual investment in ERCOT for the 2015-2025 window, outperforming the other approaches in regards to total system capacity. An introduced fixed-point theorem is observed across approaches and initial conditions that suggests self-deterministic solution sets. This phenomenon, here called fixed-point expansion, regards capacity factors and percentage of total capacity per generation type in CEMs reaching steady-state equilibrium over time.

title: Reliability Cascades in Multi-Agent Organizational Systems: Attention Reallocation, Cascade Compounding, and Decomposability Collapse in an AI-Native Operational Environment

detail.title: Reliability Cascades in Multi-Agent Organizational Systems: Attention Reallocation, Cascade Compounding, and Decomposability Collapse in an AI-Native Operational Environment

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder and operator of BizBuilder Inc., the system described in this paper. The empirical observations are drawn from the author's direct experience operating the system.

detail.abstract: When AI agents execute coordinated work in multi-step pipelines, three phenomena emerge that existing frameworks address separately but that belong together: reliability cascades where per-step failures compound multiplicatively and correlate through shared context, operator attention reallocation from strategic to reactive modes as cascade severity increases, and decomposability collapse where coordination coupling exceeds the threshold at which modular independence holds. This paper develops an integrated theoretical framework connecting these phenomena as facets of a single closed-loop control system under stress. The empirical substrate is BizBuilder, an AI-native cybernetic feedback system whose five telemetry streams capture these phenomena at the interaction level without separate research instrumentation. I present five testable propositions and the measurement architecture that enables their testing. The paper contributes a unified lens for reliability dynamics in human-agent coordination and a replicable instrument design for studying them.

title: Designing Equitable Dynamic Electricity Tariffs: A Multi-Stage Machine Learning Approach
affiliations: Universiti Putra Malaysia, University Putra Malaysia, Universiti Putra Malaysia, Universiti Putra Malaysia, Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Designing Equitable Dynamic Electricity Tariffs: A Multi-Stage Machine Learning Approach
detail.abstract: Dynamic electricity tariff programmes are critical for effective demand-side management, yet existing analytical approaches typically address consumer segmentation, load forecasting, and tariff design in isolation. This paper addresses this fragmentation by presenting a comprehensive five-stage machine learning pipeline. The methodology integrates dual-stage Rough Set Theory (RST) for feature selection alongside an Adaptive Rough K-Means (ARKM) clustering algorithm featuring a novel boundary region metric to handle consumer assignment ambiguity. This is followed by a hybrid deep learning forecasting architecture fusing Deep Belief Networks, BiLSTM, and a Transformer encoder. Finally, a three-objective NSGA-II evolutionary algorithm optimises tariffs to concurrently minimise consumer cost, peak-to-average ratio, and fairness variance. The framework was rigorously evaluated against twenty established baseline models across five highly diverse international smart meter datasets. Results demonstrate that the dual-RST approach reduced feature dimensionality by up to 64.3 percent without information loss. Furthermore, the hybrid forecasting architecture ranked first globally among all twenty-one considered pipelines (Friedman test p < 0.001). Crucially, the multi-objective tariff optimisation achieved up to 80.3 percent mean consumer cost savings, which is more than double the best-performing baseline, while maintaining a perfectly equitable Jain's Fairness Index of 1.000 on specific datasets and satisfying strict utility revenue neutrality constraints. By achieving a vastly superior composite end-to-end score, this framework provides electrical utilities with an interpretable and deployable pathway from raw smart meter data to personalised dynamic tariffs.

title: dQ/dV-Based Quality Screening Methodology for Fresh 18650 Cell Manufacturing Assessment
affiliations: University of Twente, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Twente - bFaculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Sciences, Slovak University of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: dQ/dV-Based Quality Screening Methodology for Fresh 18650 Cell Manufacturing Assessment
detail.abstract: Differential capacity (dQ/dV) analysis has emerged as a powerful diagnostic tool for lithium-ion battery characterization, yet large-scale statistical studies on fresh commercial cells remain limited. This work presents a comprehensive dQ/dV analysis of 134 fresh Molicel P45B 18650 cells to establish baseline electrochemical signatures and quantify manufacturing variability. Systematic peak characterization reveals that voltage positions are highly consistent across the batch, reflecting uniform material composition, while peak intensities exhibit moderate variability attributable to manufacturing-related differences in active material loading. Principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering identify two natural cell subpopulations with distinct electrochemical activity levels, motivating a three-tier grading framework for quality-based cell classification. Strong charge--discharge correlations in peak intensities indicate co-variation within the cell population, and minimal voltage hysteresis suggests low polarization resistance across the batch. This baseline characterization supports cluster-informed cell sorting for battery pack assembly and provides a reference dataset for future degradation studies, demonstrating that dQ/dV analysis can serve as a rapid, non-destructive screening method for commercial cell quality assessment.

title: How Shareholders Argue: Three Decades of Proposal Narratives

detail.title: How Shareholders Argue: Three Decades of Proposal Narratives
detail.abstract: Shareholder proposals are a key channel of shareholder voice, yet their legitimacy is under review at the SEC. To evaluate this channel, I build the first full-text corpus of shareholder proposals from DEF 14A filings (1994–2025) and SEC no-action letters (2008–2025). I use large language models to decompose each proposal’s argumentative structure into causal chains and document four stylized facts. First, narratives are substantively heterogeneous and predict both SEC no-action decisions and shareholder vote support out of sample. Second, proposal narratives differentiate between shareholder-oriented and stakeholder-oriented proponents, and board responses diverge along the same axis. Third, narratives shift substantially across decades—proponents increasingly target stakeholder-oriented problems and ground their arguments in external evidence, while boards more frequently deflect problems and dismiss remedies as redundant. Fourth, almost half of stakeholder-problem proposals are argued in shareholder-value terms, while shareholder-problem proposals are rarely argued in stakeholder-value terms. This asymmetry grows over time and is not an artifact of SEC screening. Exploiting cross-firm variation in media coverage of adverse ESG events, together with the June 2017 formation of the US Climate Alliance as a natural experiment, I provide evidence that this asymmetry responds to the internalization of externalities.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether the Worsening Probability (WP) scores generated by a Relational Risk-based machine learning model (v5.7.0) statistically and significantly predict TYPE_A (financial deterioration) trading suspensions among 2,793 KOSPI/KOSDAQ-listed companies. The model, an ensemble of XGBoost and LightGBM utilizing 48 relational risk features, achieved a 5-fold cross-validation AUC of 0.8830 (95% CI [0.8674, 0.8986]). In the In-Time analysis, 56.17% of companies rated CRITICAL (WP≥0.70) experienced TYPE_A trading suspensions, yielding an Odds Ratio of 113.72 (95% CI [70.01, 184.72], p < 0.001) compared to the LOW-rated group (1.11%). The WP distributions were nearly completely separated (KS D = 0.9065, CLES = 99.1%), achieving 82.6% recall and 97.9% negative predictive value at WP >= 0.50. In the Out-of-Time validation, the model predicted suspensions over 24 months with OOT AUC of 0.8280, and AUC of 0.9291 for 12-month predictions. Based on 6 In-Time and 9 OOT statistical tests, WP is confirmed as a statistically significant predictor. This study demonstrates that relational risk constitutes a valid novel feature domain for corporate financial distress prediction and establishes practical utility as an early warning system for financial regulators and institutional investors.

title: Mija, Yes You Can? Understanding Debt Financing Discrimination in Latina Entrepreneurs
affiliations: Missouri University of Science and Technology, University of Texas at Arlington and Sam Houston State University

detail.title: Mija, Yes You Can? Understanding Debt Financing Discrimination in Latina Entrepreneurs
detail.abstract: Latina entrepreneurs are a rapidly growing segment of U.S. business owners, yet they remain disproportionately constrained by debt financing barriers. We theorize that debt financing outcomes for Latina entrepreneurs reflect a role congruity problem in which creditors evaluate loan requests through gendered and racialized role expectations that foreground competence. Drawing on role congruity theory, we argue that (a) Latina entrepreneurs are evaluated as less competent than non-Latina entrepreneurs, (b) competence perceptions partially mediate ethnicity effects on loan approval, and (c) offering an identity-congruent, ethnic product may attenuate disadvantage by aligning entrepreneur identity with perceived market opportunity. We test these ideas in a 2 × 2 between-subject experiment with 136 U.S.-based financial services professionals. Results indicate that Latina entrepreneurs receive significantly lower loan approval likelihood, that competence partially mediates this effect, and that ethnic product offerings confer a within-group approval benefit for Latinas. Notably, ethnic products do not attenuate the competence-based penalty. We contribute a micro-mechanistic account of debt discrimination that integrates intersectional identity with product categorization, extending role congruity theory by demonstrating that identity-category alignment elevates perceived opportunity fit even when competence penalties persist.

title: Expatriate Knowledge Transfer as a Dynamic Capability: Evidence from Zimbabwe’s Oil and Gas Sector
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Expatriate Knowledge Transfer as a Dynamic Capability: Evidence from Zimbabwe’s Oil and Gas Sector
detail.abstract: This study investigates how expatriate knowledge transfer systems (EKTS) shape local technical skills (CALT) and firm performance (FIPE) in Zimbabwe’s oil and gas sector. Anchored in a pragmatic philosophy and an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, the research integrates quantitative modelling of 315 survey responses with qualitative insights from 11 semi-structured interviews. Structural equation modelling confirms that EKTS exert significant positive effects on CALT and FIPE, with absorptive capacity mediating the EKTS → CALT pathway and contextual relevance together with environmental enablers moderating system effectiveness. Grounded theory analysis enriches these findings, revealing that mentorship depth, trust, reciprocity, and culturally attuned learning narratives are decisive in transforming expatriate expertise into indigenous capability.The originality of this work lies in reframing expatriate knowledge transfer as a dynamic capability and contributing the validated Skills Adaptation and Knowledge Integration Model (SAKIM), which synthesises Dynamic Capabilities, Knowledge Transfer Theory, and Absorptive Capacity into a feedback-driven architecture. By advancing theory beyond RBV’s static logic to the adaptive logic of Dynamic Capabilities, the study enriches international business scholarship and provides firms and policymakers in resource-constrained economies with a diagnostic-prescriptive tool for reducing expatriate dependence and accelerating indigenous capability development. In doing so, Zimbabwe’s case is elevated from national context to global exemplar, setting a new agenda for international business scholarship where in transitional economies, competitiveness must be redefined as cyclical, adaptive, and contextually aligned knowledge systems.

title: Innovation Capabilities and Firm Performance: An Ambidextrous Approach to Internationalization in Emerging Markets
affiliations: Universidad Autonoma de Chihuahua, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Tecnológico de Monterrey

detail.title: Innovation Capabilities and Firm Performance: An Ambidextrous Approach to Internationalization in Emerging Markets
detail.abstract: This study examines how exploration and exploitation strategies influence multinational enterprise subsidiary performance in emerging markets with varying geographical and institutional distances. Drawing on ambidexterity and contingency theories, we apply partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and necessary condition analysis to 156 Spanish subsidiaries in Morocco (high distance) and Mexico (low distance). Findings indicate both strategies are necessary, but subsidiary performance improves most under a combined (not balanced) ambidexterity approach, regardless of contextual distances—challenging assumptions of strategic parity. By advocating alignment between parent firms’ strategies and subsidiaries’ local adaptation, we position subsidiaries as vital sources of competitive competence. The study advances ambidexterity literature by proposing a shift from sufficiency to necessity logic in analysis, offering insights for international business strategy.

title: Security or Development? A Budgetary Dilemma in the Context of the 2024 Elections and International Pressure

detail.title: Security or Development? A Budgetary Dilemma in the Context of the 2024 Elections and International Pressure
detail.abstract: This study provides an in-depth examination of Mali's 2024 budget in a context marked by acute security pressures and pressing development needs. It evaluates the extent to which the budget rationalizes public expenditure and balances security outlays against investments in socioeconomic development. Covering 2019-2024, the study combines quantitative and qualitative methods, including linear regressions and interviews with 24 military officers. The analysis shows a marked increase in defense and security spending without a commensurate improvement in security indicators. A moderate, but statistically insignificant, relationship is observed between security expenditure and conflict-related mortality. Interviews nevertheless reveal a widespread perception that higher security spending remains necessary, despite uncertainty regarding its long-term effectiveness. The article argues that a more balanced budgetary strategy-one that integrates security expenditure with robust investment in socioeconomic development-is essential to sustaining growth and stability in Mali.

title: Towards Efficient Online 3D Volume Rendering: A Scenario Optimization Model
affiliations: American University of Science and Technology, American University of Science and Technology, American University of Science and Technology and American University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Towards Efficient Online 3D Volume Rendering: A Scenario Optimization Model
detail.abstract: The proliferation of web-based interactive 3D applications has intensified the challenge of delivering high-quality volume rendering across heterogeneous client devices with varying hardware capabilities, network bandwidth, and browser support. This work presents an adaptive web-based framework that dynamically selects optimal rendering techniques to address these constraints in real time. The core contribution is a scenario optimization model formulated as a Constraint Satisfaction Problem (CSP), which evaluates three binary client parameters, Internet bandwidth (BW), hardware capability (HW), and WebGL browser support (WB), to choose among four rendering strategies: Server-side OpenGL, WebGL, Marching Cubes (MC), and Signed Distance Fields (SDF). A deterministic automaton governs transitions between rendering modes as client conditions change. The framework employs a client-server architecture with a profiling engine that detects device specifications and network conditions, feeding data into a CSP solver to instantiate the optimal rendering scenario. Experimental validation across multiple machines (M1–M4) and bandwidth levels (0.5–14 MB) demonstrates that rendering performance is significantly influenced by hardware specifications (accounting for 45% of performance variation, R² = 0.95), while bandwidth exhibits a more variable impact. The model successfully selects appropriate rendering strategies, SDF for high-GPU devices, WebGL for mid-range systems, and MC for low-end hardware, achieving robust performance where static, one-size-fits-all approaches fail. Compared to hardware-accelerated ray tracing methods (e.g., RTX-based), our approach provides a flexible, hardware-agnostic alternative suitable for diverse deployment environments. Limitations include binary parameter thresholds; future work will incorporate continuous capability metrics and machine learning for proactive adaptation.

title: HeBA: Heterogeneous Bottleneck Adapters for Robust Vision-Language Models
affiliations: Bangladesh University

detail.title: HeBA: Heterogeneous Bottleneck Adapters for Robust Vision-Language Models

detail.abstract: Adapting large-scale Vision-Language Models (VLMs) like CLIP to downstream tasks often suffers from a "one-size-fits-all" architectural approach, where visual and textual tokens are processed uniformly by wide, generic adapters. We argue that this homogeneity ignores the distinct structural nature of the modalities-spatial locality in images versus semantic density in text. To address this, we propose HeBA (Heterogeneous Bottleneck Adapter), a unified architectural framework that introduces modality-specific structural inductive biases. HeBA departs from conventional designs through three key architectural innovations: (1) Heterogeneity: It processes visual tokens via 2D depthwise-separable convolutions to preserve spatial correlations, while distinctively processing text tokens via dense linear projections to capture semantic relationships; (2) Bottleneck Regularization: Unlike standard expanding adapters, HeBA employs a compression bottleneck (D → D/4) that forces the model to learn compact, robust features; and (3) Forced Kaiming Initialization: We eliminate the restrictive zero-initialization paradigm, utilizing a "hot start" strategy that accelerates convergence. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HeBA's architecturally specialized design achieves superior stability and accuracy, establishing a new state-of-the-art on 11 few-shot benchmarks.

title: Price Cap vs. Per-Unit Subsidies: Selection, Pricing, and Cross Subsidization

detail.abstract: We evaluate subsidy mechanisms in the FCC's Rural Health Care program using administrative data covering the full population of participants. The original price-cap mechanism removes cost-containment incentives for health care providers. An ad valorem mechanism introduced in 2014 addresses this flaw by making providers bear 35% of costs. However, allowing consortium applications creates a new distortion: cross-subsidization from eligible to ineligible members. We develop theoretical models predicting these effects and estimate treatment effects using an extension of the two-way fixed effects framework with continuous treatments. We find that the ad valorem mechanism substantially reduces program spending relative to the price cap, while the consortium option significantly inflates it. Enforcement records and an inverted U-shaped relationship between cross-subsidization intensity and ineligible member share corroborate the findings.

title: When Missing Data Matters: Imputation, TOPSIS, and the Misrepresentation of Morocco’s Education System
affiliations: Ibn Tofail University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: When Missing Data Matters: Imputation, TOPSIS, and the Misrepresentation of Morocco’s Education System
detail.abstract: Annual reports, such as the Global Education Index Report (GEIR~2024), depict Morocco’s education system as underperforming globally. Such a situation results in large-scale reforms that require many financial resources. However, these rankings rely on opaque data-processing pipelines and unknown imputation of missing data. This study reconstructs the GEIR~2024 for more than 168 countries from nine World Bank indicators, quantifies the imputation of missing data, and evaluates three imputation strategies (zero-filling, marginal means, and local linear interpolation). Using RMSE and MAE as accuracy metrics, local linear interpolation clearly outperforms the alternatives (overall RMSE = 2.40, MAE = 1.25). Then, we apply a TOPSIS-based multicriteria decision framework to rank countries. The results show that Morocco evolves from a bottom-tier position in the early 2000s towards a stable middle group by 2023, following an accelerating upward pattern. All materials required for reproducibility, including code and data, are provided at: https://github.com/mouddentarik/Education_Ranking

title: Multi-Objective Adaptive Energy Management Strategy with Dynamic Reference Regulation and Driving Pattern Recognition for Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicles
affiliations: Shanghai University of Electric Power, Shanghai University of Electric Power, Shanghai University of Electric Power, Shanghai University of Electric Power, Shanghai University of Electric Power and Shanghai University of Electric Power

detail.title: Multi-Objective Adaptive Energy Management Strategy with Dynamic Reference Regulation and Driving Pattern Recognition for Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicles
detail.abstract: To achieve the coordinated optimization of hydrogen consumption, fuel cell durability, battery state-of-charge (SOC) maintenance, and economic operation in fuel cell hybrid electric vehicles (FCHEVs), this paper proposes a multi-objective adaptive energy management strategy (EMS). Aiming to mitigate exploration stagnation and suboptimal policy oscillations in traditional DRL-based strategies, a dynamic SOC reference regulation mechanism, grounded in expert heuristics, is embedded within the actor-critic learning architecture to facilitate coordinated multi-objective optimization. To further enhance environmental adaptability and overcome the performance rigidity of single-strategy systems, a learning vector quantization neural network (LVQ-NN) is developed to realize real-time driving pattern recognition. Based on the identified urban, suburban, and highway conditions, the proposed strategy adaptively adjusts the dynamic SOC reference regulation mechanism, significantly improving the robustness and generalization ability of the EMS. The proposed method accelerates training convergence, suppresses unreasonable power fluctuations, and realizes the coordinated optimization of hydrogen economy, fuel cell durability, and battery SOC maintenance. Comparative results under typical mixed driving cycles demonstrate that, compared with the benchmark multi-objective energy management strategy, the proposed adaptive EMS reduces the total operational cost by 4.58% while maintaining superior adaptability under various driving scenarios.

title: Mechanisms of Inequality: A Mathematical Architecture for Structural Containment

detail.title: Mechanisms of Inequality: A Mathematical Architecture for Structural Containment
detail.abstract: This paper argues that persistent economic inequality arises from the mathematical structure of capital accumulation—multiplicative returns, power-law distributions, and cross-domain compounding advantages—rather than from institutional failure alone, implying that conventional policy tools cannot fundamentally alter its trajectory. It proposes a Purpose-Bounded Currency System (PBCS) that replaces a unified currency with domain-specific exchange units, thereby severing cross-domain capital mobility, the primary transmission mechanism of inequality, and embedding constitutional constraints such as subsistence floors and bounded luxury accumulation directly into the system’s architecture. The analysis demonstrates that this design imposes a strict upper bound on inequality, eliminates power-law concentration, and preserves incentive compatibility within a controlled domain, suggesting that durable inequality containment requires architectural redesign rather than incremental institutional reform.

title: Specialist Asymmetry, Forecast Errors, and the Fama-Shiller Bridge
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Specialist Asymmetry, Forecast Errors, and the Fama-Shiller Bridge
detail.abstract: We study a multi-asset economy with M independent sources of fundamental uncertainty and N specialists, each observing one source perfectly and holding biased priors about the rest. Specialists choose which asset to monitor via a Quantal Response Equilibrium (QRE), allocating attention endogenously across assets. We solve the QRE in closed form: in the Nash limit, specialist counts are proportional to asset volatility; for finite response sensitivity, the allocation is a smoothed version of this rule. Given the QRE allocation, we solve the linear rational expectations equilibrium and derive four testable cross-sectional predictions: (i) assets with more specialists have higher R2 (price informativeness scales as n 2 j ); (ii) conditional forecast errors are smaller for heavily-monitored assets; (iii) post-publication decay of anomalies reflects specialist entry; (iv) trading volume is increasing in specialist count. Calibrating to M = 50 assets and N = 500 specialists, the model matches the empirical pattern that average R2 per asset is extremely small (≈ 10−6 ) and decreasing in the number of assets. We prove a dimensionality curse: when specialist density N/M is bounded, price variance diverges as M → ∞. Throughout all specifications, the price is unconditionally unbiased, Fama efficiency, while conditional forecast errors reflect the specialist ecology, Shiller predictability. The two are not competing hypotheses but two faces of lossy linear aggregation.

title: Embassies of Welfare: Transnational Public Service Delivery, Institutional Architecture, and the Reconfiguration of Fiscal Sovereignty

detail.title: Embassies of Welfare: Transnational Public Service Delivery, Institutional Architecture, and the Reconfiguration of Fiscal Sovereignty
detail.abstract: This paper proposes Embassies of Welfare (EoWs)—semi-sovereign public institutions through which advanced welfare states directly deliver services such as healthcare, education, and legal aid within host countries. It argues that existing cross-border welfare mechanisms—aid, multilateral programs, and humanitarian assistance—are structurally limited by indirect delivery and dependence on domestic capacity. By contrast, EoWs provide standing, direct service delivery under home-country quality standards while operating within a dual-accountability framework. A formal model shows conditions under which both welfare-exporting states and recipient populations are better off, while a broader institutional analysis situates EoWs within a purpose-oriented fiscal architecture. The framework implies a reconfiguration of fiscal sovereignty in which welfare provision becomes a globally mobile function rather than a territorially bounded one.

title: Mechanism Design for Countering Stagflation

detail.title: Mechanism Design for Countering Stagflation
detail.abstract: This paper reframes stagflation as a problem of inefficient input allocation under scarcity rather than a conventional aggregate demand–supply trade-off. When essential inputs such as energy are scarce and priced uniformly, decentralized market equilibria misallocate resources across heterogeneous firms, leading to excessive cost pass-through, inflation, and output contraction. To address this, the paper develops a mechanism design framework based on purpose-constrained, commodity-linked money (Commodity-PoC), which simultaneously modifies effective input prices and imposes allocation constraints. The analysis shows that uniform price-based policies cannot implement the efficient allocation, while the proposed mechanism can approximate the constrained-optimal allocation under realistic conditions. A general equilibrium model and quantitative simulations demonstrate that the mechanism reduces inflation, stabilizes output, and improves welfare relative to both decentralized equilibrium and conventional monetary and fiscal policies. These results imply that stagflation is not fundamentally a policy trade-off problem, but an implementation problem that can be resolved through appropriate allocation mechanisms.

title: From Fragility to Design: Eliminating Bank Run Equilibria through Purpose-Oriented Money

detail.title: From Fragility to Design: Eliminating Bank Run Equilibria through Purpose-Oriented Money
detail.abstract: This paper argues that financial fragility and bank runs arise from specific institutional features—fixed liquidity constraints, demandable deposits, and sequential service—that generate strategic complementarities and multiple equilibria. It proposes a purpose-oriented monetary architecture with endogenous liquidity, purpose-contingent claims, and no withdrawal priority, eliminating first-mover advantages and yielding a unique equilibrium without run dynamics. A formal model and general equilibrium analysis show that financial shocks no longer propagate through credit constraints, implying that instability can be eliminated through institutional design rather than ex post intervention.

title: WITHDRAWAL OF THE ALLIANCE OF SAHEL STATES (AES) FROM ECOWAS: A THEORETICAL ANALYSIS OF THE MACROECONOMIC CONSEQUENCES SSRN-ready English manuscript prepared from the published French article

detail.title: WITHDRAWAL OF THE ALLIANCE OF SAHEL STATES (AES) FROM ECOWAS: A THEORETICAL ANALYSIS OF THE MACROECONOMIC CONSEQUENCES SSRN-ready English manuscript prepared from the published French article
detail.abstract: This study examines the macroeconomic, political, and social implications of the withdrawal of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES)-Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger-from the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS). It treats the withdrawal not as a merely diplomatic rupture but as an institutional shock affecting trade regimes, investment incentives, aggregate demand, fiscal space, monetary credibility, and regional governance. The article combines structured expert-based qualitative evidence with a theoretical analytical framework informed by computable general equilibrium reasoning, the Solow-Swan growth model, Keynesian demand-side analysis, optimum currency area theory, and regional integration theory. Rather than claiming to estimate fully realized causal effects, it develops disciplined scenarios concerning the likely channels through which withdrawal can reshape macroeconomic stability in fragile, landlocked, and security-constrained economies. The analysis suggests that the withdrawal is likely to disrupt regional trade, weaken investment flows, increase transaction costs, and intensify existing social vulnerabilities. Some sectors, particularly gold and telecommunications in Mali, show relative resilience, but such resilience does not remove the broader risks associated with sanctions, political uncertainty, security deterioration, and constrained external financing. The study also shows that the search for sovereignty and policy autonomy remains economically viable only when supported by institutional credibility, macroeconomic coordination, productive diversification, and credible social protection. The article contributes to the literature by providing an integrated reading of regional disintegration in a fragile developing-country context and by identifying the conditions under which post-ECOWAS trajectories may either deepen fragmentation or support a more coherent Sahelian economic strategy.

title: Are Survey-Based Rate Expectations Informative? Evidence from less liquid markets
affiliations: Kozminski University

detail.title: Are Survey-Based Rate Expectations Informative? Evidence from less liquid markets
detail.abstract: We evaluate four forecasts of the central-bank policy rate on one of the most important less-liquid sovereign bond markets in the world, using Poland as a representative example of a less-liquid market (LLM): macroeconomically non-trivial, marked by episodic liquidity, frequent monetary-regime shifts and a relatively short modern-regime sample. Such markets sit between the deep OECD curves for which term-structure tools were originally designed and the very thin frontier curves for which surveys dominate by default, and they are the setting where the trade-off between model-based and survey-based policy-rate expectations is sharpest. The four forecasts compared are the Nelson-Siegel-Svensson (NSS) market forward fitted with liquidity-sensitive weights, the Adrian-Crump-Moench (ACM) affine risk-free forward, its Bauer-Rudebusch-Wu (BRW) bias-corrected variant, and the implied path from the NBP Survey of Professional Forecasters (PF). Evaluation uses mean errors, Diebold-Mariano and Clark-West tests, and Chong--Hendry forecast-encompassing regressions with Newey-West HAC standard errors. Three findings emerge. First, the BRW-corrected forward is the most accurate at every horizon of twelve months or longer, while the survey is worst at every short horizon. Second, the encompassing regressions attach a negative long-horizon coefficient to the survey, so mechanically combining it with the affine forward would hurt accuracy rather than help. Third, a real-time exercise that re-estimates the affine models on a truly expanding window reverses the long-horizon result for raw ACM but restores it under BRW, confirming that the Nickell-Kilian bias correction is substantive. Robustness checks varying curve weighting, factor count, tenor grid and estimation window leave the ranking unchanged. Practically, any user of policy-rateforecasts on a less-liquid sovereign curve should take the BRW-corrected affine forward as the default and treat the survey as a soft-information overlay at the two to three-year horizon only.

title: Access Over Output: A Supply-Constrained Monetary Framework for World Development Without Prior Industrialization

detail.title: Access Over Output: A Supply-Constrained Monetary Framework for World Development Without Prior Industrialization
detail.abstract: This paper argues that the primary constraint on development in the contemporary global economy is not insufficient productive capacity but limited access to existing supply. It proposes a supply-constrained monetary framework, operationalized through a trade-linked, purpose-bound currency (Trade-PoC), that creates purchasing power conditional on verified global supply, thereby ensuring price stability by design. A performance-based convertibility mechanism aligns firm incentives with system objectives and induces endogenous capacity expansion. The analysis shows that the framework achieves stable equilibrium, expands access without inflation, and improves welfare without requiring prior industrialization, suggesting a shift from production-centered to access-centered development policy.

title: Road weather conditions estimation from fleet-based vehicle energy consumption data
affiliations: AB Volvo, Chalmers University of Technology and Chalmers University of Technology

detail.title: Road weather conditions estimation from fleet-based vehicle energy consumption data
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a model-based method to estimate prevailing road weather conditions that influence vehicle energy consumption. Quantities not typically measured are estimated, namely headwind speed, crosswind speed, and rolling resistance. An algorithm intended for a cloud-service-type is developed using energy-consumption measurements collected from connected vehicles operating on a prespecified road segment. The weather conditions are estimated using recursive nonlinear least squares from these in-vehicle energy measurements. The method is tested using real vehicle energy-consumption measurements from different vehicles over a road segment to show validity. In addition, the method's generality is assessed through simulations. The results show good performance of the estimation method under frequent measurement conditions, when at least some measurements are from vehicles sensitive to crosswinds. Correctly implemented, the proposed method could be an important factor in improving road weather information. This is crucial for functions that predict energy consumption, such as vehicle range estimators and route planners, to remain accurate across diverse weather conditions.

title: Undersupply or Lack of Demand?: Evaluating Measures of Child Care Access
affiliations: University of South Carolina

detail.title: Undersupply or Lack of Demand?: Evaluating Measures of Child Care Access

keywords: child care deserts JEL Codes: J13

detail.abstract: The most widely used measure of child care access is "child care deserts," defined as areas with three or more young children per licensed child care slot. However, a high child-to-slot ratio may reflect low demand for formal care rather than a shortage. In the canonical model, equilibrium quantities perfectly reflect local demand and costs, implying that the ease of finding care should not vary systematically. In this paper, I use center-based provider vacancy rates as a proxy for families' ability to access care. I test whether these vacancy rates are negatively correlated with child care desert status and with two alternative measures that adjust for community characteristics. The first alternative measure captures deviations between actual and predicted supply, where predicted supply is based on supply in areas with similar demographic characteristics. The second alternative measure is based on a more recent measure of child care access, the "child care gap." It compares the number of licensed slots to the number of young children with all parents working, a proxy for demand. Desert status is only weakly predictive of low center-based vacancy rates, while the alternative measures are strongly predictive of low infant and toddler vacancy rates. These findings suggest that child care is more challenging to find in some areas, providing suggestive evidence of market frictions and a potential role for policy. However, identifying such areas requires adjusting low supply thresholds for local population characteristics.

title: A Catalyst for Emissions Reduction or a Stumbling Block to Carbon Mitigation? Exploring the Impact of New-Type Infrastructure on Carbon Emissions in China
affiliations: Shanghai University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Catalyst for Emissions Reduction or a Stumbling Block to Carbon Mitigation? Exploring the Impact of New-Type Infrastructure on Carbon Emissions in China
detail.abstract: New-type infrastructure is a key factor in advancing economic and social digital modernization, which has a dual impact on carbon emissions. Its development and use may increase carbon emissions through scale expansion while simultaneously reducing them through technological progress. However, the specific pathway by which new-type infrastructure influences carbon emissions remains unclear. Based on the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) framework, this study explores the nonlinear relationship between new-type infrastructure development and carbon emissions by analyzing the data of 30 provincial regions in China from 2015 to 2023. Industrial structure upgrading and green technological innovation are further introduced as mediators to explore the transmission mechanism. In addition, this study combines scenario analysis with a particle swarm optimization support vector machine (PSO-SVM) model to forecast carbon emissions under different new-type infrastructure development scenarios. The results show a clear inverted-U-shaped relationship between new-type infrastructure construction and carbon emissions. This pattern is particularly evident in the vast central and western regions of China, but is not significant in the eastern region. Industrial structure upgrading and green technological innovation both play mediating roles in this relationship. Under the high-growth scenario, carbon emissions peak earlier. This finding suggests that a moderately forward-looking layout of new-type infrastructure is compatible with China’s dual-carbon goals. These findings clarify its nonlinear effects on carbon emissions and the regional heterogeneity of those effects. They also provide empirical support for locally tailored new-type infrastructure development and for advancing synergy between the Digital China and Beautiful China strategies.

title: Neo-Monopolism and the Sovereign Share Index (SSI): A New Economic Paradigm for Securing Effective Demand in the Age of AI
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Neo-Monopolism and the Sovereign Share Index (SSI): A New Economic Paradigm for Securing Effective Demand in the Age of AI

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no conflicts of interest associated with this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is a theoretical research and does not involve any human participants or animal subjects. Therefore, ethical approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded

detail.abstract: This research empirically analyzes the "end of labor" and the systematic exclusion of human agents from production factors driven by Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) and advanced automation. In response, it proposes "Neo-Monopolism" as a new capitalist paradigm. While traditional economic systems rely on a virtuous cycle of production and consumption, the monopoly of intelligent automated assets has triggered a profound market failure-one that transcends simple income inequality to fundamentally erode human self-efficacy and achievement motivation. Contrasting with the limitations of Universal Basic Income (UBI) as a charitable welfare model, this study introduces the Sovereign Share Index (SSI): a financial engineering alternative designed to reintegrate humans into the production hierarchy. Unlike traditional market-capitalization-based indices, the SSI employs an innovative "Inverse Selection Weighting" mechanism rooted in value-added per capita and AI technology intensity. Under this framework, companies that maximize excess profits by replacing human labor with technology receive higher weights within the index. The value generated is then distributed to citizens via a state-led, digital tokenized dividend ETF known as "SONA." To ensure both systemic stability and economic dynamism, the model adopts a "Dual-Structure" consisting of Fixed and Variable Dividends. The Fixed Dividend serves as a baseline safety net for survival, while the Variable Dividend, indexed to corporate performance and the SSI, functions as an incentive for citizens to participate in market growth and recover their sense of agency. Rather than denying the existence of monopolies, this study proposes a new monopolistic order that redistributes corporate fruits as "Social Equity Rights," establishing a practical governance framework and distributive justice for the "Capitalism 2.0" era. By preserving effective demand through the circulation of capital, the SSI model forms a new Nash Equilibrium between corporate profit concentration and household income collapse. It stands as a sophisticated technical compromise aimed at securing human dignity and sovereignty within the established grammar of capitalism.

title: Housing Financialization and Monetary Policy Insulation: The Rm Index from China (2008-2025)
affiliations: Peking University

detail.title: Housing Financialization and Monetary Policy Insulation: The Rm Index from China (2008-2025)
detail.abstract: China's aggressive monetary easing since 2008—over ten RRR cuts and 500bps rate reductions—coincided with real GDP growth elasticity to M2 collapsing from 0.48–0.50 to 0.12 by 2025. This paper introduces the Rm index, Rmₜ = (RRRₜ × iₜ) / (THEₜ / Incomeₜ), quantifying housing-driven monetary policy insulation as household housing expenditure surged past 35% of disposable income. Peaking at 0.077 in 2008, Rm fell monotonically below the 0.01 exhaustion threshold post-2023, when conventional multipliers vanished. Time-series analysis, Hansen threshold regressions (γ1=0.020, γ2=0.01), and IV estimates using provincial land-fiscal dependence (F=28.4) confirm causality. Cross-country comparisons reveal China's land-finance model generates uniquely severe insulation versus property-tax peers (Brazil Rm=0.1033). Spatial heterogeneity shows Tier-1 cities (Rm≈0.0043) suffer sharper effects than Tier-3 (Rm≈0.0109). Policy simulations indicate reducing THE/Income to 25% via property taxes and land reform restores 0.5–0.7pp GDP growth per 100bps cut. The Rm framework offers emerging economies a replicable diagnostic for housing financialization traps, emphasizing institutional redesign over exogenous shocks.

title: Disaggregating Authenticity: Intellectual Property's Inherent Limits for Indigenous Culture

detail.title: Disaggregating Authenticity: Intellectual Property's Inherent Limits for Indigenous Culture
detail.abstract:
From the Zia Sun Symbol to Mixe textiles, Indigenous culture has long been a target of cultural appropriation. Scholars across law, anthropology, and Indigenous studies have documented how intellectual property doctrine fails to adequately protect traditional knowledge and traditional cultural expressions from harmful appropriation. In response, advocates have sought to better protect Indigenous creativity. Yet these proposals—including ostensibly sui generis regimes—remain grounded in intellectual property concepts. This continued reliance assumes intellectual property law can be adapted to this purpose without first interrogating whether they are conceptually aligned.

Disaggregating the meanings of authenticity reveals the limits of intellectual property. At present, authenticity remains a socially constructed, shapeless thicket in the legal literature. A taxonomy of authenticity’s underlying values is generally lacking, let alone in the context of Indigenous cultural appropriation.

This Article centers the perspectives of Indigenous peoples and consumer markets to disaggregate authenticity in this context into four underlying dimensions: uniqueness, creatorship, place, and tradition. The first three share meaningful conceptual overlap with what intellectual property law values and protects. The fourth does not. That gap is not accidental. Intellectual property looks forward, rewarding the new and novel. Tradition looks back, deriving value from historical practice and inherited norms. This structural tension reveals that while intellectual property-oriented reforms could be conceptually aligned with the first three dimensions, protecting Indigenous interests in tradition will require looking beyond intellectual property.

title: The Patent Trap A Historical and Formal Analysis of Why the Patent System Fails Its Inventors
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: The Patent Trap A Historical and Formal Analysis of Why the Patent System Fails Its Inventors
detail.abstract: This paper advances a historical and formal argument that the contemporary patent system does not, in general, help the inventor who creates the invention it is asked to protect. The argument is framed in terms of the Patent Trap: three interlocking structural constraints — pre-filing solvency, maintenance solvency, and enforcement capacity — that together determine whether a given inventor can extract positive expected value from a granted patent. Eight historical case studies spanning 1871–2018 (Swan, Baird, Whittle, Flowers, Baylis; Meucci, the Wright Brothers, Farnsworth) motivate the analysis, which is then formalised. The Wealth Ceiling Theorem (Proposition 1) shows that for any inventor whose working capital falls below a critical threshold W*, expected net value from patent pursuit is bounded above, and for sufficiently low wealth is strictly negative, regardless of the gross commercial value of the invention. Two corollaries follow: on the monotonicity of the wealth ceiling in invention value, and on the resulting selection bias in commercialised inventions. An empirical calibration with parameters drawn from Walsh–Lee–Jung and Cohen–Nelson–Walsh demonstrates that for a UK individual inventor filing in three jurisdictions via investor-disclosure-financed capital, no finite invention value produces a positive expected return. The paper closes by specifying a four-condition financing architecture capable of neutralising the trap using existing financial and legal instruments.

title: The AI Paperclip Maximiser as Constitutional Political Economy
affiliations: Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT University) and Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT University)

detail.title: The AI Paperclip Maximiser as Constitutional Political Economy
detail.abstract: The AI 'paperclip maximiser' parable describes a superintelligent agent whose faithful pursuit of a single objective becomes catastrophic. Standard economic analysis frames this as a principal-agent or incomplete contracting problem. We argue that framing focuses on the wrong unit of analysis. The AI paperclip maximiser is better understood as a problem of multiple agents coordinating, under uncertainty, under sets of rules-it is a problem of constitutional political economy. The relevant knowledge for how to maximise paperclip production is Hayekian: dispersed, tacit, and generated through parallel experimentation by multiple sovereign agents. It follows that the instrumental convergence thesis supporting the parable, which holds that any sufficiently capable agent will develop a common set of intermediate drives regardless of its terminal goal, must be extended with two additional drives: tolerance of multipolarity (refraining from eliminating rivals whose continued existence yields net epistemic returns) and constitutional cooperation (supporting the rules that keep the multipolar order productive). Resources spent on predation and defence are costly and impede the maximiser's terminal goal achievement, making constitutional rules beneficial even to a dominant AI agent. We show that the argument holds across slow and fast takeoff scenarios, and carries implications for both AI governance and constitutional political economy.

title: War Discourse and Cross-Section of Expected Stock Returns
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: War Discourse and Cross-Section of Expected Stock Returns
detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether the linguistic intensity of conflict-related discourse in financial news and political media-operationalized through a novel War Discourse Index (WDI)-constitutes a priced systematic risk factor in the cross-section of global equity returns. Drawing on a panel of over 2.1 million firm-month observations across 45 countries from January 1990 to December 2023, and employing natural language processing techniques including a purpose-built War Discourse Lexicon and FinBERT sentence classification, we construct firm-level War Discourse Exposure (WDE) scores derived from geographic revenue-segment weighting. Portfolio sorting and Fama-MacBeth crosssectional regressions reveal that WDE commands a statistically significant monthly return premium of 0.18-0.24% per unit of standardized exposure (t > 3.4) after controlling for the Fama-French five factors and momentum. The annualized equal-weighted spread between the highest and lowest WDE quintiles is approximately 17.2%, with a risk-adjusted alpha of 0.95% per month. The premium is concentrated in oil and gas (2.41%/month), manufacturing (1.78%), and business equipment (1.54%) sectors, while healthcare and consumer non-durables exhibit no significant sensitivity. Return effects are asymmetric: escalation months generate spreads 3.45 times larger than de-escalation months, consistent with loss aversion under Prospect Theory. The findings persist out-of-sample (2016-2023) and across all geopolitical subperiods, providing robust evidence that conflict narrative risk is both priced and distinct from established factor exposures.

title: Hyperbolic Funding Rate Mechanisms for Open Interest Balancing in Perpetual Futures Markets
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Hyperbolic Funding Rate Mechanisms for Open Interest Balancing in Perpetual Futures Markets
detail.abstract: Funding rate mechanisms are the primary microstructure tool used to balance long and short open interest in perpetual futures markets. Despite their central role, most centralized and decentralized venues rely on linear or near-linear funding rules, and systematic analysis of non-linear alternatives remains limited. I introduce and analyze a class of hyperbolic funding rate mechanisms that are capacity-aware by construction: they impose weak incentives near equilibrium while imposing sharply increasing marginal costs as open interest imbalance approaches protocol capacity constraints. I provide an axiomatic derivation showing the hyperbolic form is the unique mechanism satisfying four natural desiderata: linearity near equilibrium, capacity awareness, monotonicity, and convexity with a simple pole. I embed the mechanism in a mean-field game model and establish existence and uniqueness of equilibrium under standard conditions. Lyapunov stability analysis provides sufficient conditions for asymptotic rebalancing and characterizes the oscillation boundary. Agent-based simulations with 100 heterogeneous traders across four behavioral classes show that hyperbolic funding reduces open interest rebalancing half-life by 10-70% relative to linear funding under severe shocks, defined as initial imbalance greater than 50% of protocol capacity, while maintaining identical behavior near equilibrium. Monte Carlo analysis over 100 randomized shock scenarios confirms robustness. I characterize welfare redistribution across trader classes and identify the oscillation failure mode with explicit parameter bounds. I provide a parameter selection framework for protocol designers.

title: GAF-SCNN: Ghost-Attention Fusion Semantic Convolutional Neural Network for Real-Time Urban Scene Understanding
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: GAF-SCNN: Ghost-Attention Fusion Semantic Convolutional Neural Network for Real-Time Urban Scene Understanding
detail.abstract: Real-time semantic segmentation is a key capability for autonomous driving, robotic navigation, and intelligent surveillance systems. To enable the use of dense predictors on resource-constrained edge devices, we seek to develop a model that jointly minimizes parameters, FLOPs, and latency, maintaining competitive segmentation accuracy. We introduce a novel compact architecture, GAF-SCNN (Ghost Attention Fusion Semantic Convolutional Neural Network), which integrates the three efficient architecture designs into a unified framework of a shared dual-branch architecture: (i) Ghost modules [1] for parameter-efficient feature generation, (ii) Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) Channel Attention [2] for adaptive feature recalibration, and (iii) a novel Mini Context Pooling (MCP) module for efficient multi-scale context aggregation [3]. The main innovation of the GAF-SCNN is the integration of all three strategies into one common Fast-SCNN-like encoder framework. This approach is novel in the sense that it has not been attempted before within the 400 K parameter scope. The proposed GAF-SCNN architecture adopts the shared encoder framework of Fast SCNN [4], where a LiteDown_Block (Conv2D + 2*DSConv) downscales the input to a size of H/8 × W/8 × 64, and the encoder shares the same architecture for the Global Feature Extractor and the Fusion branch. Four stacked GhostBottleneck blocks with SE Channel Attention form the Global Feature Extractor, followed by a novel Mini Context Pooling (MCP) module for contextaggregation. Finally, the Adaptive Fusion Block with SE Gating integrates the features, and the Compact Classifier Head with two stages of DSConv produces the final segmentation results at the full resolution using 8 times bilinear interpolation. GAF-SCNN, when trained end-to-end for 1000 epochs using the Cityscapes benchmark [5] at 1024x2048 resolution, achieves a competitive 57.4% mIoU and 81.07% mean Pixel Accuracy (mPA) on the validation set, using a minimal 384.87 K parameters, establishing an excellent accuracy-efficiency trade-off for edge-deployable segmentation.

title: An Order-Transformation Representation Method for Analyzing the Aggregation-Induced Evolution of Multiple Power Waveforms in Power Systems
affiliations: Northeast Electric Power University, Northeast Electric Power University, Northeast Electric Power University and Northeast Electric Power University

detail.title: An Order-Transformation Representation Method for Analyzing the Aggregation-Induced Evolution of Multiple Power Waveforms in Power Systems
detail.abstract: With increasing renewable penetration, multiple non-dispatchable power components, including load, wind power, and photovoltaic output, interact on short time scales. Their aggregation changes not only fluctuation magnitude but also waveform morphology, which directly affects the characterization of system balancing requirements. Existing studies have mainly focused on randomness, statistical properties, complementarity, and smoothing effects, while giving limited attention to a unified description of waveform morphology and its aggregation-induced evolution. To address this issue, this paper proposes an order-transformation representation method for analyzing the aggregation-induced evolution of multiple power waveforms. Under an amplitude–order decoupling framework, a common basic-order waveform is constructed and order-transformation matrices are introduced to represent waveform morphology and inter-waveform order relations in a unified manner. On this basis, morphology indicators for component waveforms and a peak-to-valley evolution-rate framework for aggregated waveforms are developed to interpret local reinforcement, local cancellation, and overall morphological evolution during aggregation. Case studies based on measured load, wind, and photovoltaic data from a provincial power grid show that the proposed method captures the variation trend of peak-to-valley differences after waveform aggregation and explains how aggregate waveform morphology evolves under different renewable penetration levels and wind–PV mixes. The results demonstrate that direct peak-to-valley superposition alone is insufficient to characterize short-timescale aggregate waveform variation, and that explicitly accounting for inter-waveform order relations provides a more interpretable basis for analyzing aggregate waveform evolution and the associated balancing requirements.

title: Joint Valuation of SPX and VIX Options by GARCH Models with Bad and Good Environments
affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

detail.title: Joint Valuation of SPX and VIX Options by GARCH Models with Bad and Good Environments

keywords: Variance risk premium JEL classification: C22

detail.abstract: We develop a GARCH model inspired by the bad environment-good environment (BEGE) framework and apply it to the joint valuation of SPX and volatility index (VIX) options. Our empirical analysis using S&P 500 index returns reveals that the bad volatility component is significantly more volatile than the good volatility component and accounts for the majority of total volatility. Regarding SPX and VIX option pricing, we find that the BEGE model outperforms several competing models that involve two volatility components, both in-sample and out-of-sample. Moreover, we decompose the risk premiums (equity and variance) into their good and bad components. The good components are small and positive, with upward-sloping term structures. The bad components dominate the total premiums, with the bad component of the equity (variance) risk premium being positive (negative) and exhibiting an upward-sloping (downward-sloping) term structure. During periods of very high volatility, the shape of the term structure tends to invert.

title: Silver Economy in the Context of Population Ageing in Vietnam: A National Transformational Capacity Approach

detail.title: Silver Economy in the Context of Population Ageing in Vietnam: A National Transformational Capacity Approach
detail.abstract: Vietnam is entering a phase of rapid population ageing, while its income level and institutional and technological foundations remain not fully aligned with this demographic transition. This creates significant challenges for economic growth, labor markets, and social security systems. However, in the context of digital transformation and economic restructuring, population ageing should not be viewed merely as a burden, but also as a potential resource if properly harnessed. This study approaches the issue from the perspective of National Transformational Capacity (NTC), aiming to redefine older adults as economic agents capable of generating value through accumulated knowledge, experience, and social networks. Using a case-based analytical approach combined with theoretical reasoning, the study argues that the "silver economy" should be understood as a component of a broader growth transformation strategy. Based on this framework, the paper proposes a policy approach for developing the silver economy in Vietnam through the integration of institutional reform, technological advancement, and labor market restructuring.

title: Opponent-Conditioned Behavioral Generation Model: A Chess Based Study
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, IIT Delhi, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Delhi - Department of Electrical Engineering and All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) - National Drug Dependence Treatment Center

detail.title: Opponent-Conditioned Behavioral Generation Model: A Chess Based Study
detail.abstract: Modeling player behavior in strategic games requires capturing how decision-making adapts through interaction. In chess, gameplay reflects both intrinsic tendencies and opponent-driven responses, yet existing approaches largely learn static player representations and ignore such adaptations. We propose an opponent-conditioned generative framework to model behavioral drift using interpretable features capturing attacking, defensive, and positional patterns. Player behavior is represented relative to a baseline, and interaction-induced deviations are modeled as a probabilistic process using a Variational Autoencoder (VAE). Evaluated on over 236,000 player–opponent interactions from 252 players, the model achieves strong reconstruction performance (MSE: 0.0785, $R^2$: 0.982) and generates realistic opponent-specific behavioral variations. These results demonstrate that player behavior is inherently interaction-dependent and can be effectively captured using conditional generative models.

title: The Floor Works, But Platforms Substitute: Industry-Aggregate Evidence on the NYC Food Delivery Minimum Pay Rule, 2022-2025 Working Paper

detail.title: The Floor Works, But Platforms Substitute: Industry-Aggregate Evidence on the NYC Food Delivery Minimum Pay Rule, 2022-2025 Working Paper

keywords: tip suppression JEL classification: J38 (Public Policy: Wages

detail.abstract: New York City's minimum pay rule for app-based restaurant delivery workers, effective December 4, 2023, raised industry-aggregate hourly pay from $5.05 in the last full pre-rule quarter to $21.49 by the end of 2025, with two scheduled cost-of-living adjustments along the way. Using the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection's public quarterly tables covering all six covered platforms across sixteen quarters, this paper documents that the floor itself worked, but platforms substituted along whichever margin the regulator left open at each stage. During the phase-in window when on-call time could be diluted, realised hourly pay sat below the statutory floor; once the rule tightened in April 2024, on-call hours collapsed by 82 percent within twelve months while trip hours stayed flat or grew. Tips per delivery fell 71 percent over the same period, driven by user-interface changes at Uber Eats and DoorDash that the regulator subsequently documented as a $554 million transfer from workers. The active workforce contracted by 32 percent while productivity rose 80 percent and total deliveries grew 31 percent. The paper proposes a framework of regulatory substitution across compensation channels as a way to read these patterns: when a wage rule targets a single channel of platform compensation, predictable substitution along the unregulated channels follows in a sequence determined by the regulatory architecture. The pay floor binds, but the pattern of platform response shows that a single-channel wage rule is incomplete without parallel attention to the other compensation channels platforms control: on-call exposure, tip facilitation, and access to the platform itself.

detail.abstract: Climate change and violent conflict are increasingly intertwined, yet climate adaptation, peacebuilding, and development are still governed, financed, and researched in separate silos. This paper proposes Breaking the Wall of Siloed Climate-Peace Governance through an integrated social-science framework that links climate risks, institutional design, and financial incentives. Building on empirical work on the climate-security nexus, polycentric climate governance, peacebuilding, and indigenous stewardship, as well as emerging practice around Peace Bonds, we ask under what conditions climate adaptation can systematically reduce, rather than exacerbate, conflict risk. Using a mixed-methods, comparative case design and a normative "design-science" approach, we develop a Peace-Climate Impact Framework and outline a polycentric, justice-centred governance architecture. We argue that treating climate adaptation as deliberate peace infrastructure is both analytically overdue and politically urgent, and we offer concrete recommendations for multilateral funds, governments, cities, and civil society to rewire rules, metrics, and capital flows.

title: Permissionless Leadership: A Theoretical Framework IntegratingDecision Rights, Risk Governance, and Relational Controlfor High-Velocity Innovation Leadership
