detail.title: Permissionless Leadership: A Theoretical Framework IntegratingDecision Rights, Risk Governance, and Relational Controlfor High-Velocity Innovation Leadership
detail.abstract: ABSTRACT The leadership literature has not yet produced a formal construct capable of explaining how senior leaders design organisational environments in which initiative is the default rather than approval the default. This theoretical article introduces Permissionless Leadership as a governance-level leadership logic and develops it through abductive conceptual integration across empowerment, organisational design, innovation governance, and leader competence research streams. The framework specifies three interdependent dimensions: decision-rights architecture (the formal and informal structuring of who may act without prior approval, on what scope of decisions, and within what thresholds); risk and guardrail design (the differentiation of experimentation contexts into green, amber, and red zones by consequence magnitude and reversibility); and relational and competence infrastructure (the leader technical fluency and team psychological safety that enable soft control in lieu of bureaucratic oversight). The paper defends the theoretical distinctiveness of the construct by demonstrating that each existing stream is individually insufficient, that no current framework captures the configurational interdependence of all three dimensions, and that the high velocity digital innovation context creates a cost structure for delayed initiative that existing empowerment and governance theories have not addressed. Eight propositions are derived, including interaction and configurational effects, alongside explicit causal identification strategies for each, to support empirical testing. Boundary conditions specify scope constraints for regulated sectors, high-power-distance contexts, and different firm lifecycle stages. The paper closes with an operationalisation and research agenda oriented toward the causal designs that will allow the framework's propositions to be evaluated rigorously.

title: Innovation-Driven Contractions: A Missing Link for Asset Pricing Puzzles
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Finance Area and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)

detail.title: Innovation-Driven Contractions: A Missing Link for Asset Pricing Puzzles
detail.abstract: We provide a unified resolution for prominent conditional asset-pricing puzzles through "innovationdriven contractions." Empirically, we document two stylized facts: (1) technological innovations initially cause significant labor contractions and have negligible impact on capital, and (2) puzzling disconnectionsbetween stock returns and either investment growth or hiring surprises-intensify under stickier prices. To quantitatively tie these facts, we develop a two-sector New Keynesian model. Our core mechanism relies on the interaction between endogenous markup fluctuations and the division of production into investment and consumption sectors. These model-implied dynamics explain the anomalous negative correlation between stock returns and contemporaneous investment returns, the negative market reactions to favorable labor market news, and the procyclical equity yield term-structure slope. Finally, investment-based dividend yields filtered from our model strongly predict future returns, underscoring our mechanism's empirical applicability.

title: Informal Relational Microfoundations of Triple Helix Innovation Systems
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Informal Relational Microfoundations of Triple Helix Innovation Systems
detail.abstract: This study examines how informal relational mechanisms shape innovation performance in university–industry collaboration contexts. While prior research has emphasized formal institutional arrangements, limited attention has been given to the relational processes through which knowledge exchange occurs. Drawing on microfoundations and social capital perspectives, we conceptualize informal mentorship, alumni engagement, and faculty–industry interaction as relational mechanisms that foster trust and informal knowledge exchange. Using multi-actor survey data and PLS-SEM analysis, the results show that these mechanisms are positively associated with innovation performance through a sequential mediation of trust and informal knowledge exchange. The findings also indicate that innovation culture strengthens these relationships and that effects vary across actor groups. This study contributes by providing empirical evidence on the role of relational mechanisms in shaping innovation outcomes and offers practical insights for managing collaboration in innovation ecosystems.

title: Decision Support for Phased Industrialization of ECU Testing: Balancing Flexibility, Readiness, and Cost Across Development Stages
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Decision Support for Phased Industrialization of ECU Testing: Balancing Flexibility, Readiness, and Cost Across Development Stages
detail.abstract: Prototype testing in staged product development requires a practical balance between flexible bench-based testing and earlier investment into fixed end-of-line (EOL) test solutions. Starting EOL development too early increases rework caused by frequent hardware and software changes, whereas starting too late may delay ramp-up and require costly post-SOP support. This paper presents (i) a phase-oriented overview of prototype testing activities based on a generic B0--DV development taxonomy and (ii) a quantitative decision-support model for timing the transition from test-bench (TB) testing to EOL testing. The model is evaluated on anonymized weekly production-event data from two industrial ECU programs and captures realistic industrial effects, including software-driven usability resets, alternative EOL start scenarios, readiness-gate constraints, and post-SOP penalty costs. A readiness gate approximately four weeks before start of production is introduced to represent the minimum required EOL usability before ramp-up. The results identify an economically favorable EOL start window around the C1 phase, where required usability can still be achieved while avoiding excessive rework from early software churn. The proposed framework provides practical support for test industrialization planning and resource allocation in phased product development.

title: Traffic Signal Control with Extended Perception for Enhanced Robustness andResilience Using Graph Attention and Temporal Encoders
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Gustave Eiffel University

detail.title: Traffic Signal Control with Extended Perception for Enhanced Robustness andResilience Using Graph Attention and Temporal Encoders
detail.abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning has demonstrated significant potential in optimizing Traffic Signal Control; however, existing Multi-Agent approaches often struggle with the non-stationarity inherent to abnormal traffic conditions. Most models, trained in nominal simulation environments, lack the resilience to withstand unforeseen disturbances such as sensor failures, road blockages, or extreme weather. To address this gap, this paper proposes a robust Spatio-Temporal Graph Reinforcement Learning framework explicitly designed for structural stability. Our architecture facilitates intelligent inter-agent collaboration by selectively weighting relevant neighbors via a Graph Attention Network (GATv2), while a Transformer-based Temporal Interaction Encoder captures long-term historical trends. This dual mechanism enables agents to distinguish between transient noise and persistent failure patterns, facilitating proactive rather than reactive control. Furthermore, we introduce a rigorous stress-testing benchmark comprising stochastic perturbation scenarios; ranging from high-frequency random blockages to critical arterial collapses, to quantify system resilience. Extensive experiments on a stochastic grid network demonstrate that our approach not only achieves superior throughput under high-demand nominal conditions but also exhibits exceptional resilience, recovering stable traffic flow significantly faster than state-of-the-art baselines following severe structural disruptions.

title: Transactional Economics: A Conceptual Framework and Measurement Perspective

detail.title: Transactional Economics: A Conceptual Framework and Measurement Perspective

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest

keywords.keywords: Value Transfer; Economic Flows; Macroeconomic Measurement; Gross Transaction Product; Network Economics; Payment Systems; Economic Systems; Flow-Based Analysis

detail.abstract: This paper defines Transactional Economics as a distinct school of economic thought. The school conceptualizes economies as systems of value transfer and treats transactions as the primary observable events through which economic activity occurs. Unlike traditional economic approaches that center on production, allocation, or aggregate outcomes, Transactional Economics focuses on economic motion: the scale, structure, and systemic properties of value transfer between agents. In addition to defining the ontological and methodological foundations of the school, the paper introduces a minimal formal representation and provides an illustrative application using aggregate payment data. The aim is to establish Transactional Economics as a measurement-oriented, system-level framework that complements, rather than replaces, established economic traditions.

title: Optimal Financial Contracting with Multiple Capital Goods and Commitment Risk

detail.title: Optimal Financial Contracting with Multiple Capital Goods and Commitment Risk
detail.abstract: We study optimal financial contracting with partially irreversible investment in multiple heterogeneous capital goods and a small probability of the lender rescinding the contract for exogenous reasons, forcing the firm to restart from scratch. We show how lenders drive firm technology adoption by favoring capital goods that are less prone to obsolescence and that have more liquid resale markets. Consequently, for newer, more productive types that also tend to have thin resale markets or high obsolescence rates, adoption will be slower, especially by smaller or newer firms constrained by credit. Our model yields a richer set of testable predictions relative to the canonical models such as Clementi and Hopenhayn (2006), and entails a more realistic long-run firm size-equity distribution.

detail.title: Neural Discovery of Volatility Dynamics: From Black-Box to a Parsimonious Fragility-Persistence GARCH
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a sequential teacher-student methodology for volatility model discovery. A neural network is used only as a temporary diagnostic device to identify the most misspecified channel in a benchmark model; the final specification remains a lowdimensional, likelihood-based, interpretable econometric recursion. Applied to daily S&P 500 returns from 2000 to 2024, the procedure starts from a Student's t GARCH(1,1) benchmark and is used twice. First, the teacher identifies time variation in tail thickness through (ν t); second, conditional on that baseline, it identifies time variation in overall persistence through (π t = α + β t). The resulting asymmetric fragility-persistence GARCH captures most of the teachers' likelihood gains with limited added dimension. In recursive 2016-2024 forecasting, it outperforms Student's t GARCH, Student's t NGARCH, and a lean Student's t GAS benchmark in predictive log score. Targeted bootstrap evidence empirically supports the persistence block's asymmetric shock structure and its modest volatility refinement.

detail.abstract: Domain Generation Algorithms (DGAs) are commonly used by botnets to create a huge number of domain names dynamically for establishing communication channels. These dynamically generated domains are not easily detected by the blacklisting method because the malicious domains are constantly changing and are able to bypass the security system. Recent studies indicate that machine learning and deep learning methods can effectively detect malicious domains by examining domain name patterns and DNS traffic behavior. However, the existing techniques are not able to detect zero-day domain flux attacks caused by the changing DGA domains. The present paper proposes AdaptiveFusionBERT framework for the detection and classification of malicious domains generated by DGAs. The proposed system uses contextual embedding techniques based on the BERT architecture along with lexical features and machine learning classifiers. The system uses the characteristics of the domain, entropy value, and DNS traffic to differentiate between malicious and benign domains. The proposed system is analyzed to show improved performance in the detection of malicious domains and the classification of zero-day attacks. The proposed framework is capable of providing a solution to enhance the security system against cyber attacks. detail.title: Currency Substitution in High-Inflation Economies: Are Cryptocurrencies Emerging as an Alternative to Fiat Currencies
detail.abstract: In recent years, the global monetary system has faced heightened instability, particularly in economies struggling with chronic inflation, currency depreciation, and a lack of trust in domestic monetary authorities. This paper examines the evolving phenomenon of currency substitution, traditionally characterized by "dollarization"-the shift toward stable foreign fiat currencies to preserve purchasing power. However, with the rise of decentralized financial technology, cryptocurrencies have emerged as a novel, technologically advanced alternative for economic agents seeking a store of value independent of central bank policy. This study explores the drivers behind the adoption of digital assets in high-inflation contexts, comparing them with traditional foreign exchange substitution. Through a review of current literature and economic trends, the research investigates whether cryptocurrencies serve as a complete replacement for fiat money or as a supplementary tool for financial hedging. The analysis highlights a critical trade-off: while cryptocurrencies offer autonomy and accessibility, their price volatility, regulatory uncertainty, and limited acceptance as a medium of exchange hinder their ability to fully perform the functions of money. The paper concludes by discussing the implications of this "digital dollarization" for national monetary policy and financial stability, filling a gap in the literature by integrating traditional substitution theories with the modern digital asset landscape.

detail.title: SATARK: Predictive Pre-emption of Agricultural Stubble Burning via Cascaded Vision Transformer NDVI Phenology, Multi-Constellation Fire Radiometry, and ESP-NOW Ground-Truth Validation
detail.abstract: Agricultural stubble burning across the Indo-Gangetic Plain and its eastward extension into West Bengal constitutes one of the most consequential land-management failures in contemporary South Asian agriculture. VIIRS satellite telemetry documents a 200% inter-annual increase in localised fire events in West Bengal over the study period (2012–2023), as the region transitions from a passive smoke sink into an active producer of its own hydrological destruction. Existing enforcement paradigms — satellite detection followed by administrative fines — are structurally incoherent when applied to smallholder farmers for whom the cost of field clearance by burning (Rs. 1 per matchstick) is offset by a Rs. 600–1,200 per bigha invoice for mechanised alternatives within a 10–14 day harvest window that admits no delay. This thesis presents the complete technical architecture of Project SATARK (Sanskrit: satark, meaning ‘Alert’ or ‘Vigilant’) — an autonomous, multi-layer detection and pre-emptive dispatch system that reframes the problem from post-hoc fire detection to logistics-first intervention. The architecture integrates three mutually validating intelligence layers. The first is a multi-constellation space-to-soil telemetry pipeline fusing NASA FIRMS VIIRS 375m near-real-time fire products with 15-minute geostationary coverage from INSAT-3DR and GK-2A, bypassing the 4-hour state reporting latency to achieve a target orbit-to-intervention loop of approximately 30 minutes. The second is a Cascaded SwinIR Vision Transformer that ingests NDVI time-series from Sentinel-2 and MODIS 16-day composites to map the ‘green-to-brown’ phenological transition and predict the 14-day harvest vulnerability window at individual field parcel resolution, generating a per-parcel Burn Risk Index (BRI) that drives pre-emptive machinery dispatch. The third is a distributed ESP-NOW mesh swarm of ESP8266 nodes deployed in the field as in-situ soil-hydraulics sentinels, providing ground-truth thermal and micro-climatic validation that extends detection capability through cloud-obscured satellite coverage windows and validates satellite signals against industrial false-positive sources. The domain adaptation strategy — pre-training the SwinIR model on 32,000+ images from the California 2020 August Complex wildfire before domain transfer to West Bengal agricultural conditions — is detailed in full, alongside the cascaded super-resolution protocol (INSAT 4km → MODIS 1km → Landsat-8 100m → Sentinel-2 guided 20m) that eliminates the AI hallucination failure mode identified at direct 4km-to-200m upscaling. The Llama-3 70B semantic false-positive filter, operating on OpenStreetMap LULC overlays, achieves target-zero false dispatch rates in the mixed-use Kolaghat deployment zone. Phase 1 field validation results from the Kolaghat Development Block, Purba Medinipur — including the first systematic micro-climatic dataset for the region — are presented alongside the institutional integration pathway secured through BDO and ADA mandates. The ESP-NOW IoT hardware stack is OSHWA-certified IN000084. The Phase 1 ground-truth dataset is published at Harvard Dataverse DOI: 10.7910/DVN/QG8W63

detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of decentralized finance (DeFi) has introduced unprecedented opportunities for financial inclusion, yet the irreversible and permissionless nature of blockchain networks has simultaneously made them a primary target for sophisticated fraud, including rug pulls, phishing drains, and layering schemes. Traditional manual compliance and rule-based systems are increasingly inadequate against the speed of on-chain attackers. This study proposes an advanced AI-driven detection framework that utilizes temporal graph modeling and behavioral data fusion to identify malicious activities in real-time. Using a substantial dataset of over 1.25 million unique addresses and 18.4 million transactions across the Ethereum, BSC, and Solana blockchains, the research evaluates the efficacy of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and unsupervised autoencoders. The methodology emphasizes a "ground truth" labeling process and chronological data splitting to prevent data leakage. Results indicate that the hybrid systemincorporating on-chain transaction traces, smart contract bytecode, and off-chain social signalsachieves an F1-score of 0.81 with a remarkably low false-positive rate of 0.008. Furthermore, the study demonstrates operational efficiency with an inference time of 18ms, making it viable for high-throughput networks. The findings suggest that while AI significantly enhances blockchain security, ongoing challenges in "explainability" and adversarial obfuscation require a "human-inthe-loop" approach to maintain long-term ecosystem trust.

detail.title: The Impact of Digitalization on Retail Investor Participation: Empirical Evidence from NEPSE
detail.abstract: This study aims to examine the impact of digitalization on retail investor participation in the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) by analyzing key determinants, including accessibility, usefulness, technological literacy, security, and information quality. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was adopted using primary data collected from 345 respondents across different regions of Nepal. A structured questionnaire based on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree) was utilized. Data was analyzed using IBM SPSS, applying rigorous methodological procedures. Validity testing confirmed that all items were valid (r = 0.374-0.696 > r-table 0.106 at α = 0.05). Reliability analysis indicated strong internal consistency (Cronbach's Alpha = 0.749-0.836). Normality testing showed acceptable distribution (skewness =-0.803 to-0.621; kurtosis =-0.016 to 0.983), while multicollinearity diagnostics confirmed no issues (tolerance = 0.472-0.559; VIF = 1.789-2.118). Correlation analysis revealed significant positive relationships between retail investor participation and all independent variables (r = 0.442-0.552, p < 0.001), indicating that digitalization-related factors are strongly associated with increased market engagement. Regression results demonstrated that accessibility (β = 0.252, p < 0.001), usefulness (β = 0.211, p < 0.001), and security (β = 0.113, p = 0.042) have a statistically significant positive effect on participation, while technological literacy (β = 0.037, p = 0.411) and information quality (β = 0.090, p = 0.096) were not significant predictors. The overall model was statistically significant (F = 45.324, p < 0.001), explaining 39.2% of the variance (Adjusted R² = 0.392), with a Durbin-Watson value of 2.076 indicating no autocorrelation. These findings suggest that ease of access and perceived usefulness are the most influential drivers of retail investor participation, while basic technological familiarity and information availability alone are insufficient to significantly influence investment behavior in Nepal's digital financial environment.

detail.abstract: This chapter examines digital sovereignty as a geopolitical instrument through which national economies position themselves within an increasingly fragmented global technological order. detail.title: Avoiding Fields on Fire: Information Dissemination Policies for Environmentally Safe Crop-Residue Management
detail.abstract:
Agricultural open burning, i.e., the practice of burning crop residue in harvested fields to prepare land for sowing a new crop, is well-recognized as a significant contributor to CO2 and black-carbon emissions, and long-term climate change. Low-soil-tillage practices using a specific agricultural machine called Happy Seeder, which can sow the new seed without removing the previous crop residue, have emerged as the most effective and profitable alternative to open burning. However, given the limited number of Happy Seeders that the government can supply, and the fact that farmers incur a significant yield loss if they delay sowing the new crop, farmers are often unwilling to wait to be processed by the Happy Seeder and, instead, decide to burn their crop residue.

We study how the government can use effective information-disclosure policies in the operation of Happy Seeders to minimize agricultural open burning. A Happy Seeder is assigned to process a group of farms in an arbitrary order. The government knows, but does not necessarily disclose, the schedule for the Happy Seeder at the start of the sowing season. Farmers incur a disutility per unit of time while waiting for the Happy Seeder due to the yield loss as a result of late sowing of the new crop. If the Happy Seeder processes a farm, then the farmer gains a positive utility. At the beginning of each period, each farmer decides whether to burn her crop residue or to wait, given the information provided by the government about the Happy Seeder's schedule. We propose a class of information-disclosure policies, which we refer to as dilatory policies, that provide no information to the farmers about the schedule until a pre-specified period and then reveal the entire schedule. By obtaining the unique symmetric Markov perfect equilibrium under any dilatory policy, we show that the use of an optimal dilatory policy can significantly lower the number of farms burnt compared to that under the full-disclosure and the no-disclosure policies. Using data from the rice-wheat crop system in northwestern India -- an area of the world with the highest prevalence of open burning -- we conduct a comprehensive case study and demonstrate that the optimal dilatory policy can reduce CO2 and black-carbon emissions by 17% on average. We also examine the impact of the government’s policy on the tradeoff between environmental damage and farmers’ welfare

detail.title: The Aspiration Horizon

detail.abstract: Global fertility has declined from 4.7 births per woman in 1960 to approximately 2.2 today. In post-transition wealthy societies the decline extends far below replacement: South Korea recorded 0.72 in 2023, Japan 1.20, and most of Southern and Eastern Europe sits between 1.2 and 1.5. Despite unprecedented pronatalist expenditure, South Korea alone spent over $210 billion United States dollars (USD) since 2006, no country has reversed a sustained fertility decline. This paper proposes and develops the Aspiration Horizon framework, combining a conceptual argument with comparative case study evidence and empirical correlation analysis, as a more mechanistically precise account of this failure than existing theories provide. We argue that development itself continuously generates the aspirations that make its own demographic continuation less likely: as education, urbanisation, and economic growth expand the range of lives that women can vividly imagine for themselves, motherhood becomes not impossible but directly competitive with a specific and desirable imagined future. This foreclosed-self cost, distinct from the transactional opportunity cost of foregone income, is the primary suppressor of fertility in post-transition societies, and it is not addressable through cash transfers or financial incentives. Drawing on case studies from South Korea, Hungary, France, Japan, and the Nordic countries, we demonstrate that pronatalist policy succeeds only when it reduces the structural incompatibility between motherhood and the aspiration horizon and fails when it attempts to compensate financially for a forfeiture it does not remove. We further show that the policy gap is not merely persistent but structurally self-widening i.e the same prosperity engine that funds pronatalist spending continuously generates new aspirations that make that spending insufficient. We term this the Structural Impossibility Loop. Finally, we examine immigration as the primary available circuit breaker and argue that its effectiveness is conditional on integration infrastructure, particularly cross-cultural education, that most wealthy societies are not currently building at scale. title: Order Now, Pickup in 30 Minutes: Managing Queues with Static Delivery Guarantees
affiliations: , University of Texas at Dallas - Department of Information Systems & Operations Management and University of Texas at Dallas - Naveen Jindal School of Management

detail.title: Order Now, Pickup in 30 Minutes: Managing Queues with Static Delivery Guarantees
detail.abstract: We study the problem of managing queues in online food-ordering services where customers, who place orders online and pick up at the store, are offered a common quote time, i.e., the promised pick-up time minus the time the order is placed. The objective is to minimize the long-run average expected earliness and tardiness cost incurred by the customers. We introduce the family of static threshold policies for managing such queues. A static threshold policy is one that starts serving the first customer in the queue as soon as the server is free and the time remaining until the promised pick-up time of that customer falls below a fixed threshold. In important technical contributions for establishing the attractiveness of the optimal static threshold policy, we develop three sets of lower bounds on the optimal cost. The first set of lower bounds exploits structural properties of two special static threshold policies, while the second set utilizes the idea of a clairvoyant optimal policy by considering a decision maker who has either full or partial knowledge of the outcomes of future uncertainties. To obtain our third set of lower bounds, we develop bounds on the optimal earliness and tardiness costs by establishing lower and upper bounds on the steady-state waiting time under an optimal policy. The optimal static threshold policy is asymptotically optimal in several cases, including the heavy traffic and the light traffic regimes. We also develop a dynamic threshold policy in which the threshold depends on the queue length. Finally, through a comprehensive numerical study, we demonstrate the excellent performance of both the static and the dynamic threshold policies.

title: Subjectively Attractive – The Effect of Process Transparency on Contract Choice, Procedural Fairness, and Long-Term Decisions

detail.title: Subjectively Attractive – The Effect of Process Transparency on Contract Choice, Procedural Fairness, and Long-Term Decisions
detail.abstract: Encouraging long-term oriented decision-making is a key reason why organizations incorporate subjectivity into managers' performance-based contracts. However, contracts with a higher degree of subjectivity may be perceived as less attractive due to the uncertainty surrounding the performance evaluation process, although they are genuinely intended to mitigate the effects of environmental uncertainty. As a result, managers may favor formula-based bonus systems over those involving discretionary weighting. In an experiment with experienced managers, we examine whether process transparency (PT) increases the attractiveness of discretionary-weight contracts and whether PT fosters long-term oriented decision-making through this contract choice and enhanced perceptions of procedural fairness. Our findings reveal that PT significantly increases both the proportion of managers choosing discretionary-weight contracts and the procedural fairness that managers perceive. Furthermore, contract choice and procedural fairness mediate a positive effect of PT on long-term decision-making. These results suggest that PT is an effective mechanism for guiding contract selection in ways that ultimately support beneficial long-term decisions.

title: The Gaconnet Cloud Thesis
affiliations: LifePillar Institute

detail.title: The Gaconnet Cloud Thesis
detail.abstract: We observe molecular clouds birthing stars throughout the observable universe. We observe stars returning enriched material to molecular clouds at death. We observe those enriched clouds birthing subsequent generations of more complex stars. This cycle—cloud to ignition to enriched cloud to more complex ignition—is confirmed at every stage by direct observation, spectroscopic analysis, isotopic evidence from meteorites, and computational modeling. Our own solar system formed through this exact process approximately 4.6 billion years ago, triggered by a supernova shockwave compressing a region of a molecular cloud (Banerjee et al., 2016; Boss & Keiser, 2017; Cameron & Truran, 1977). We currently reside within cloud-topology structures at every observable scale, from the Local Group through the Laniakea Supercluster (Tully et al., 2014) to the cosmic web itself (Gaite, 2019). This paper makes a single deductive argument: the principle of scale invariance, which is foundational to physics, requires that the cloud-to-ignition-to-cloud cycle operate at every scale where the structural conditions for it are present. The assumption that the Big Bang is a universal, singular event—rather than one instance of this cycle at the cosmic scale—constitutes an arbitrary suspension of scale invariance at one specific scale. This suspension is not derived from any physical law. It is an inference from isotropy, and isotropy is the signature of both universality and interiority. An observer inside a sufficiently large, sufficiently uniform cloud will observe isotropy in every direction and will be unable to determine whether anything exists beyond the cloud’s luminous boundary. The thesis: the Big Bang is a local ignition event within a larger pre-generative medium. The observable universe is the interior of the activated region. The cosmic microwave background is the luminous boundary of this local cloud. Every previous cosmological revolution has consisted of the recognition that what was taken for the totality is the interior of a larger structure the observer could not see from inside. This paper applies the same structural correction one more time. No new physics is proposed. No exotic mechanisms are invoked. Six falsification conditions are specified. All required evidence is already collected.

detail.abstract:
This study examines whether mutual funds predict market movements or primarily reflect contemporaneous market conditions. Using a large-scale dataset comprising over 34 million Net Asset Value (NAV) observations across 34,320 schemes from 2006 to 2026, the analysis provides a comprehensive evaluation of return dynamics, market linkages, and volatility behaviour.

The empirical results show that, within the contemporaneous framework examined in this study, mutual fund returns do not exhibit forward-looking predictive behaviour. Instead, they are strongly driven by contemporaneous market returns. Regression analysis indicates a significant positive relationship between mutual fund returns and market returns, while changes in market volatility exert a statistically significant negative effect. These findings are supported by substantial explanatory power, indicating that systematic market factors account for a substantial proportion of return variation.

Further analysis reveals that mutual fund returns exhibit non-normal distributional characteristics, including fat tails and volatility clustering. GARCH estimates confirm that volatility is highly persistent, with shocks dissipating slowly over time. Rolling correlation analysis demonstrates that while the strength of the relationship between mutual fund returns and market returns varies in the short term, it remains consistently strong over longer horizons.

This study contributes to the literature in three key ways. First, it leverages a uniquely large and granular dataset, enabling a comprehensive analysis of mutual fund behaviour in an emerging market context. Second, it explicitly incorporates data integrity diagnostics, demonstrating how unfiltered anomalies can distort empirical inference. Third, it integrates distributional analysis, regression modelling, and volatility estimation within a unified framework to provide a multi-dimensional understanding of mutual fund return dynamics.

title: EMPLOYEE MOTIVATION IN THE WORKPLACE
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia

detail.title: EMPLOYEE MOTIVATION IN THE WORKPLACE
detail.abstract: One of the main elements influencing an organization's overall performance and efficacy is employee motivation. Employers require workers who are not only competent but also driven to carry out their duties with responsibility and enthusiasm in today's highly competitive and ever-increasing workplaces. Increasing productivity, fostering a healthy work environment, and enhancing employee performance are all directly impacted by motivation. Motivated workers are more involved in their work, commit less errors, and are more likely to stick with the company. The purpose of this essay is to examine the idea of employee motivation and discuss its significance in the workplace. It focuses on determining the key elements that affect motivation, including non-financial elements like recognition, communication, the workplace, and chances for professional advancement as well as financial elements like pay and bonuses. The study's foundation is the examination of popular theories of motivation and straightforward observations of actual work environments. The study's conclusions demonstrate that while monetary incentives are crucial for meeting fundamental necessities, they are insufficient to sustain motivation over the long run. When it comes to fostering deeper and longer-lasting employee motivation, non-financial aspects are crucial. Employees are more motivated, for instance, when their work is valued, when they have positive relationships with supervisors and coworkers, and when they have chances to advance their careers. Building trust and raising employee satisfaction are further benefits of a positive workplace and good communication. The study also emphasizes that depending on their own requirements and objectives, various employees may be driven by different causes. This implies that rather than depending just on one tactic, managers should adopt a flexible approach and use various motivational techniques. Businesses that comprehend and implement this strategy are more likely to see long-term profitability, improved performance, and increased employee happiness. In summary, employee motivation is a result of a variety of interrelated components rather than a single issue. To develop a well-rounded and efficient system, businesses should concentrate on both financial and non-financial aspects of incentive. By doing this, businesses may increase worker engagement, lower attrition, and develop a solid and effective team.

title: Outgroup Neighbor Exposure (ONE): A Framework for Hyperlocal Residential Segregation

detail.title: Outgroup Neighbor Exposure (ONE): A Framework for Hyperlocal Residential Segregation

publicationDetails.journalName: Indian Institute of Management Bangalore Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: The "contact hypothesis," or the idea that effective interpersonal contact can ameliorate outgroup prejudice, is a central (even if sometimes implicit) motivation for the quantitative measurement of residential segregation. However, extant segregation metrics typically do not account for group diversity or spatial arrangements within administratively defined neighborhoods, such as census blocks, which are the sites of everyday outgroup interactions that modulate anomie or trust between groups. We introduce ONE (Outgroup Neighbor Exposure), a simple framework combining neighborhood diversity and neighbor homophily to better account for salient outgroup contact opportunities. Using a unique census-scale demographic microdataset, we apply our framework to examine outgroup contact opportunities for two of the most spatially and socioeconomically marginalized groups in India-Dalits (historically "untouchable" caste groups) and Muslims. We uncover a non-monotonic association between neighborhood diversity and neighbor homophily, such that the most diverse neighborhoods are associated with the greatest hyperlocal segregation.

title: Better to Bend than to Break: Sharing Supply Risk Using the Supply-Flexibility Contract
affiliations: , University of Texas at Dallas - Department of Information Systems & Operations Management, State University of New York, SUNY at Stony Brook University, College of Business and University of Texas at Dallas - Naveen Jindal School of Management

detail.title: Better to Bend than to Break: Sharing Supply Risk Using the Supply-Flexibility Contract

publicationDetails.detailsText: Manufacturing & Service Operations Management, volume 23, issue 5, 2021[10.1287/msom.2020.0886]

detail.abstract:
Problem Definition: We analyze a contract in which a supplier, who is exposed to disruption risk, offers a supply-flexibility contract comprising of a wholesale price and a minimum-delivery fraction ("flexibility'' fraction) to a buyer facing random demand. The supplier is allowed to deviate below the order quantity by at most the flexibility fraction. The supplier's regular production is subject to random disruption but she has access to a reliable expedited supply source at a higher marginal cost.

Academic/Practical Relevance: Despite the prevalence of supply-flexibility contracts in practice, to the best of our knowledge, there is no previous academic literature examining the optimal design of supply-flexibility contracts. As such, the level of flexibility in practice is usually set on an ad-hoc basis, with buyers typically reluctant to share risk with suppliers. Our analysis of supply-flexibility contracts informs practice in two ways: First, using analytically-supported arguments, it educates managers on the effects of their decisions on the economic outcomes. Second, it shows that the supply-flexibility contract benefits both the supplier and the buyer, regardless of which player chooses how supply risk is allocated in the supply chain.

Methodology: Non-Cooperative Game Theory, Non-Convex Optimization.

Results: We derive the supplier-led optimal contract and show that supply-chain efficiency improves relative to the price-only contract. More interestingly, even though the buyer lets the supplier decide how the two share supply risk, profits of both the players increase by the introduction of flexibility into the contract. Further, supply-flexibility may be even more valuable for the buyer compared to the supplier. Interestingly, the flexibility fraction is not monotone in supplier reliability and a more reliable supplier may even prefer to transfer more risk to the buyer. The robustness of these findings is established on two extensions: one where we study a buyer-led contract (i.e., the buyer chooses the flexibility fraction) and the other where the expedited supply option is available to both the supplier and the buyer.

Managerial Implications: The supply-flexibility contract is mutually beneficial for both players and yet retains all the advantages of the price-only contract -- it is easy to implement, requires minimal operational and administrative burden, and there is evidence of the use of such contracts in practice. While our focus is not on supply-chain coordination, we note that the combination of two mechanisms -- the supply-flexibility contract derived in this paper to share supply risk and a buyback contract to share demand risk -- yields a coordinating contract.

detail.title: Chief M.S. Sowole of Ipara-Remo: Legislator, Diplomat, and Public Servant of Western Nigeria
detail.abstract: Ipara-Remo in present-day Ogun State, Nigeria. A senior member of Chief Obafemi Awolowo's Action Group (AG) and a close personal friend of the Premier himself, Sowole served as a member of the Western Region House of Assembly (WRHA), moved the landmark 14 June 1955 legislative motion that gave the first parliamentary recognition to what became the Midwest Region of Nigeria in 1963, and subsequently represented the Western Region as Agent-General and Ambassador in London. He later served as a commissioner in the post-1967 Western State government. Despite his evident significance to the First Republic era (1960-1966), Sowole has received minimal sustained scholarly attention. This working paper, drawing on contemporaneous newspaper records, the Western Region House of Assembly Debates (14 June 1955), royal memoirs, archival photographic captions from Paul Popper Limited (1956) and Getty Images/Keystone (1958), and published personal interviews, presents the most comprehensive account of his career assembled to date. Three findings are offered as new contributions to the historical record: (1) that Sowole received 82 votes to Awolowo's 81 in the 1951 Remo Electoral College, a result unreported in prior scholarship; (2) the full dialogue of the 1956 ministerial withdrawal episode; and (3) the identification of 45A Kensington Gardens, London, as a significant diplomatic and social hub for Yoruba elites in Britain in the late 1950s.

title: Do Not Look Far: Performance of Myopic Policies for Inventory Management at Retail Stores
affiliations: and

detail.title: Do Not Look Far: Performance of Myopic Policies for Inventory Management at Retail Stores
detail.abstract:
Problem definition: Myopic replenishment policies are widely used in retail practice and often perform comparably to far more complex look-ahead approaches, despite prior literature suggesting such policies are suboptimal because they ignore future demand information. We study a finite-horizon multi-product lost-sales inventory problem with joint shelf capacity and minimum presentation constraints and ask under what structural conditions the myopic policy is optimal, rendering the complexity of look-ahead optimization unnecessary. 
Methodology/results: We first show that the myopic policy is optimal when available shelf capacity falls below a characterizable threshold at which the capacity constraint binds in every period and across all demand realizations. We then develop an efficient solution algorithm based on Lagrangian relaxation that solves the capacity-constrained myopic problem in time linear in the number of products. To evaluate the performance of the myopic policy beyond the optimality threshold, we construct three upper bounds on optimal profit: a capacity-margin bound obtained by solving a continuous knapsack problem that maximizes per-period margin under capacity and presentation constraints, a clairvoyant bound that assumes perfect foresight of demand realizations, and an information-relaxation dual bound that penalizes violations of non-anticipativity. Through a comprehensive numerical study, we demonstrate that the composite of these three bounds is remarkably tight within the proven optimality regime, confirming the quality of our bounding procedure. Benchmarking against two forward-looking policies confirms that the myopic policy degrades as capacity grows beyond the optimality threshold, where both benchmarks deliver meaningfully better solutions, but at substantially greater computational cost. 
Managerial implications: For many retailers operating in capacity-constrained settings, myopic replenishment policies may be optimal without sacrificing performance. In such environments, additional investment in more complex look-ahead methods is unlikely to improve performance; managerial effort may be better directed toward demand forecasting and execution capabilities.

title: Twin Fiscal Stimulus and Inequality in a New Keynesian DSGE Model

detail.title: Twin Fiscal Stimulus and Inequality in a New Keynesian DSGE Model
detail.abstract: This study attempts to investigate the distributional consequences of a ‘twin fiscal stimulus’ – comprising simultaneous reductions in consumption and income taxes – within a Three-Agent New Keynesian (THRANK) Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium (DSGE) framework. Motivated by the 2025 GST rate rationalization and income tax reform in India, the paper develops an ex-ante analysis by conducting tax policy experiments to study the resulting shifts in consumption inequality in an economy with three categories of households – the non-hand-to-mouth (Ricardian), the wealthy hand-to-mouth and, poor hand-to-mouth. The findings reveal a complex trade-off: first, a persistent income tax reduction targeted at wealthy hand-to-mouth households reduces the inequality between Ricardian and wealthy hand-to-mouth agents but exacerbates intra-hand-to-mouth inequality. Conversely, tax relief targeted to Ricardian households widens inter-group inequality while inadvertently reducing disparities within hand-to-mouth cohorts. Furthermore, while GST rationalization favouring hand-to-mouth groups successfully reduces the consumption inequality between Ricardian and hand-to-mouth cohorts, it induces a marginal increase in intra-HM inequality. Finally, within the twin fiscal stimulus framework, the GST rationalization shock emerges as a critical corrective instrument, offsetting the adverse distributional spillovers of income tax cuts and acting as a net positive shifter toward broader inequality reduction.

title: The Economic and Environmental Implications of Carbon Tariffs: A Supply Chain Competition Perspective
affiliations: , Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech) - Department of Information Systems and Management Engineering, Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech) - Department of Information Systems and Management Engineering and Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Information Systems, Business Statistics and Operations Management

detail.title: The Economic and Environmental Implications of Carbon Tariffs: A Supply Chain Competition Perspective
detail.abstract: Inconsistent carbon emission regulations worldwide have raised two concerns for countries with stringent regulations: (1) local firms relocate production/sourcing to countries with lenient regulations, causing carbon leakage and increasing global emissions, and (2) local firms face disadvantages in global competition due to high emissions costs. To address these concerns, carbon tariffs have been imposed to equalize the emissions costs of imported goods with those produced in regulated countries. The ongoing debates surrounding the efficacy of carbon tariffs have focused primarily on production relocation, while paying less attention to sourcing relocation, where firms’ vertical interactions with suppliers and horizontal competition with rivals both play important roles. Our study contributes by examining the efficacy of carbon tariffs from a supply chain competition perspective. We develop a game-theoretical model to analyze the sourcing decision of a local manufacturer (i.e., sourcing from a local or foreign supplier), who competes with a foreign manufacturer in the domestic market. Our analysis reveals three main findings. First, while carbon leakage is traditionally understood as cost-driven, we identify a novel form of leakage that is competition-driven, where the local manufacturer strategically opts for global sourcing to weaken the competitiveness of the foreign competitor, even at higher sourcing costs. Second, carbon tariffs mitigate carbon leakage through a distinctive channel by incentivizing foreign clean technology adoption. Despite its potential to induce clean leakage, the foreign adoption instead mitigates such leakage by intensifying competition from the foreign supply chain. Finally, when regulatory disparities are small, carbon tariffs fail to reconcile economic and environmental goals and may even amount to “green protectionism,” protecting domestic production whereas increasing global emissions as local production remains carbon-intensive. Our research highlights the important role of supply chain competition in shaping the efficacy of carbon tariffs and provides new insights to governments in policy implementation.

detail.abstract: This study aims to investigate the nuances of organizational culture and its influence on employee involvement within national and multinational companies. Utilizing established frameworks in organizational behavior and culture, the research explores dimensions such as empowerment, team orientation, and capability development. Design/methodology/approach: Drawing from Cameron and Quinn's Competing Values Framework (2006) and Denison's model (1990), the study employs statistical analysis to compare mean "Involvement" scores between national and multinational companies. Subsequent analysis delves into the traits of empowerment, team orientation, and capability development. ANOVA is utilized to scrutinize variations in Team Orientation and Capability Development, considering leadership and cultural context. Findings: Multinational companies exhibit lower mean involvement scores, particularly emphasizing team orientation with slightly higher capability development. ANOVA identifies significant differences in Team Orientation, highlighting leadership's role. Borderline significance in Capability Development warrants further exploration. Research limitations/implications: The study's scope is limited to national and multinational companies, potentially overlooking nuances in smaller organizations or across diverse industries. Longitudinal studies could provide deeper insights into the evolving nature of organizational culture and involvement. Practical implications: Tailored interventions are recommended for multinational companies, emphasizing team collaboration and capability development. National companies are advised to address variability in empowerment perceptions for a more consistent organizational culture. Social implications: Fostering a culture of involvement not only enhances organizational effectiveness but also contributes to employee well-being and satisfaction, ultimately benefiting society by promoting healthier work environments. Originality/value: This study contributes to the understanding of how organizational culture influences employee involvement across different types of companies, offering insights for 562 A. Varma, A. Vajpayee, P. Sanghani practitioners to foster more engaged and effective workplaces. Additionally, it underscores the importance of considering cultural context and leadership in shaping organizational dynamics.

The findings reveal that multinational companies exhibit significantly higher adaptability, driven particularly by strong scores in creative change and organizational learning. Although no significant disparities were identified in overall consistency scores, multinational organizations consistently demonstrated higher scores across core values, agreement, and coordination and integration. The study emphasizes the interdependence of adaptability and consistency traits, providing actionable insights for leaders aiming to foster resilient and effective organizational cultures. While the research has certain limitations, such as a reliance on self-reported data and a cross-sectional design, it lays a foundation for future explorations into the nuanced dimensions of organizational dynamics across diverse global contexts.

title: Legitimate Organizational Culture: A Comparative Study

detail.title: Legitimate Organizational Culture: A Comparative Study
detail.abstract: Culture as a concept has had a long and checkered history. It has been used by the layperson as a word to indicate sophistication, as when we say that someone is very "cultured". It has been used by anthropologists to refer to the customs and rituals that societies develop over the course of their history. In the last decade or so it has been used by some organizational researchers and managers to indicate the climate and practices that organizations develop around their handling of people or to the espoused values and credo of an organization. In this context managers speak of developing the "right kind of culture" or a "culture of the quality", suggesting that culture is concerned with certain values that managers are trying to inculcate in their organizations. Also implied in this usage is the assumption that there are better or worse cultures, stronger or weaker cultures and that the right kind of the culture will influence how effective organizations are. Culture will be most useful, as a concept if it helps us better understand the hidden and complex aspects of organizational life. This understanding cannot be obtained if one use superficial definitions. Present Study: Since organizational culture is an important dimension to be considered for almost all aspect of the organization, the present project has taken up this issue for study and analyzing the focus between multinational and national organizations. It has been generally observed that the organizational culture and climate differ a great deal from one organization to another and this is seen more clearly in national and multinational organizations. Assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of organizational culture to helps an organization get an insight into the problem and thus try to attain maximum benefits. The comparison of multinationals with national organizations will help to understand the cultural attributes in a particular organizational set up. Organizational traits are divided into four major traits along with 12 sub components. These enable the organization to identify the weaknesses if any worked to overcome the same. Thus the main Objectives of the present study were as follows:  To examine the typical culture that exists in organizations.  To ascertain if this culture differs between multinational and national organizations.  To find out if there exists a difference in the sub-dimension of the overall culture of the organization viz, multinational and national organizations.  To ascertain if there is any association between the dimensions of organizational culture in regard to its twelve traits and whether there relationships vary between multinationals and national organizations. METHODLOGY Hypotheses: (1) There will be a significant difference between the multinational and national organization in regard to organizational culture. detail.abstract: Based on the existing twelve core definition systems of value analysis, this paper expands and adds two value definitions of positive value religion and negative value religion. Following the core law of dynamic value change, it abandons the binary judgment thinking of being either black or white, and clarifies the phased and comprehensive judgment criteria for the value attributes of religions at the national governance level. Taking orthodox Christianity and religious forms such as the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom religion in the Late Qing Dynasty as comparative cases, this paper analyzes the concrete manifestations of religious positive value creation and negative value release, reveals the governance misunderstanding of the Late Qing government that confused the value attributes of the two types of religions and implemented a one-size-fits-all crackdown policy. It demonstrates that the judgment of religious value must be based on the net value effect and actual externalities, rejecting absolute and final qualitative judgment, and provides theoretical support at the axiological level for the rational identification and governance of religious value.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether government officials should be restricted from appointing individuals with whom they have personal relationships, with a focus on promoting merit-based recruitment and transparency in the public sector. It discusses nepotism and its global effects, noting both short-term advantages such as trust and efficiency, and major drawbacks including corruption, inefficiency, and reduced public trust. The study focuses on Jordan, where wasta is a common practice that can ease processes but undermines fairness and equal opportunity. Through analysis of various perspectives, the paper highlights the ethical and practical consequences of such systems and considers potential reforms, including stronger regulations and greater institutional oversight. It concludes that despite some cultural relevance, the negative impacts of wasta outweigh its benefits, making increased transparency and enforcement necessary for good governance.

title: FlameFNO: Fourier neural operator for solving the auto-ignition and laminar premixed flame problems
affiliations: Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory and Zhejiang University

detail.title: FlameFNO: Fourier neural operator for solving the auto-ignition and laminar premixed flame problems
detail.abstract: Combustion kinetics simulations typically face issues of high stiffness and computational cost due to multiscale coupling between chemical reactions and transport processes. This paper proposes an operator network framework FlameFNO for combustion problems based on the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO). By directly learning the mapping relationship from initial and boundary conditions to the complete spatiotemporal solution field, it achieves efficient solution of combustion problems while avoiding explicit time advancement and spatial discretization. FlameFNO is validated on zero-dimensional auto-ignition and one-dimensional laminar premixed flame problems, covering both simplified reaction models and detailed chemical reaction mechanisms. Results demonstrate that the model accurately predicts temperature, key species distributions, and flow variables with low error. It maintains strong generalization capabilities under extrapolated conditions and exhibits significant resolution insensitivity. Compared to traditional numerical methods and benchmark neural network models, FlameFNO significantly reduces computational cost while maintaining accuracy, revealing the high efficiency and universal potential of operator neural networks in combustion dynamics and flame simulation.

detail.abstract:
This paper asks a simple but central question: do climate beliefs causally reduce emissions? Using a U.S. county-year panel that combines high-resolution CO₂ emissions with geographically disaggregated measures of climate attitudes, I construct a Climate Transition Index capturing local support for climate policy.

I first document a strong negative cross-sectional relationship between climate beliefs and emissions. However, this relationship disappears once county fixed effects are introduced, suggesting that it reflects persistent structural differences rather than within-county changes over time.

To address endogeneity, I implement an instrumental variables strategy exploiting climate-related disasters interacted with local political composition. While these shocks shift climate beliefs, they do not affect emissions. The reduced-form relationship is near zero across all specifications, and two-stage least squares estimates are small and statistically insignificant.

These results indicate that exogenous changes in climate beliefs do not translate into measurable emissions reductions in the short run. Instead, emissions are primarily determined by structural factors such as energy systems, infrastructure, and industrial composition.

The findings suggest that climate beliefs function as an indicator of local transition capacity rather than a direct driver of emissions. This has important implications for policy design: interventions that target beliefs alone are unlikely to reduce emissions without corresponding structural change..

Keywords:
Climate change; Emissions; Public opinion; Climate beliefs; Political economy; Energy policy; Instrumental variables; Structural constraints; Environmental economics; Transition risk

detail.abstract:
《元素化的枷锁》以“劳动力的分解”为核心线索，重新审视人类压迫的整个历史，从原始社会到数字资本主义，并推断出通往共产主义解放的道路。以下是本书的核心摘要：

 

一、核心论点：区分压迫与剥削的根本原因

书中做出了一个关键区分：压迫的最终根源是“劳动力的分解”——即劳动力能力与人类生活活动的混乱统一分离，使其成为一个可以被识别、衡量、组织和拥有的独立元素。而剥削则是因果劳动力与“私人控制”结合的产物。换句话说，私人行为者通过控制生产资料等，剥夺工人创造的剩余价值而无偿。文明数千年的历史，同时是劳动力因素加深和压迫演变的过程，剥削从直接形式转向更隐蔽的形式。

 

二、劳动力分解的历史演变

本书系统地考察了这一过程的各个阶段：

 

· 原始社会：劳动力与生活活动不可区分地融合，处于“尚未被分解”的状态。

· Slave Society: Labor power completed its “resource-ization,” with slave owners directly possessing the bodies of laborers, treating them as resources no different from minerals or livestock.

· Feudal Society: The mode of control shifted to an indirect one mediated by land. The personal dependency of labor power weakened, but oppression deepened into forms like land rent, taxes, and patriarchy.

· Industrial Capitalism: Labor power completed its “commodification.” Workers gained formal legal freedom but were in substance propertyless, forced to sell their labor power on the market.

· Digital Capitalism: The commodification of labor power has expanded comprehensively. Through algorithms and platforms, capital has extended its control from the “workplace” to the “field of education” and the “field of life,” achieving a panoramic colonization of the worker’s entire life process. People’s rest, social interaction, emotions, and data all become sites of value extraction.

 

III. The Path to Liberation: Sublating Factorization, Regaining Control

The book argues that merely overthrowing private ownership only abolishes one institutional form of exploitation but does not touch the root cause of oppression. True liberation, the essence of communism, lies in thoroughly “sublating the factorization of labor power” itself. This requires a two-stage revolution:

 

1. 政治革命：废除劳动力买卖的联系，从而消除工资劳动制度。

2. 社会革命：重新掌控劳动力生产的整个过程。

最终，在共产主义阶段，人类意识将成为劳动力的主要形式，所有具体执行权都交由先进工具承担。劳动将部分从强制社会生产领域中解放出来，回归为生活的基本需求和自由自我实现的活动。届时，“各人按能力分配，按需分配”的原则将从分配问题转变为生产问题，个人直接利用共同拥有的生产资料生产所需物资。

 

书中总结道，共产主义不仅是道德理想，更是人类文明唯一不可避免的命运，是摆脱资本逻辑推动我们走向的两个死胡同的唯一出路：“绝对过度生产”和“存在性毁灭”。

title: Who Gains from Trade? Labor Market Impacts of RTAs in a Sectoral-Armington Model *

detail.title: Who Gains from Trade? Labor Market Impacts of RTAs in a Sectoral-Armington Model *
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the general equilibrium effects of RTAs on labor market outcomes using a sectoral-Armington framework with endogenous labor allocation across sectors. Using RTA trade effects estimated with a gravity model, I compute the changes in trade costs due to the implementation of RTAs between 1986 and 2018, which are used to solve the equilibrium condition in changes for changes in relative wages and sectoral employment across countries. The results show that small and developing countries benefit in relative wage terms, while advanced economies experience losses. Applying the model to an ex ante trade policy, the Transatlantic Trade and Investment Partnership (TTIP) between the US and European Union (EU), the analysis finds that TTIP could significantly boost relative wages in the EU, while modestly reducing them in the US and non-member countries.

title: Res Publica Forma III: The Republical Engine: Constitutional Theory of Value Admission and Non-debt Issuance

detail.title: Res Publica Forma III: The Republical Engine: Constitutional Theory of Value Admission and Non-debt Issuance

detail.abstract:
Modern monetary systems operate through a structural inversion: value is admitted into circulation prior to its realisation. Credit, projection, and expectation precede recognition, making debt the primary mechanism of economic coordination. This paper argues that this ordering is not a technical necessity but a constitutional choice.

At its centre lies a missing category: the absence of a formal act by which surplus is publicly recognised before it is abstracted into value. In the absence of such recognition, value is introduced on the basis of anticipation, and legitimacy is deferred into the future.

The paper introduces declaration as a distinct constitutional act, separate from production, measurement, and issuance. It demonstrates why markets, prices, and growth indicators cannot perform this function, and shows how anticipatory systems become structurally dependent on debt and continuous validation.

From this follows the possibility of non-debt issuance: a system in which value is admitted only after recognised surplus. The Republical Engine is defined as the constitutional framework governing this order. The argument is doctrinal rather than programmatic, establishing conditions of admissible issuance while leaving institutional implementation to subsequent work.

title: From monopoly to justice: The (non) evolution of public interest objectives in South African competition law

detail.title: From monopoly to justice: The (non) evolution of public interest objectives in South African competition law
detail.abstract: This article examines the historical development and contemporary influence of selected public interest objectives in South Africa's competition law. It traces the trajectory from colonial and apartheid-era statutes that entrenched monopoly power and excluded black entrepreneurs to the transformative ambitions of the Competition Act 89 of 1998 and its 2018 amendments. The article argues that while public interest provisions were introduced to promote economic inclusion, their implementation has been inconsistent and susceptible to excessive ministerial discretion and conceptual vagueness. A review of case law reveals doctrinal tensions between traditional competition adjudicative frameworks and the Act's transformative objectives. The article contends that the transformative potential of competition law will remain unrealised unless these tensions are resolved through more explicit interpretive guidance and a principled balancing of public interest factors. It concludes that South Africa's competition regime must strengthen the adjudicative framework and ensure institutional independence in order to transform competition law from a symbolic policy commitment to a substantive mechanism for advancing inclusive and equitable economic justice.

title: Artificial Intelligence at the Crossroads: Productivity J-Curves and Carbon Trade-Offs in the Global Economy
affiliations: Panskura Banamali College, Panskura Banamali College and Panskura Banamali College

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence at the Crossroads: Productivity J-Curves and Carbon Trade-Offs in the Global Economy
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence functions as an engine for increasing productivity and economic growth of a nation. At the same time, it creates economic inequalities. The rapid development of the AI sector has profoundly transformed global systems, fundamentally altered operational paradigms and paved novel pathways for economic growth. This study is trying to examine the intricate relationship between AI and economic growth, particularly on both the productivity gains and economic inequalities associated with AI adoption. We frame this scenario through the lens of Productivity J-Curve analysis. Using a panel of selected OECD countries spanning a period of eight years (2013-2020), the present study seeks to shed some light to examine the association among technological, political, and environmental factors, particularly AI patent and robot installation and their effects on economic growth, measured by Gross domestic product (GDP) growth. Furthermore, this study also focuses on the complex relationship between political factors, specifically democracy and political stability, and their impact on environmental degradation, measured by carbon emissions. To assess this relationship, we apply a novel econometric technique Seemingly Unrelated Regression Estimation (SURE) approach. Findings from our empirical study supports the productivity J-curve hypothesis where AI adoption at the early phase exhibit slower productivity growth, and the organizational changes catch up over time. It highlights the necessity for sustained organizational adaptation, realizing full productivity gain of emerging technologies. Democratic systems frequently face delays in enacting and enforcing stringent environmental regulations due to political negotiations. Governments may prioritize economic development, often postponing environmental regulations to boost economic growth.

detail.title: Deep Image Prior Meets Spectrogram: Zero-Shot Denoising for Blind RF Detection
detail.abstract: In non-cooperative RF sensing, spectrogram denoising is critical for blind detection, yet conventional deep learning suffers from performance degradation caused by domain shift due to their heavy reliance on paired training data. This paper presents a systematic study of Deep Image Prior (DIP) for zero-shot RF spectrogram enhancement. We evaluate three optimization strategies—Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics (SGLD), Regularization by Denoising (RED), and Optimal Eye Surgeon (OES)—and propose two hybrid architectures (OES+SGLD/RED) that combine architectural sparsification with weight optimization. Notably, we demonstrate that log-magnitude spectrograms outperform raw IQ components as DIP inputs under high-noise-power conditions, revealing that energy distribution dominates over phase information for RF signal recovery. Experimental results show that the proposed methods significantly outperform BM3D baselines and successfully restore weak signals even when visually imperceptible, offering a practical, information-leakage-free solution for wideband blind RF surveillance.

detail.abstract: Liquidity crises in financial institutions are often characterized by abrupt funding shortfalls rather than by insolvency in a narrow accounting sense. During such episodes, margin requirements, funding withdrawals, and balance-sheet constraints interact to force deleveraging and asset sales, even when asset fundamentals remain sound. This paper develops a structural framework for analyzing funding liquidity risk at the level of a financial institution, emphasizing the endogenous nature of funding stress. The framework models funding liquidity risk as a balance-sheet constraint linking margin requirements, contractual and behavioral cash outflows, contingent liquidity demands, and the quality of funding sources to effective funding capacity. A central object of the analysis is a funding scarcity variable that summarizes the tightness of the funding constraint and evolves endogenously under stress. The model captures margin spirals and loss spirals as mutually reinforcing mechanisms that amplify liquidity shocks and generate non-linear stress dynamics. By explicitly linking funding scarcity to market liquidity outcomes, the framework explains price dislocations, commonality of liquidity across assets, and flight-to-quality dynamics as equilibrium consequences of constrained intermediation rather than changes in beliefs or fundamentals. The paper further discusses policy and risk management implications, highlighting the limitations of static liquidity ratios and the role of central bank interventions in alleviating funding constraints. A prototype implementation illustrates how the framework can be operationalized for liquidity stress testing and contingency funding planning.

title: Beyond Retention Metrics: A Student Engagement Centered Lifecycle Framework

detail.abstract: Higher education is a voluntary enterprise-institutions earn students' continued presence, not require it. Yet despite genuine investment in data systems and student success initiatives, institutions lack a principled guide for what to measure, when to measure it, and what institutional response the measurement should inform at each stage of the student journey. This paper proposes a student engagement centered lifecycle framework that addresses this structural gap. The framework identifies four stages-Entry, Early Formation, Stabilization, and Transition-each defined by the question the student is asking and each calling for qualitatively different measurement and institutional response. The framework extends Tinto's integration theory by proposing that the relative importance of academic and social integration shifts across stages: academic integration is relatively more salient at Early Formation, while social integration and friction reduction become relatively more important at Stabilization-a shift driven by declining population heterogeneity as students progress. The framework's central argument is that upstream intervention at the early stage is particularly important and effective-student engagement is more heterogeneous there, behavioral signals are more informative, and institutional leverage is higher before engagement patterns stabilize. The practical value of the framework lies in its implications for institutional action: enabling stage-specific measurement, more effective intervention design, and more precise resource allocation so that institutions can better serve students at each point in their academic journey.

detail.abstract:
This paper presents a structured corpus of aphorisms that define the conceptual foundations of Institutional Counterintelligence Analysis (ICA), an analytical discipline founded by Andrey Spiridonov, PhD.

The work advances the argument that, in conditions of information surplus, the decisive variable in intelligence and security systems is not the volume of data, but the quality of its interpretation. Within this framework, counterintelligence is reconceptualized as a structural practice focused on the management of uncertainty within institutional systems and its redistribution within adversarial environments.

The aphoristic form is used as a method of analytical compression, capturing stable relationships between analysis, decision-making, and institutional security. The paper contributes to the development of a systematic approach to understanding how institutional vulnerabilities emerge from procedural regularities and how adversarial integration operates within complex systems.

title: Investigating the Effects of External Debt and Inflation on Inclusive Growth in West Africa
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN and Obafemi Awolowo University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Investigating the Effects of External Debt and Inflation on Inclusive Growth in West Africa
detail.abstract: Over time, West African (WA) countries have struggled with high levels of external debt and inflation. Existing studies have primarily focused on the isolated effects of external debt or inflation on economic growth. Recognizing that growth can occur without being broadly inclusive, this study investigates both the distinct and joint effects of external debt and inflation on inclusive growth in WA countries. The study is anchored in Neoclassical and Keynesian economic theories. Empirically, the Pooled Mean Group (PMG) approach was used to examine the distinct effects of external debt and inflation, while the Panel Dynamic Least Squares (PDLS) method was employed to assess their joint effects on per capita income (PCI) in selected WA countries. The findings indicate that, among other predictors, external debt (-0.98) and inflation (-0.01) exert negative and statistically significant effects on PCI in the long run. In the short run, only external debt remains significant, though both variables maintain negative signs. Additionally, the joint effect of external debt and inflation (-0.31) is negatively signed and statistically significant. The study concludes that both external debt and inflation, individually and jointly, have a detrimental impact on inclusive growth in WA countries. Consequently, the study recommends promoting fiscal discipline and implementing social safety net programs to mitigate these adverse effects and support more inclusive development.
